The father of their charge was one of those Italians nursed in the memory of the antique glory of Italy—one among the schiavi ognor frementi, who exerted himself to obtain the liberty of his country. He became the victim of its weakness. Whether he had died or still lingered in the dungeons of Austria was not known. His property was confiscated; his child became an orphan and a beggar. She continued with her foster parents and bloomed in their rude abode, fairer than a garden rose among dark-leaved brambles.
paras.uz: Onam bu yoqimtoy qizga hayrat va zavq bilan tikilib qolganini payqagan dehqon ayol uning tarixini ishtiyoq bilan aytib berdi. U uning farzandi emas, balki milanlik bir zodagonning qizi ekan. Onasi nemis bo'lib, uni tug'ayotganda vafot etgan ekan. Go'dakni emizish uchun bu yaxshi odamlarga berishgan ekan: o'shanda ularning ahvoli yaxshiroq edi. Ular turmush qurganiga ko'p bo'lmagan, to'ng'ich farzandlari endigina tug'ilgan edi. Ular tarbiyasidagi qizning otasi Italiyaning qadimiy shon-shuhrati xotirasi bilan tarbiyalangan italiyaliklardan biri — schiavi ognor frementi, doimo g'azabda qaynagan qullardan biri bo'lib, mamlakatining ozodligi uchun kurashgan. U uning zaifligining qurboni bo'ldi. U o'ldimi yoki hali ham Avstriya zindonlarida chiriyaptimi, ma'lum emas edi. Mulki musodara qilindi; bolasi yetim va gado bo'lib qoldi. U tarbiyachi ota-onasi bilan qoldi va ularning qo'pol uyida qora bargli tikanzorlar orasidagi bog' atirgulidan ham go'zalroq bo'lib ochildi.

paras.en: When my father returned from Milan, he found playing with me in the hall of our villa a child fairer than pictured cherub—a creature who seemed to shed radiance from her looks and whose form and motions were lighter than the chamois of the hills. The apparition was soon explained. With his permission my mother prevailed on her rustic guardians to yield their charge to her. They were fond of the sweet orphan. Her presence had seemed a blessing to them, but it would be unfair to her to keep her in poverty and want when Providence afforded her such powerful protection. They consulted their village priest, and the result was that Elizabeth Lavenza became the inmate of my parents’ house—my more than sister—the beautiful and adored companion of all my occupations and my pleasures.
paras.uz: Otam Milandan qaytganda, villamizning zalida men bilan o'ynab yurgan, suratdagi farishtadan ham go'zalroq bolani ko'rdi — u nigohlaridan nur sochayotgandek tuyuladigan, qomati va harakatlari tog' takasidan ham yengilroq mavjudot edi. Bu sharpa tez tushuntirildi. Otamning ruxsati bilan onam qishloqlik tarbiyachilarini qizni unga topshirishga ko'ndirdi. Ular shirin yetimchani yaxshi ko'rishardi. Uning borligi ularga baraka bo'lib tuyulgan edi, lekin Taqdir unga shunday qudratli himoya taqdim etayotganda uni qashshoqlik va muhtojlikda saqlash unga nisbatan adolatsizlik bo'lardi. Ular qishloq ruhoniylari bilan maslahatlashishdi va natijada Elizabet Lavenza ota-onamning uyida yashay boshladi — men uchun singlidan ham ortiq — barcha mashg'ulotlarim va zavqlarimning go'zal va suyukli hamrohi.

paras.en: Everyone loved Elizabeth. The passionate and almost reverential attachment with which all regarded her became, while I shared it, my pride and my delight. On the evening previous to her being brought to my home, my mother had said playfully, “I have a pretty present for my Victor—tomorrow he shall have it.” And when, on the morrow, she presented Elizabeth to me as her promised gift, I, with childish seriousness, interpreted her words literally and looked upon Elizabeth as mine—mine to protect, love, and cherish. All praises bestowed on her I received as made to a possession of my own. We called each other familiarly by the name of cousin. No word, no expression could body forth the kind of relation in which she stood to me—my more than sister, since till death she was to be mine only.
paras.uz: Elizabetni hamma sevardi. Hammaning unga bo'lgan ehtirosli va deyarli sig'inishga yaqin mehri, men ham uni baham ko'rganim sababli, mening g'ururim va quvonchimga aylandi. Uni uyimga olib kelishlaridan oldingi kechqurun onam hazillashib: «Mening Viktorim uchun chiroyli sovg'am bor — ertaga uni oladi», degan edi. Ertasi kuni u Elizabetni menga va'da qilingan sovg'asi sifatida taqdim etganda, men bolalarcha jiddiylik bilan uning so'zlarini so'zma-so'z tushundim va Elizabetga meniki deb qaradim — himoya qilishim, sevishim va asrashim uchun meniki. Unga aytilgan barcha maqtovlarni o'z mulkimga aytilgandek qabul qilardim. Biz bir-birimizni samimiy ravishda amakivachcha deb atardik. Hech qanday so'z, hech qanday ibora u menga nisbatan turgan munosabat turini ifoda eta olmasdi — u men uchun singlidan ham ortiq edi, chunki o'limigacha faqat meniki bo'lishi kerak edi.

paras.en: We were brought up together; there was not quite a year difference in our ages. I need not say that we were strangers to any species of disunion or dispute. Harmony was the soul of our companionship, and the diversity and contrast that subsisted in our characters drew us nearer together. Elizabeth was of a calmer and more concentrated disposition; but, with all my ardour, I was capable of a more intense application and was more deeply smitten with the thirst for knowledge. She busied herself with following the aerial creations of the poets; and in the majestic and wondrous scenes which surrounded our Swiss home —the sublime shapes of the mountains, the changes of the seasons, tempest and calm, the silence of winter, and the life and turbulence of our Alpine summers—she found ample scope for admiration and delight.
paras.uz: Biz birga tarbiyalandik; yoshimiz o'rtasida bir yilga ham farq yo'q edi. Hech qanday ajralish yoki janjal bizga begona bo'lganini aytishim shart emas. Ahillik hamrohligimizning joni edi, xarakterlarimizdagi xilma-xillik va qarama-qarshilik esa bizni yanada yaqinlashtirardi. Elizabet xotirjamroq va diqqatini jamlaganroq tabiatli edi; men esa butun qizg'inligim bilan ko'proq zo'r berib shug'ullana olardim va bilimga tashnalik meni chuqurroq qamrab olgan edi. U shoirlarning havoiy ijodlariga ergashish bilan band edi; Shveytsariyadagi uyimizni o'rab turgan ulug'vor va ajoyib manzaralarda — tog'larning salobatli shakllari, fasllar almashinuvi, bo'ron va sokinlik, qish sukunati va Alp tog'laridagi yozlarimizning hayoti va shovqinida — u hayrat va zavq uchun keng imkoniyat topardi.

paras.en: While my companion contemplated with a serious and satisfied spirit the magnificent appearances of things, I delighted in investigating their causes. The world was to me a secret which I desired to divine. Curiosity, earnest research to learn the hidden laws of nature, gladness akin to rapture, as they were unfolded to me, are among the earliest sensations I can remember.
paras.uz: Hamrohim narsalarning ajoyib ko'rinishlarini jiddiy va mamnun ruh bilan tomosha qilarkan, men ularning sabablarini tekshirishdan zavqlanardim. Dunyo men uchun topmoqchi bo'lgan sir edi. Qiziquvchanlik, tabiatning yashirin qonunlarini bilish uchun astoydil izlanish, ular menga ochilganda vajdga yaqin quvonch — men eslay oladigan eng ilk his-tuyg'ular qatorida.

paras.en: On the birth of a second son, my junior by seven years, my parents gave up entirely their wandering life and fixed themselves in their native country. We possessed a house in Geneva, and a campagne on Belrive, the eastern shore of the lake, at the distance of rather more than a league from the city. We resided principally in the latter, and the lives of my parents were passed in considerable seclusion. It was my temper to avoid a crowd and to attach myself fervently to a few. I was indifferent, therefore, to my school-fellows in general; but I united myself in the bonds of the closest friendship to one among them. Henry Clerval was the son of a merchant of Geneva. He was a boy of singular talent and fancy. He loved enterprise, hardship, and even danger for its own sake.
paras.uz: Mendan yetti yosh kichik ikkinchi o'g'il tug'ilgach, ota-onam sayyohlik hayotidan butunlay voz kechib, ona yurtlarida o'rnashishdi. Bizning Jenevada uyimiz va shahardan bir ligadan sal ko'proq masofada, ko'lning sharqiy sohilidagi Belrivda qishloq uyimiz bor edi. Biz asosan ikkinchisida yashardik va ota-onamning hayoti ancha xilvatda o'tardi. Olomondan qochish va bir nechta kishiga qizg'in bog'lanish mening tabiatim edi. Shuning uchun umuman maktabdoshlarimga befarq edim; lekin ulardan biri bilan eng yaqin do'stlik rishtalari bilan bog'landim. Genri Klerval jenevalik savdogarning o'g'li edi. U g'ayrioddiy iste'dod va xayol egasi bo'lgan bola edi. U tashabbusni, mashaqqatni va hatto xavfning o'zini ham sevardi.

paras.en: He was deeply read in books of chivalry and romance. He composed heroic songs and began to write many a tale of enchantment and knightly adventure. He tried to make us act plays and to enter into masquerades, in which the characters were drawn from the heroes of Roncesvalles, of the Round Table of King Arthur, and the chivalrous train who shed their blood to redeem the holy sepulchre from the hands of the infidels.
paras.uz: U ritsarlik va sarguzasht kitoblarini chuqur o'qigan edi. U qahramonlik qo'shiqlari to'qir va sehr va ritsarlik sarguzashtlari haqida ko'plab hikoyalar yozishni boshlardi. U bizni pyesalar o'ynashga va niqobli o'yinlarga qo'shilishga undardi, ulardagi qahramonlar Ronsevaldagi qahramonlardan, Qirol Arturning Davra stolidan va muqaddas qabrni kofirlar qo'lidan ozod qilish uchun qonlarini to'kkan ritsarlar safidan olinardi.

paras.en: No human being could have passed a happier childhood than myself. My parents were possessed by the very spirit of kindness and indulgence. We felt that they were not the tyrants to rule our lot according to their caprice, but the agents and creators of all the many delights which we enjoyed. When I mingled with other families I distinctly discerned how peculiarly fortunate my lot was, and gratitude assisted the development of filial love.
paras.uz: Hech bir inson mendan baxtliroq bolalikni o'tkaza olmasdi. Ota-onamni mehribonlik va kechirimlilik ruhining o'zi qamrab olgan edi. Biz ular qismatimizni o'z injiqliklariga ko'ra boshqaradigan zolimlar emas, balki biz bahramand bo'lgan ko'plab zavqlarning vositachilari va yaratuvchilari ekanini his qilardik. Boshqa oilalar bilan aralashganimda, qismatim naqadar alohida baxtli ekanini aniq ko'rardim va minnatdorlik farzandlik muhabbatining rivojlanishiga yordam berardi.

paras.en: My temper was sometimes violent, and my passions vehement; but by some law in my temperature they were turned not towards childish pursuits but to an eager desire to learn, and not to learn all things indiscriminately. I confess that neither the structure of languages, nor the code of governments, nor the politics of various states possessed attractions for me. It was the secrets of heaven and earth that I desired to learn; and whether it was the outward substance of things or the inner spirit of nature and the mysterious soul of man that occupied me, still my inquiries were directed to the metaphysical, or in its highest sense, the physical secrets of the world.
paras.uz: Fe'lim ba'zan shiddatli, ehtiroslarim qizg'in edi; lekin tabiatimdagi qandaydir qonun tufayli ular bolalarcha mashg'ulotlarga emas, balki o'rganishga ishtiyoqli intilishga, va hamma narsani tartibsiz o'rganishga emas, qaratilgan edi. Tan olamanki, na tillarning tuzilishi, na hukumatlar qonunlari, na turli davlatlarning siyosati meni o'ziga jalb qilardi. Men o'rganishni istagan narsa osmon va yer sirlari edi; va meni narsalarning tashqi moddasi bandmi yoki tabiatning ichki ruhi va insonning sirli qalbimi, baribir izlanishlarim dunyoning metafizik, yoki eng oliy ma'noda, fizik sirlariga qaratilgan edi.

paras.en: Meanwhile Clerval occupied himself, so to speak, with the moral relations of things. The busy stage of life, the virtues of heroes, and the actions of men were his theme; and his hope and his dream was to become one among those whose names are recorded in story as the gallant and adventurous benefactors of our species. The saintly soul of Elizabeth shone like a shrine-dedicated lamp in our peaceful home. Her sympathy was ours; her smile, her soft voice, the sweet glance of her celestial eyes, were ever there to bless and animate us. She was the living spirit of love to soften and attract; I might have become sullen in my study, rough through the ardour of my nature, but that she was there to subdue me to a semblance of her own gentleness. And Clerval—could aught ill entrench on the noble spirit of Clerval? Yet he might not have been so perfectly humane, so thoughtful in his generosity, so full of kindness and tenderness amidst his passion for adventurous exploit, had she not unfolded to him the real loveliness of beneficence and made the doing good the end and aim of his soaring ambition.
paras.uz: Bu orada Klerval, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, narsalarning axloqiy munosabatlari bilan band edi. Hayotning serharakat sahnasi, qahramonlarning fazilatlari va odamlarning ishlari uning mavzusi edi; uning umidi va orzusi esa nomlari tarixda zotimizning jasur va sarguzashtparast xayrixohlari sifatida qayd etilganlardan biri bo'lish edi. Elizabetning avliyolarga xos ruhi tinch uyimizda mehrobga bag'ishlangan chiroqdek porlardi. Uning hamdardligi biz bilan edi; uning tabassumi, yumshoq ovozi, samoviy ko'zlarining shirin nigohi bizni duo qilish va jonlantirish uchun doimo yonimizda edi. U yumshatuvchi va o'ziga tortuvchi muhabbatning tirik ruhi edi; men o'qishimda qovog'i soliq, tabiatimning qizg'inligi tufayli qo'pol bo'lib qolishim mumkin edi, lekin u meni o'z muloyimligiga o'xshash holatga bo'ysundirish uchun yonimda edi. Klerval-chi — Klervalning olijanob ruhiga biror yomonlik yo'l topa olarmidi? Shunga qaramay, agar u unga xayrixohlikning haqiqiy go'zalligini ochib bermaganida va yaxshilik qilishni yuksak orzusining maqsadi va muddaosi qilmaganida, u sarguzashtli jasoratlarga ehtirosi orasida bunchalik mukammal insonparvar, saxovatida bunchalik mulohazakor, mehribonlik va nozik tuyg'uga bunchalik to'la bo'lmasligi mumkin edi.

paras.en: I feel exquisite pleasure in dwelling on the recollections of childhood, before misfortune had tainted my mind and changed its bright visions of extensive usefulness into gloomy and narrow reflections upon self. Besides, in drawing the picture of my early days, I also record those events which led, by insensible steps, to my after tale of misery, for when I would account to myself for the birth of that passion which afterwards ruled my destiny I find it arise, like a mountain river, from ignoble and almost forgotten sources; but, swelling as it proceeded, it became the torrent which, in its course, has swept away all my hopes and joys.
paras.uz: Baxtsizlik aqlimni bulg'ab, uning keng foydalilik haqidagi yorqin tasavvurlarini o'zim haqimdagi g'amgin va tor mulohazalarga aylantirishidan oldingi bolalik xotiralari ustida to'xtalishdan nafis zavq olaman. Bundan tashqari, ilk kunlarimning manzarasini chizar ekanman, men sezilmas qadamlar bilan keyingi baxtsizlik hikoyamga olib kelgan voqealarni ham qayd etaman, chunki keyinchalik taqdirimni boshqargan o'sha ehtirosning tug'ilishini o'zimga tushuntirmoqchi bo'lsam, u tog' daryosidek past va deyarli unutilgan manbalardan boshlanganini ko'raman; lekin oqib borgani sari to'lib, u o'z yo'lida barcha umidlarim va quvonchlarimni supurib ketgan sel oqimiga aylandi.

paras.en: Natural philosophy is the genius that has regulated my fate; I desire, therefore, in this narration, to state those facts which led to my predilection for that science. When I was thirteen years of age we all went on a party of pleasure to the baths near Thonon; the inclemency of the weather obliged us to remain a day confined to the inn. In this house I chanced to find a volume of the works of Cornelius Agrippa. I opened it with apathy; the theory which he attempts to demonstrate and the wonderful facts which he relates soon changed this feeling into enthusiasm. A new light seemed to dawn upon my mind, and bounding with joy, I communicated my discovery to my father. My father looked carelessly at the title page of my book and said, “Ah! Cornelius Agrippa! My dear Victor, do not waste your time upon this; it is sad trash.”
paras.uz: Tabiat falsafasi taqdirimni boshqargan daho; shuning uchun bu hikoyada men meni o'sha fanga moyil qilgan faktlarni bayon qilmoqchiman. O'n uch yoshimda biz hammamiz Tonon yaqinidagi issiq suvlarga sayrga bordik; havoning yomonligi bizni bir kun mehmonxonada qamalib qolishga majbur qildi. Bu uyda men tasodifan Korneliy Agrippa asarlarining bir jildini topib oldim. Uni befarqlik bilan ochdim; lekin u isbotlashga urinayotgan nazariya va u hikoya qilgan ajoyib faktlar tez orada bu tuyg'uni ishtiyoqqa aylantirdi. Aqlimda go'yo yangi nur tong otgandek bo'ldi va quvonchdan sakrab, kashfiyotimni otamga aytdim. Otam kitobimning sarvarag'iga beparvo qaradi va dedi: «Oh! Korneliy Agrippa! Aziz Viktorim, bunga vaqtingni sarflama; bu achinarli bema'nilik.»

paras.en: If, instead of this remark, my father had taken the pains to explain to me that the principles of Agrippa had been entirely exploded and that a modern system of science had been introduced which possessed much greater powers than the ancient, because the powers of the latter were chimerical, while those of the former were real and practical, under such circumstances I should certainly have thrown Agrippa aside and have contented my imagination, warmed as it was, by returning with greater ardour to my former studies. It is even possible that the train of my ideas would never have received the fatal impulse that led to my ruin. But the cursory glance my father had taken of my volume by no means assured me that he was acquainted with its contents, and I continued to read with the greatest avidity.
paras.uz: Agar bu gap o'rniga otam menga Agrippaning tamoyillari butunlay rad etilganini va eskisidan ancha katta imkoniyatlarga ega zamonaviy ilm tizimi joriy etilganini, chunki eskisining kuchlari xayoliy, zamonaviysiniki esa haqiqiy va amaliy ekanini tushuntirishga zahmat chekkanida, bunday sharoitda men Agrippani albatta chetga uloqtirgan va qizigan tasavvurimni avvalgi mashg'ulotlarimga katta ishtiyoq bilan qaytib qondirgan bo'lardim. Hatto fikrlarim silsilasi meni halokatga olib kelgan o'sha halokatli turtkini hech qachon olmagan bo'lishi ham mumkin. Lekin otamning kitobimga yuzaki nazar tashlagani uning mazmunidan xabardor ekaniga meni aslo ishontirmadi va men eng katta ochko'zlik bilan o'qishda davom etdim.

paras.en: When I returned home my first care was to procure the whole works of this author, and afterwards of Paracelsus and Albertus Magnus. I read and studied the wild fancies of these writers with delight; they appeared to me treasures known to few besides myself. I have described myself as always having been imbued with a fervent longing to penetrate the secrets of nature. In spite of the intense labour and wonderful discoveries of modern philosophers, I always came from my studies discontented and unsatisfied. Sir Isaac Newton is said to have avowed that he felt like a child picking up shells beside the great and unexplored ocean of truth. Those of his successors in each branch of natural philosophy with whom I was acquainted appeared even to my boy’s apprehensions as tyros engaged in the same pursuit.
paras.uz: Uyga qaytgach, birinchi tashvishim bu muallifning barcha asarlarini, keyin esa Paratsels va Albert Magnusning asarlarini qo'lga kiritish bo'ldi. Men bu yozuvchilarning yovvoyi xayollarini zavq bilan o'qib, o'rgandim; ular menga mendan boshqa kam kishiga ma'lum bo'lgan xazinalar bo'lib tuyulardi. Men o'zimni doimo tabiat sirlariga kirib borish uchun qizg'in intilish bilan sug'orilgan deb ta'rifladim. Zamonaviy faylasuflarning zo'r mehnati va ajoyib kashfiyotlariga qaramay, men har doim mashg'ulotlarimdan norozi va qoniqmagan holda chiqardim. Aytishlaricha, ser Isaak Nyuton o'zini haqiqatning buyuk va o'rganilmagan okeani yonida chig'anoq terayotgan boladek his qilganini tan olgan ekan. Tabiat falsafasining har bir sohasida men tanish bo'lgan uning izdoshlari hatto mening bolalarcha tushunchamga ham xuddi shu ish bilan band bo'lgan yangi boshlovchilar bo'lib ko'rinardi.

paras.en: The untaught peasant beheld the elements around him and was acquainted with their practical uses. The most learned philosopher knew little more. He had partially unveiled the face of Nature, but her immortal lineaments were still a wonder and a mystery. He might dissect, anatomise, and give names; but, not to speak of a final cause, causes in their secondary and tertiary grades were utterly unknown to him. I had gazed upon the fortifications and impediments that seemed to keep human beings from entering the citadel of nature, and rashly and ignorantly I had repined.
paras.uz: O'qimagan dehqon atrofidagi unsurlarni ko'rardi va ularning amaliy foydalarini bilardi. Eng bilimdon faylasuf undan sal ko'proq bilardi. U Tabiatning yuzidan pardani qisman ko'targan edi, lekin uning boqiy qiyofasi hali ham mo''jiza va sir edi. U kesib, anatomiya qilib, nom berishi mumkin edi; lekin yakuniy sabab haqida gapirmasa ham, ikkinchi va uchinchi darajadagi sabablar unga mutlaqo noma'lum edi. Men insonlarni tabiat qal'asiga kirishdan to'sib turgandek tuyulgan istehkomlar va to'siqlarga tikilgan edim va shoshqaloqlik va nodonlik bilan nolib yurgan edim.

paras.en: But here were books, and here were men who had penetrated deeper and knew more. I took their word for all that they averred, and I became their disciple. It may appear strange that such should arise in the eighteenth century; but while I followed the routine of education in the schools of Geneva, I was, to a great degree, self-taught with regard to my favourite studies. My father was not scientific, and I was left to struggle with a child’s blindness, added to a student’s thirst for knowledge. Under the guidance of my new preceptors I entered with the greatest diligence into the search of the philosopher’s stone and the elixir of life; but the latter soon obtained my undivided attention. Wealth was an inferior object, but what glory would attend the discovery if I could banish disease from the human frame and render man invulnerable to any but a violent death!
paras.uz: Lekin mana kitoblar, mana chuqurroq kirib borgan va ko'proq biladigan odamlar. Men ularning aytgan hamma gapiga ishondim va ularning shogirdi bo'ldim. O'n sakkizinchi asrda bunday narsa paydo bo'lishi g'alati tuyulishi mumkin; lekin Jeneva maktablarida ta'limning odatiy yo'lidan borar ekanman, sevimli mashg'ulotlarim borasida katta darajada o'zim o'rgandim. Otam ilm odami emas edi va men bolaning ko'rligi, unga qo'shilgan talabaning bilimga tashnaligi bilan kurashish uchun yolg'iz qoldirildim. Yangi ustozlarimning rahbarligi ostida men faylasuf toshi va hayot eliksirini izlashga eng katta tirishqoqlik bilan kirishdim; lekin tez orada ikkinchisi butun diqqatimni egalladi. Boylik ikkinchi darajali maqsad edi, lekin agar men kasallikni inson vujudidan quvib, insonni zo'ravon o'limdan boshqa har qanday o'limga daxlsiz qila olsam, bu kashfiyotni qanday shon-shuhrat kutardi!

paras.en: Nor were these my only visions. The raising of ghosts or devils was a promise liberally accorded by my favourite authors, the fulfilment of which I most eagerly sought; and if my incantations were always unsuccessful, I attributed the failure rather to my own inexperience and mistake than to a want of skill or fidelity in my instructors. And thus for a time I was occupied by exploded systems, mingling, like an unadept, a thousand contradictory theories and floundering desperately in a very slough of multifarious knowledge, guided by an ardent imagination and childish reasoning, till an accident again changed the current of my ideas.
paras.uz: Bular yagona orzularim ham emas edi. Arvohlar yoki shaytonlarni chaqirish sevimli mualliflarim saxiylik bilan va'da qilgan narsa edi va men uning amalga oshishini eng ishtiyoq bilan izladim; agar afsunlarim doim muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'lsa, men muvaffaqiyatsizlikni ustozlarimning mahorati yoki sadoqati yetishmasligiga emas, ko'proq o'z tajribasizligim va xatoyimga nisbat berardim. Shunday qilib bir muddat men rad etilgan tizimlar bilan band bo'ldim, nodon kabi mingta bir-biriga zid nazariyalarni aralashtirib, qizg'in tasavvur va bolalarcha mulohaza boshqaruvida xilma-xil bilimlarning botqog'ida umidsiz tipirchilab yurdim, toki bir tasodif yana fikrlarim oqimini o'zgartirmaguncha.

paras.en: When I was about fifteen years old we had retired to our house near Belrive, when we witnessed a most violent and terrible thunderstorm. It advanced from behind the mountains of Jura, and the thunder burst at once with frightful loudness from various quarters of the heavens. I remained, while the storm lasted, watching its progress with curiosity and delight. As I stood at the door, on a sudden I beheld a stream of fire issue from an old and beautiful oak which stood about twenty yards from our house; and so soon as the dazzling light vanished, the oak had disappeared, and nothing remained but a blasted stump. When we visited it the next morning, we found the tree shattered in a singular manner. It was not splintered by the shock, but entirely reduced to thin ribbons of wood. I never beheld anything so utterly destroyed.
paras.uz: Taxminan o'n besh yoshda bo'lganimda, biz Belriv yaqinidagi uyimizga chekingan edik va eng shiddatli va dahshatli momaqaldiroqli bo'ronga guvoh bo'ldik. U Yura tog'lari ortidan bostirib keldi va momaqaldiroq birdaniga osmonning turli tomonlaridan qo'rqinchli gumburlab yorildi. Bo'ron davom etar ekan, men uning borishini qiziqish va zavq bilan kuzatib turdim. Eshik oldida turganimda birdan uyimizdan taxminan yigirma yard narida turgan eski va go'zal eman daraxtidan olov oqimi otilib chiqqanini ko'rdim; ko'zni qamashtiruvchi nur so'nishi bilanoq eman g'oyib bo'lgan va undan kuygan to'nkadan boshqa hech narsa qolmagan edi. Ertasi kuni ertalab uni ko'rgani borganimizda, daraxt g'alati tarzda parchalanganini ko'rdik. U zarbadan shunchaki tilka-pora bo'lmagan, balki butunlay yupqa yog'och tasmalariga aylangan edi. Men hech qachon bunchalik butunlay vayron qilingan narsani ko'rmaganman.

paras.en: Before this I was not unacquainted with the more obvious laws of electricity. On this occasion a man of great research in natural philosophy was with us, and excited by this catastrophe, he entered on the explanation of a theory which he had formed on the subject of electricity and galvanism, which was at once new and astonishing to me. All that he said threw greatly into the shade Cornelius Agrippa, Albertus Magnus, and Paracelsus, the lords of my imagination; but by some fatality the overthrow of these men disinclined me to pursue my accustomed studies. It seemed to me as if nothing would or could ever be known. All that had so long engaged my attention suddenly grew despicable.
paras.uz: Bundan oldin men elektrning ravshanroq qonunlari bilan tanish emas emasdim. Bu safar biz bilan tabiat falsafasida katta izlanishlar qilgan bir odam bor edi va bu falokatdan hayajonlanib, u elektr va galvanizm mavzusida o'zi tuzgan nazariyani tushuntira boshladi, bu men uchun bir vaqtning o'zida yangi va hayratlanarli edi. Uning aytgan hamma gapi tasavvurimning hukmdorlari Korneliy Agrippa, Albert Magnus va Paratselsni qattiq soyada qoldirdi; lekin qandaydir taqdir taqozosi bilan bu odamlarning ag'darilishi meni odatiy mashg'ulotlarimni davom ettirishdan sovutdi. Menga go'yo hech narsa hech qachon bilinmaydigan va bilinishi mumkin emasdek tuyuldi. Shuncha vaqt diqqatimni band qilgan hamma narsa birdan jirkanch bo'lib qoldi.

paras.en: By one of those caprices of the mind which we are perhaps most subject to in early youth, I at once gave up my former occupations, set down natural history and all its progeny as a deformed and abortive creation, and entertained the greatest disdain for a would-be science which could never even step within the threshold of real knowledge. In this mood of mind I betook myself to the mathematics and the branches of study appertaining to that science as being built upon secure foundations, and so worthy of my consideration.
paras.uz: Biz balki ilk yoshlikda ko'proq duchor bo'ladigan aqlning injiqliklaridan biri tufayli men darhol avvalgi mashg'ulotlarimdan voz kechdim, tabiatshunoslik va uning barcha avlodlarini xunuk va chala tug'ilgan ijod deb hisobladim va haqiqiy bilimning ostonasiga ham hech qachon qadam qo'ya olmaydigan soxta ilmga eng katta nafrat bilan qaradim. Shu kayfiyatda men matematika va bu ilmga tegishli soha mashg'ulotlariga o'tdim, chunki ular mustahkam poydevorga qurilgan va shuning uchun e'tiborimga loyiq edi.

paras.en: Thus strangely are our souls constructed, and by such slight ligaments are we bound to prosperity or ruin. When I look back, it seems to me as if this almost miraculous change of inclination and will was the immediate suggestion of the guardian angel of my life—the last effort made by the spirit of preservation to avert the storm that was even then hanging in the stars and ready to envelop me. Her victory was announced by an unusual tranquillity and gladness of soul which followed the relinquishing of my ancient and latterly tormenting studies. It was thus that I was to be taught to associate evil with their prosecution, happiness with their disregard.
paras.uz: Ruhlarimiz shunday g'alati tuzilgan va bizni farovonlik yoki halokatga shunday ingichka rishtalar bog'laydi. Orqaga qarasam, menga istak va irodaning bu deyarli mo''jizaviy o'zgarishi hayotimning qo'riqchi farishtasining bevosita ishorasi bo'lgandek tuyuladi — o'shanda ham yulduzlarda osilib turgan va meni qamrab olishga tayyor bo'lgan bo'ronni qaytarish uchun saqlovchi ruh qilgan so'nggi urinish. Uning g'alabasi qadimiy va oxirgi paytlarda qiynab kelgan mashg'ulotlarimdan voz kechganimdan keyin kelgan ruhning g'ayrioddiy xotirjamligi va quvonchi bilan e'lon qilindi. Shu tarzda menga ularni davom ettirishni yovuzlik bilan, ulardan voz kechishni esa baxt bilan bog'lashni o'rgatishlari kerak edi.

paras.en: It was a strong effort of the spirit of good, but it was ineffectual. Destiny was too potent, and her immutable laws had decreed my utter and terrible destruction.
paras.uz: Bu ezgulik ruhining kuchli harakati edi, lekin u samarasiz bo'ldi. Taqdir haddan tashqari qudratli edi va uning o'zgarmas qonunlari mening butunlay va dahshatli halokatimni hukm qilgan edi.

paras.en: When I had attained the age of seventeen my parents resolved that I should become a student at the university of Ingolstadt. I had hitherto attended the schools of Geneva, but my father thought it necessary for the completion of my education that I should be made acquainted with other customs than those of my native country. My departure was therefore fixed at an early date, but before the day resolved upon could arrive, the first misfortune of my life occurred—an omen, as it were, of my future misery.
paras.uz: O'n yetti yoshga to'lganimda ota-onam meni Ingolshtadt universitetiga talaba qilishga qaror qilishdi. Shu paytgacha men Jeneva maktablarida o'qigan edim, lekin otam ta'limimni yakunlash uchun ona yurtimnikidan boshqa urf-odatlar bilan tanishishim zarur deb hisobladi. Shuning uchun jo'nashim erta sanaga belgilandi, lekin belgilangan kun kelmasdan hayotimdagi birinchi baxtsizlik yuz berdi — go'yo kelajakdagi kulfatimning darakchisi.

paras.en: Elizabeth had caught the scarlet fever; her illness was severe, and she was in the greatest danger. During her illness many arguments had been urged to persuade my mother to refrain from attending upon her. She had at first yielded to our entreaties, but when she heard that the life of her favourite was menaced, she could no longer control her anxiety. She attended her sickbed; her watchful attentions triumphed over the malignity of the distemper—Elizabeth was saved, but the consequences of this imprudence were fatal to her preserver. On the third day my mother sickened; her fever was accompanied by the most alarming symptoms, and the looks of her medical attendants prognosticated the worst event. On her deathbed the fortitude and benignity of this best of women did not desert her. She joined the hands of Elizabeth and myself.
paras.uz: Elizabet qizilchaga chalindi; kasalligi og'ir kechdi va u eng katta xavf ostida edi. Kasalligi davomida onamni unga qarashdan qaytarish uchun ko'p dalillar keltirildi. Dastlab u iltijolarimizga bo'ysundi, lekin sevimlisining hayoti xavf ostida ekanini eshitgach, xavotirini boshqara olmay qoldi. U uning bemor to'shagiga qaradi; uning hushyor g'amxo'rligi kasallikning yovuzligi ustidan g'alaba qozondi — Elizabet qutqarildi, lekin bu ehtiyotsizlikning oqibatlari uning qutqaruvchisi uchun halokatli bo'ldi. Uchinchi kuni onam kasal bo'lib qoldi; uning isitmasi eng xavotirli alomatlar bilan kechdi va tabiblarning qiyofasi eng yomon oqibatni bashorat qilardi. O'lim to'shagida ham ayollarning eng yaxshisining matonati va mehribonligi uni tark etmadi. U Elizabet bilan mening qo'llarimni birlashtirdi.

paras.en: “My children,” she said, “my firmest hopes of future happiness were placed on the prospect of your union. This expectation will now be the consolation of your father. Elizabeth, my love, you must supply my place to my younger children. Alas! I regret that I am taken from you; and, happy and beloved as I have been, is it not hard to quit you all? But these are not thoughts befitting me; I will endeavour to resign myself cheerfully to death and will indulge a hope of meeting you in another world.”
paras.uz: «Bolalarim, — dedi u, — kelajakdagi baxt haqidagi eng mustahkam umidlarim sizlarning turmush qurishingiz istiqboliga bog'langan edi. Bu umid endi otangizning tasallisi bo'ladi. Elizabet, jonim, kichik bolalarimga mening o'rnimni bosishing kerak. Afsus! Sizlardan olib ketilayotganimdan afsuslanaman; baxtli va sevimli bo'lgan menga hammangizni tark etish og'ir emasmi? Lekin bular menga yarashmaydigan fikrlar; o'limga quvnoq taslim bo'lishga harakat qilaman va sizlar bilan boshqa dunyoda uchrashish umidini qalbimda saqlayman.»

paras.en: She died calmly, and her countenance expressed affection even in death. I need not describe the feelings of those whose dearest ties are rent by that most irreparable evil, the void that presents itself to the soul, and the despair that is exhibited on the countenance. It is so long before the mind can persuade itself that she whom we saw every day and whose very existence appeared a part of our own can have departed for ever—that the brightness of a beloved eye can have been extinguished and the sound of a voice so familiar and dear to the ear can be hushed, never more to be heard. These are the reflections of the first days; but when the lapse of time proves the reality of the evil, then the actual bitterness of grief commences. Yet from whom has not that rude hand rent away some dear connection?
paras.uz: U osoyishta vafot etdi va hatto o'limda ham chehrasi mehr ifodalardi. Eng aziz rishtalari bu eng tuzatib bo'lmas yovuzlik bilan uzilganlarning his-tuyg'ularini, ruhda paydo bo'ladigan bo'shliqni va chehrada namoyon bo'ladigan umidsizlikni ta'riflashim shart emas. Har kuni ko'rgan va borligining o'zi biznikining bir qismidek tuyulgan inson abadiy ketishi mumkinligiga — suyukli ko'zning nuri so'nishi va quloqqa shunchalik tanish va aziz ovoz jim bo'lib, endi hech qachon eshitilmasligi mumkinligiga aql ishonishi uchun shunchalik ko'p vaqt kerak. Bular ilk kunlarning mulohazalari; lekin vaqt o'tib, yovuzlikning haqiqiyligini isbotlaganda, qayg'uning haqiqiy achchig'i boshlanadi. Shunga qaramay, o'sha qo'pol qo'l kimdan biror aziz rishtani uzib olmagan?

paras.en: And why should I describe a sorrow which all have felt, and must feel? The time at length arrives when grief is rather an indulgence than a necessity; and the smile that plays upon the lips, although it may be deemed a sacrilege, is not banished. My mother was dead, but we had still duties which we ought to perform; we must continue our course with the rest and learn to think ourselves fortunate whilst one remains whom the spoiler has not seized.
paras.uz: Va nega men hamma his qilgan va his qilishi kerak bo'lgan qayg'uni ta'riflashim kerak? Nihoyat shunday vaqt keladiki, qayg'u zaruratdan ko'ra ko'proq o'zini erkalashga aylanadi; va lablarda o'ynayotgan tabassum, garchi uni kufr deb hisoblash mumkin bo'lsa ham, quvilmaydi. Onam o'lgan edi, lekin bizning hali bajarishimiz kerak bo'lgan burchlarimiz bor edi; biz qolganlar bilan birga yo'limizni davom ettirishimiz va talonchi hali olib ketmagan biror kishi qolgan ekan, o'zimizni omadli deb hisoblashni o'rganishimiz kerak.

paras.en: My departure for Ingolstadt, which had been deferred by these events, was now again determined upon. I obtained from my father a respite of some weeks. It appeared to me sacrilege so soon to leave the repose, akin to death, of the house of mourning and to rush into the thick of life. I was new to sorrow, but it did not the less alarm me. I was unwilling to quit the sight of those that remained to me, and above all, I desired to see my sweet Elizabeth in some degree consoled.
paras.uz: Bu voqealar tufayli kechiktirilgan Ingolshtadtga jo'nashim endi yana belgilandi. Men otamdan bir necha haftalik muhlat oldim. Motam uyining o'limga yaqin osoyishtaligini bunchalik tez tark etib, hayotning qoq o'rtasiga shoshilish menga kufrdek tuyuldi. Men qayg'uga yangi edim, lekin u meni kamroq qo'rqitmadi. Menga qolganlarni ko'zdan qochirishni istamasdim va eng muhimi, shirin Elizabetimni qaysidir darajada taskin topganini ko'rmoqchi edim.

paras.en: She indeed veiled her grief and strove to act the comforter to us all. She looked steadily on life and assumed its duties with courage and zeal. She devoted herself to those whom she had been taught to call her uncle and cousins. Never was she so enchanting as at this time, when she recalled the sunshine of her smiles and spent them upon us. She forgot even her own regret in her endeavours to make us forget.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham u qayg'usini yashirib, hammamizga tasalli beruvchi bo'lishga intildi. U hayotga qat'iy qaradi va uning burchlarini jasorat va g'ayrat bilan o'z zimmasiga oldi. U o'zini amaki va amakivachchalar deb atashga o'rgatilganlarga bag'ishladi. U hech qachon tabassumlarining quyosh nurini qaytarib, ularni bizga sarflagan bu paytdagidek maftunkor bo'lmagan edi. U bizni unuttirishga urinishda hatto o'z afsusini ham unutdi.

paras.en: The day of my departure at length arrived. Clerval spent the last evening with us. He had endeavoured to persuade his father to permit him to accompany me and to become my fellow student, but in vain. His father was a narrow-minded trader and saw idleness and ruin in the aspirations and ambition of his son. Henry deeply felt the misfortune of being debarred from a liberal education. He said little, but when he spoke I read in his kindling eye and in his animated glance a restrained but firm resolve not to be chained to the miserable details of commerce.
paras.uz: Nihoyat jo'nash kunim keldi. Klerval oxirgi kechani biz bilan o'tkazdi. U otasini menga hamroh bo'lishiga va hamkursim bo'lishiga ruxsat berishga ko'ndirishga uringan edi, lekin behuda. Uning otasi tor fikrli savdogar edi va o'g'lining intilishlari va orzusida dangasalik va halokatni ko'rardi. Genri keng ta'limdan mahrum bo'lish baxtsizligini chuqur his qilardi. U kam gapirdi, lekin gapirganda men uning yonayotgan ko'zida va jonli nigohida savdoning ayanchli mayda-chuydalariga zanjirband bo'lmaslikka jilovlangan, lekin qat'iy qarorni o'qidim.

paras.en: We sat late. We could not tear ourselves away from each other nor persuade ourselves to say the word “Farewell!” It was said, and we retired under the pretence of seeking repose, each fancying that the other was deceived; but when at morning’s dawn I descended to the carriage which was to convey me away, they were all there—my father again to bless me, Clerval to press my hand once more, my Elizabeth to renew her entreaties that I would write often and to bestow the last feminine attentions on her playmate and friend.
paras.uz: Biz kechgacha o'tirdik. Bir-birimizdan ajrala olmasdik va «Xayr!» so'zini aytishga o'zimizni ko'ndira olmasdik. U aytildi va biz dam olish bahonasi bilan xonalarimizga ketdik, har birimiz boshqamizni aldangan deb tasavvur qildik; lekin tong saharda meni olib ketadigan aravaga tushganimda, ularning hammasi u yerda edi — otam meni yana duo qilish uchun, Klerval qo'limni yana bir bor qisish uchun, Elizabetim esa tez-tez yozishimni iltimos qilishni yangilash va o'yindoshi va do'stiga so'nggi ayollarcha g'amxo'rlikni ko'rsatish uchun.

paras.en: I threw myself into the chaise that was to convey me away and indulged in the most melancholy reflections. I, who had ever been surrounded by amiable companions, continually engaged in endeavouring to bestow mutual pleasure—I was now alone. In the university whither I was going I must form my own friends and be my own protector. My life had hitherto been remarkably secluded and domestic, and this had given me invincible repugnance to new countenances. I loved my brothers, Elizabeth, and Clerval; these were “old familiar faces,” but I believed myself totally unfitted for the company of strangers. Such were my reflections as I commenced my journey; but as I proceeded, my spirits and hopes rose. I ardently desired the acquisition of knowledge. I had often, when at home, thought it hard to remain during my youth cooped up in one place and had longed to enter the world and take my station among other human beings. Now my desires were complied with, and it would, indeed, have been folly to repent.
paras.uz: Meni olib ketadigan aravaga o'zimni tashladim va eng g'amgin mulohazalarga berildim. Doimo yoqimli hamrohlar bilan o'ralgan, doimo bir-birimizga zavq berishga harakat qilgan men — endi yolg'iz edim. Men borayotgan universitetda o'zim do'st orttirishim va o'zimning himoyachim bo'lishim kerak edi. Hayotim shu paytgacha juda xilvat va oilaviy o'tgan edi va bu menda yangi chehralarga yengib bo'lmas jirkanish paydo qilgan edi. Men ukalarimni, Elizabetni va Klervalni sevardim; bular «eski tanish chehralar» edi, lekin o'zimni begonalar davrasiga butunlay yaroqsiz deb hisoblardim. Safarimni boshlaganimda mulohazalarim shunday edi; lekin oldinga borgan sari ruhim va umidlarim ko'tarildi. Men bilim olishni qizg'in istardim. Uyda bo'lganimda ko'pincha yoshligimda bir joyda qamalib qolishni og'ir deb o'ylardim va dunyoga chiqib, boshqa insonlar orasida o'z o'rnimni egallashni orzu qilardim. Endi istaklarim bajo keltirildi va pushaymon bo'lish, haqiqatan ham, ahmoqlik bo'lardi.

paras.en: I had sufficient leisure for these and many other reflections during my journey to Ingolstadt, which was long and fatiguing. At length the high white steeple of the town met my eyes. I alighted and was conducted to my solitary apartment to spend the evening as I pleased.
paras.uz: Uzoq va charchatadigan Ingolshtadt safarim davomida bu va boshqa ko'plab mulohazalar uchun yetarli bo'sh vaqtim bo'ldi. Nihoyat ko'zimga shaharning baland oq qo'ng'iroqxonasi tushdi. Men aravadan tushdim va kechqurunni xohlaganimcha o'tkazish uchun meni yolg'iz xonamga olib borishdi.

paras.en: The next morning I delivered my letters of introduction and paid a visit to some of the principal professors. Chance—or rather the evil influence, the Angel of Destruction, which asserted omnipotent sway over me from the moment I turned my reluctant steps from my father’s door—led me first to M. Krempe, professor of natural philosophy. He was an uncouth man, but deeply imbued in the secrets of his science. He asked me several questions concerning my progress in the different branches of science appertaining to natural philosophy. I replied carelessly, and partly in contempt, mentioned the names of my alchemists as the principal authors I had studied. The professor stared. “Have you,” he said, “really spent your time in studying such nonsense?”
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab tavsiyanoma maktublarimni topshirdim va ba'zi asosiy professorlarga tashrif buyurdim. Tasodif — yoki to'g'rirog'i, otamning eshigidan istamay qadam tashlaganimdan beri ustimdan qudratli hukmronlik qilgan yovuz ta'sir, Halokat Farishtasi — meni birinchi bo'lib tabiat falsafasi professori janob Krempe huzuriga olib bordi. U qo'pol odam edi, lekin o'z fanining sirlariga chuqur singgan edi. U mendan tabiat falsafasiga tegishli turli fan sohalaridagi yutuqlarim haqida bir nechta savol berdi. Men beparvolik bilan javob berdim va qisman nafrat bilan o'zim o'rgangan asosiy mualliflar sifatida alkimyogarlarimning ismlarini tilga oldim. Professor ko'zlarini katta ochdi. «Siz haqiqatan ham vaqtingizni shunday bema'nilikni o'rganishga sarflaganmisiz?» — dedi u.

paras.en: I replied in the affirmative. “Every minute,” continued M. Krempe with warmth, “every instant that you have wasted on those books is utterly and entirely lost. You have burdened your memory with exploded systems and useless names. Good God! In what desert land have you lived, where no one was kind enough to inform you that these fancies which you have so greedily imbibed are a thousand years old and as musty as they are ancient? I little expected, in this enlightened and scientific age, to find a disciple of Albertus Magnus and Paracelsus. My dear sir, you must begin your studies entirely anew.”
paras.uz: Men tasdiqlab javob berdim. «Har bir daqiqa, — davom etdi janob Krempe qizishib, — o'sha kitoblarga sarflagan har bir lahzangiz butunlay va mutlaqo yo'qotilgan. Siz xotirangizni rad etilgan tizimlar va befoyda nomlar bilan yuklagansiz. Yaxshi Xudo! Qaysi sahroda yashagansizki, u yerda hech kim siz shunchalik ochko'zlik bilan singdirgan bu xayollar ming yillik ekanini va qadimiy bo'lganidek mog'orlab ketganini aytishga iltifot qilmagan? Bu ma'rifatli va ilmiy asrda Albert Magnus va Paratselsning shogirdini uchratishni hech kutmagan edim. Aziz janob, o'qishingizni butunlay yangidan boshlashingiz kerak.»

paras.en: So saying, he stepped aside and wrote down a list of several books treating of natural philosophy which he desired me to procure, and dismissed me after mentioning that in the beginning of the following week he intended to commence a course of lectures upon natural philosophy in its general relations, and that M. Waldman, a fellow professor, would lecture upon chemistry the alternate days that he omitted.
paras.uz: Shunday deb, u chetga chiqib, men sotib olishimni istagan tabiat falsafasiga oid bir nechta kitobning ro'yxatini yozdi va keyingi haftaning boshida tabiat falsafasining umumiy munosabatlari bo'yicha ma'ruzalar kursini boshlamoqchi ekanini, uning hamkasbi professor janob Valdman esa u qoldiradigan navbatdagi kunlarda kimyo bo'yicha ma'ruza o'qishini aytib, meni jo'natib yubordi.

paras.en: I returned home not disappointed, for I have said that I had long considered those authors useless whom the professor reprobated; but I returned not at all the more inclined to recur to these studies in any shape. M. Krempe was a little squat man with a gruff voice and a repulsive countenance; the teacher, therefore, did not prepossess me in favour of his pursuits. In rather a too philosophical and connected a strain, perhaps, I have given an account of the conclusions I had come to concerning them in my early years. As a child I had not been content with the results promised by the modern professors of natural science.
paras.uz: Uyga umidsizlanmay qaytdim, chunki aytganimdek, professor qoralagan o'sha mualliflarni uzoq vaqtdan beri befoyda deb hisoblab kelgan edim; lekin bu mashg'ulotlarga biror shaklda qaytishga sira ham moyilroq bo'lmay qaytdim. Janob Krempe qo'pol ovozli va jirkanch chehrali kichkina, pakana odam edi; shuning uchun o'qituvchi meni o'z mashg'ulotlariga moyil qilmadi. Balki haddan tashqari falsafiy va izchil ohangda men ilk yillarimda ular haqida qanday xulosalarga kelganimni hikoya qilib berdim. Bolaligimda men tabiatshunoslikning zamonaviy professorlari va'da qilgan natijalardan qoniqmagan edim.

paras.en: With a confusion of ideas only to be accounted for by my extreme youth and my want of a guide on such matters, I had retrod the steps of knowledge along the paths of time and exchanged the discoveries of recent inquirers for the dreams of forgotten alchemists. Besides, I had a contempt for the uses of modern natural philosophy. It was very different when the masters of the science sought immortality and power; such views, although futile, were grand; but now the scene was changed. The ambition of the inquirer seemed to limit itself to the annihilation of those visions on which my interest in science was chiefly founded. I was required to exchange chimeras of boundless grandeur for realities of little worth.
paras.uz: Faqat haddan tashqari yoshligim va bunday masalalarda yo'lboshchim yo'qligi bilan izohlash mumkin bo'lgan fikrlar chalkashligi bilan men vaqt so'qmoqlari bo'ylab bilim izlaridan orqaga qaytgan va yaqindagi tadqiqotchilarning kashfiyotlarini unutilgan alkimyogarlarning orzulariga almashtirgan edim. Bundan tashqari, men zamonaviy tabiat falsafasining foydalarini mensimasdim. Fan ustalari boqiylik va qudrat izlagan paytlarda bu butunlay boshqacha edi; bunday qarashlar, behuda bo'lsa ham, ulug'vor edi; lekin endi manzara o'zgardi. Tadqiqotchining orzusi faqat ilmga qiziqishim asosan tayangan o'sha orzularni yo'q qilish bilan cheklangandek tuyulardi. Mendan cheksiz ulug'vorlikdagi xayollarni kam qadrli haqiqatlarga almashtirish talab qilinardi.

paras.en: Such were my reflections during the first two or three days of my residence at Ingolstadt, which were chiefly spent in becoming acquainted with the localities and the principal residents in my new abode. But as the ensuing week commenced, I thought of the information which M. Krempe had given me concerning the lectures. And although I could not consent to go and hear that little conceited fellow deliver sentences out of a pulpit, I recollected what he had said of M. Waldman, whom I had never seen, as he had hitherto been out of town.
paras.uz: Ingolshtadtda yashashimning dastlabki ikki-uch kunida, asosan yangi maskanimning joylari va asosiy aholisi bilan tanishishga sarflangan kunlarda mulohazalarim shunday edi. Lekin keyingi hafta boshlangach, men janob Krempe menga ma'ruzalar haqida bergan ma'lumotni esladim. Garchi o'sha kichkina manman odamning minbardan jumlalar o'qishini borib tinglashga rozi bo'lmasam ham, uning shu paytgacha shahardan tashqarida bo'lgani uchun hech qachon ko'rmagan janob Valdman haqida aytganlarini esladim.

paras.en: Partly from curiosity and partly from idleness, I went into the lecturing room, which M. Waldman entered shortly after. This professor was very unlike his colleague. He appeared about fifty years of age, but with an aspect expressive of the greatest benevolence; a few grey hairs covered his temples, but those at the back of his head were nearly black. His person was short but remarkably erect and his voice the sweetest I had ever heard. He began his lecture by a recapitulation of the history of chemistry and the various improvements made by different men of learning, pronouncing with fervour the names of the most distinguished discoverers. He then took a cursory view of the present state of the science and explained many of its elementary terms. After having made a few preparatory experiments, he concluded with a panegyric upon modern chemistry, the terms of which I shall never forget:
paras.uz: Qisman qiziquvchanlikdan, qisman bekorchilikdan men ma'ruza zaliga kirdim, ko'p o'tmay janob Valdman ham kirib keldi. Bu professor hamkasbiga sira o'xshamasdi. U taxminan ellik yoshlarda ko'rinardi, lekin qiyofasi eng katta xayrixohlikni ifodalardi; chakkalarini bir nechta oq soch qoplagan, lekin boshining orqasidagi sochlari deyarli qora edi. Uning qaddi past, lekin g'ayrioddiy tik edi, ovozi esa men eshitgan eng shirin ovoz edi. U ma'ruzasini kimyo tarixi va turli olimlar qilgan turli yutuqlarni qisqacha takrorlashdan boshladi, eng mashhur kashfiyotchilarning ismlarini qizg'inlik bilan tilga oldi. Keyin u fanning hozirgi holatini qisqacha ko'zdan kechirdi va uning ko'plab boshlang'ich atamalarini tushuntirdi. Bir nechta tayyorlov tajribalarini o'tkazgach, u zamonaviy kimyoga madhiya bilan yakunladi, uning so'zlarini hech qachon unutmayman:

paras.en: “The ancient teachers of this science,” said he, “promised impossibilities and performed nothing. The modern masters promise very little; they know that metals cannot be transmuted and that the elixir of life is a chimera but these philosophers, whose hands seem only made to dabble in dirt, and their eyes to pore over the microscope or crucible, have indeed performed miracles. They penetrate into the recesses of nature and show how she works in her hiding-places. They ascend into the heavens; they have discovered how the blood circulates, and the nature of the air we breathe. They have acquired new and almost unlimited powers; they can command the thunders of heaven, mimic the earthquake, and even mock the invisible world with its own shadows.”
paras.uz: «Bu fanning qadimgi o'qituvchilari, — dedi u, — imkonsiz narsalarni va'da qilishgan va hech narsa qilishmagan. Zamonaviy ustalar juda kam va'da qiladi; ular metallarni bir-biriga aylantirib bo'lmasligini va hayot eliksiri xayol ekanini bilishadi, lekin qo'llari faqat axloqda kovlashish uchun, ko'zlari esa mikroskop yoki tigel ustiga engashish uchun yaratilgandek tuyuladigan bu faylasuflar haqiqatan ham mo''jizalar yaratishgan. Ular tabiatning ichkarisiga kirib boradi va uning yashirin joylarida qanday ishlashini ko'rsatadi. Ular osmonga ko'tariladi; ular qon qanday aylanishini va biz nafas oladigan havoning tabiatini kashf etishgan. Ular yangi va deyarli cheksiz kuchlarga ega bo'lishgan; ular osmon momaqaldiroqlariga buyruq bera oladi, zilzilaga taqlid qila oladi va hatto ko'rinmas dunyoni uning o'z soyalari bilan masxara qila oladi.»

paras.en: Such were the professor’s words—rather let me say such the words of the fate—enounced to destroy me. As he went on I felt as if my soul were grappling with a palpable enemy; one by one the various keys were touched which formed the mechanism of my being; chord after chord was sounded, and soon my mind was filled with one thought, one conception, one purpose. So much has been done, exclaimed the soul of Frankenstein—more, far more, will I achieve; treading in the steps already marked, I will pioneer a new way, explore unknown powers, and unfold to the world the deepest mysteries of creation.
paras.uz: Professorning so'zlari shunday edi — yaxshisi, meni yo'q qilish uchun aytilgan taqdirning so'zlari shunday edi, deyay. U davom etarkan, men ruhim qo'l bilan ushlasa bo'ladigan dushman bilan olishayotgandek his qildim; borlig'im mexanizmini tashkil etgan turli tugmalar birma-bir bosildi; tor ketidan tor jarangladi va tez orada aqlim bitta fikr, bitta tushuncha, bitta maqsad bilan to'ldi. Shuncha ish qilingan, deb xitob qildi Frankenshteynning ruhi — men ko'proq, ancha ko'proq narsaga erishaman; allaqachon belgilangan izlardan borib, yangi yo'l ochaman, noma'lum kuchlarni o'rganaman va dunyoga yaratilishning eng chuqur sirlarini ochib beraman.

paras.en: I closed not my eyes that night. My internal being was in a state of insurrection and turmoil; I felt that order would thence arise, but I had no power to produce it. By degrees, after the morning’s dawn, sleep came. I awoke, and my yesternight’s thoughts were as a dream. There only remained a resolution to return to my ancient studies and to devote myself to a science for which I believed myself to possess a natural talent. On the same day I paid M. Waldman a visit. His manners in private were even more mild and attractive than in public, for there was a certain dignity in his mien during his lecture which in his own house was replaced by the greatest affability and kindness. I gave him pretty nearly the same account of my former pursuits as I had given to his fellow professor.
paras.uz: O'sha kecha ko'zimni yummadim. Ichki dunyom isyon va g'alayon holatida edi; undan tartib paydo bo'lishini his qilardim, lekin uni vujudga keltirishga qudratim yo'q edi. Asta-sekin, tong otgandan keyin uyqu keldi. Uyg'onganimda kechagi fikrlarim tushdek edi. Faqat qadimiy mashg'ulotlarimga qaytish va o'zimda tabiiy iste'dod bor deb hisoblagan fanga o'zimni bag'ishlash qarori qoldi. O'sha kuni men janob Valdmanga tashrif buyurdim. Uning shaxsiy muomalasi ko'pchilik oldidagidan ham muloyimroq va jozibaliroq edi, chunki ma'ruza paytidagi qiyofasida ma'lum viqor bor edi, u o'z uyida eng katta xushmuomalalik va mehribonlik bilan almashtirilgan edi. Men unga avvalgi mashg'ulotlarim haqida hamkasb professoriga bergan hisobotga deyarli o'xshash hisobot berdim.

paras.en: He heard with attention the little narration concerning my studies and smiled at the names of Cornelius Agrippa and Paracelsus, but without the contempt that M. Krempe had exhibited. He said that “These were men to whose indefatigable zeal modern philosophers were indebted for most of the foundations of their knowledge. They had left to us, as an easier task, to give new names and arrange in connected classifications the facts which they in a great degree had been the instruments of bringing to light. The labours of men of genius, however erroneously directed, scarcely ever fail in ultimately turning to the solid advantage of mankind.” I listened to his statement, which was delivered without any presumption or affectation, and then added that his lecture had removed my prejudices against modern chemists;
paras.uz: U o'qishlarim haqidagi kichik hikoyani diqqat bilan tingladi va Korneliy Agrippa va Paratsels nomlarini eshitib jilmaydi, lekin janob Krempe ko'rsatgan nafratsiz. U dedi: «Bular zamonaviy faylasuflar bilimlarining ko'p asoslari uchun charchoq bilmas g'ayratidan qarzdor bo'lgan odamlar edi. Ular bizga osonroq vazifa sifatida yangi nomlar berishni va katta darajada o'zlari yuzaga chiqarishga vosita bo'lgan faktlarni izchil tasniflarga solishni qoldirishgan. Daho odamlarning mehnati, qanchalik noto'g'ri yo'naltirilgan bo'lmasin, oxir-oqibat insoniyatning mustahkam foydasiga aylanmasdan qolmaydi.» Men uning hech qanday takabburlik yoki soxtaliksiz aytilgan bayonotini tingladim, keyin uning ma'ruzasi zamonaviy kimyogarlarga nisbatan xurofotlarimni yo'q qilganini qo'shimcha qildim;

paras.en: I expressed myself in measured terms, with the modesty and deference due from a youth to his instructor, without letting escape (inexperience in life would have made me ashamed) any of the enthusiasm which stimulated my intended labours. I requested his advice concerning the books I ought to procure.
paras.uz: men o'zimni o'lchovli iboralar bilan, yigitning ustoziga nisbatan lozim bo'lgan kamtarlik va hurmat bilan ifoda etdim, rejalashtirgan mehnatlarimni rag'batlantirgan ishtiyoqning hech qanday qismini (hayotdagi tajribasizlik meni uyaltirgan bo'lardi) bildirib qo'ymadim. Men undan qanday kitoblarni sotib olishim kerakligi haqida maslahat so'radim.

paras.en: “I am happy,” said M. Waldman, “to have gained a disciple; and if your application equals your ability, I have no doubt of your success. Chemistry is that branch of natural philosophy in which the greatest improvements have been and may be made; it is on that account that I have made it my peculiar study; but at the same time, I have not neglected the other branches of science. A man would make but a very sorry chemist if he attended to that department of human knowledge alone. If your wish is to become really a man of science and not merely a petty experimentalist, I should advise you to apply to every branch of natural philosophy, including mathematics.”
paras.uz: «Shogird orttirganimdan xursandman, — dedi janob Valdman, — va agar tirishqoqligingiz qobiliyatingizga teng bo'lsa, muvaffaqiyatingizga shubham yo'q. Kimyo tabiat falsafasining eng katta yutuqlarga erishilgan va erishilishi mumkin bo'lgan sohasi; shuning uchun men uni o'zimning alohida mashg'ulotim qilganman; lekin shu bilan birga, fanning boshqa sohalarini ham e'tibordan chetda qoldirmaganman. Agar inson faqat inson bilimining shu sohasi bilan shug'ullansa, juda ayanchli kimyogar bo'lardi. Agar sizning istagingiz shunchaki mayda tajribachi emas, balki haqiqatan ham ilm odami bo'lish bo'lsa, sizga tabiat falsafasining har bir sohasiga, jumladan matematikaga ham kirishishni maslahat beraman.»

paras.en: He then took me into his laboratory and explained to me the uses of his various machines, instructing me as to what I ought to procure and promising me the use of his own when I should have advanced far enough in the science not to derange their mechanism. He also gave me the list of books which I had requested, and I took my leave.
paras.uz: Keyin u meni laboratoriyasiga olib kirdi va menga turli mashinalarining vazifalarini tushuntirdi, nimalarni sotib olishim kerakligi haqida ko'rsatma berdi va men fanda ularning mexanizmini buzib qo'ymaydigan darajada ilgarilaganimda o'z asboblaridan foydalanishga ruxsat berishni va'da qildi. U menga so'ragan kitoblar ro'yxatini ham berdi va men xayrlashdim.

paras.en: Thus ended a day memorable to me; it decided my future destiny.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib men uchun unutilmas kun tugadi; u kelajakdagi taqdirimni hal qildi.

paras.en: From this day natural philosophy, and particularly chemistry, in the most comprehensive sense of the term, became nearly my sole occupation. I read with ardour those works, so full of genius and discrimination, which modern inquirers have written on these subjects. I attended the lectures and cultivated the acquaintance of the men of science of the university, and I found even in M. Krempe a great deal of sound sense and real information, combined, it is true, with a repulsive physiognomy and manners, but not on that account the less valuable. In M. Waldman I found a true friend. His gentleness was never tinged by dogmatism, and his instructions were given with an air of frankness and good nature that banished every idea of pedantry. In a thousand ways he smoothed for me the path of knowledge and made the most abstruse inquiries clear and facile to my apprehension. My application was at first fluctuating and uncertain; it gained strength as I proceeded and soon became so ardent and eager that the stars often disappeared in the light of morning whilst I was yet engaged in my laboratory.
paras.uz: Shu kundan boshlab tabiat falsafasi, ayniqsa so'zning eng keng ma'nosidagi kimyo, deyarli yagona mashg'ulotimga aylandi. Zamonaviy tadqiqotchilar bu mavzularda yozgan, daho va zukkolikka to'la asarlarni ishtiyoq bilan o'qidim. Ma'ruzalarga qatnashdim va universitet olimlari bilan tanishlik orttirdim, hatto janob Krempeda ham ko'p sog'lom aql va haqiqiy bilim topdim, to'g'ri, ular jirkanch qiyofa va muomala bilan qo'shilgan edi, lekin shuning uchun kam qadrli emas edi. Janob Valdmanda chin do'st topdim. Uning muloyimligiga hech qachon aqidaparastlik aralashmasdi va saboqlarini ilm-fan bilan maqtanish haqidagi har qanday fikrni quvib yuboradigan samimiylik va xushfe'llik bilan berardi. U ming xil yo'l bilan men uchun bilim yo'lini tekisladi va eng mavhum izlanishlarni ham men uchun ravshan va oson qildi. Tirishqoqligim dastlab o'zgaruvchan va noaniq edi; oldinga borgan sari kuch oldi va tez orada shunchalik qizg'in va ishtiyoqli bo'ldiki, men hali laboratoriyamda band bo'lganimda yulduzlar ko'pincha tong nurida g'oyib bo'lib ketardi.

paras.en: As I applied so closely, it may be easily conceived that my progress was rapid. My ardour was indeed the astonishment of the students, and my proficiency that of the masters. Professor Krempe often asked me, with a sly smile, how Cornelius Agrippa went on, whilst M. Waldman expressed the most heartfelt exultation in my progress. Two years passed in this manner, during which I paid no visit to Geneva, but was engaged, heart and soul, in the pursuit of some discoveries which I hoped to make. None but those who have experienced them can conceive of the enticements of science. In other studies you go as far as others have gone before you, and there is nothing more to know; but in a scientific pursuit there is continual food for discovery and wonder.
paras.uz: Shunchalik zo'r berib shug'ullanganim uchun yutuqlarim tez bo'lganini osongina tasavvur qilish mumkin. Mening ishtiyoqim haqiqatan ham talabalarni, mahoratim esa ustozlarni hayratga solardi. Professor Krempe ko'pincha ayyorona jilmayib, Korneliy Agrippa qanday ketyapti, deb so'rardi, janob Valdman esa yutuqlarimdan chin yurakdan quvonchini bildirardi. Shu tarzda ikki yil o'tdi, bu vaqt davomida men Jenevaga bormadim, balki qilishga umid qilgan ba'zi kashfiyotlar ortidan jonu dil bilan band edim. Ularni boshdan kechirmaganlar ilmning jozibasini tasavvur qila olmaydi. Boshqa mashg'ulotlarda siz sizdan oldingilar borgan joygacha borasiz va bilishga boshqa narsa qolmaydi; lekin ilmiy izlanishda kashfiyot va hayrat uchun doimiy ozuqa bor.

paras.en: A mind of moderate capacity which closely pursues one study must infallibly arrive at great proficiency in that study; and I, who continually sought the attainment of one object of pursuit and was solely wrapped up in this, improved so rapidly that at the end of two years I made some discoveries in the improvement of some chemical instruments, which procured me great esteem and admiration at the university. When I had arrived at this point and had become as well acquainted with the theory and practice of natural philosophy as depended on the lessons of any of the professors at Ingolstadt, my residence there being no longer conducive to my improvements, I thought of returning to my friends and my native town, when an incident happened that protracted my stay.
paras.uz: Bitta fanni astoydil o'rganadigan o'rtacha qobiliyatli aql o'sha fanda muqarrar ravishda katta mahoratga erishadi; doimo bitta maqsadga erishishni izlagan va faqat shunga berilgan men shunchalik tez rivojlandimki, ikki yil oxirida ba'zi kimyoviy asboblarni takomillashtirishda bir nechta kashfiyot qildim, bu menga universitetda katta hurmat va hayrat keltirdi. Shu nuqtaga yetib, tabiat falsafasining nazariyasi va amaliyotini Ingolshtadtdagi har qanday professorning darslariga bog'liq bo'lgan darajada yaxshi o'zlashtirgach, u yerda yashashim endi rivojlanishimga xizmat qilmayotgani uchun do'stlarim va ona shahrimga qaytishni o'ylay boshladim, shunda qolishimni cho'zgan bir voqea yuz berdi.

paras.en: One of the phenomena which had peculiarly attracted my attention was the structure of the human frame, and, indeed, any animal endued with life. Whence, I often asked myself, did the principle of life proceed? It was a bold question, and one which has ever been considered as a mystery; yet with how many things are we upon the brink of becoming acquainted, if cowardice or carelessness did not restrain our inquiries. I revolved these circumstances in my mind and determined thenceforth to apply myself more particularly to those branches of natural philosophy which relate to physiology. Unless I had been animated by an almost supernatural enthusiasm, my application to this study would have been irksome and almost intolerable. To examine the causes of life, we must first have recourse to death. I became acquainted with the science of anatomy, but this was not sufficient;
paras.uz: Diqqatimni alohida tortgan hodisalardan biri inson vujudining, aslida hayot ato etilgan har qanday hayvonning tuzilishi edi. Hayot tamoyili qayerdan kelib chiqadi, deb ko'pincha o'zimdan so'rardim. Bu dadil savol edi va doimo sir deb hisoblangan savol edi; shunga qaramay, agar qo'rqoqlik yoki beparvolik izlanishlarimizni to'xtatmaganida, qanchadan-qancha narsalarni bilib olish arafasida turibmiz. Men bu holatlarni xayolimda aylantirdim va bundan buyon tabiat falsafasining fiziologiyaga tegishli sohalariga alohida kirishishga qaror qildim. Agar meni deyarli g'ayritabiiy ishtiyoq jonlantirmaganida, bu fan bilan shug'ullanish zerikarli va deyarli chidab bo'lmas bo'lardi. Hayot sabablarini tekshirish uchun avvalo o'limga murojaat qilishimiz kerak. Men anatomiya ilmi bilan tanishdim, lekin bu yetarli emas edi;

paras.en: I must also observe the natural decay and corruption of the human body. In my education my father had taken the greatest precautions that my mind should be impressed with no supernatural horrors. I do not ever remember to have trembled at a tale of superstition or to have feared the apparition of a spirit. Darkness had no effect upon my fancy, and a churchyard was to me merely the receptacle of bodies deprived of life, which, from being the seat of beauty and strength, had become food for the worm. Now I was led to examine the cause and progress of this decay and forced to spend days and nights in vaults and charnel-houses. My attention was fixed upon every object the most insupportable to the delicacy of the human feelings. I saw how the fine form of man was degraded and wasted;
paras.uz: men inson tanasining tabiiy chirishi va buzilishini ham kuzatishim kerak edi. Tarbiyamda otam aqlimga hech qanday g'ayritabiiy dahshatlar o'rnashmasligi uchun eng katta ehtiyot choralarini ko'rgan edi. Hech qachon xurofiy hikoyadan titraganimni yoki arvoh paydo bo'lishidan qo'rqqanimni eslamayman. Qorong'ilik xayolimga ta'sir qilmasdi, qabriston esa men uchun shunchaki go'zallik va kuch maskani bo'lgandan keyin qurtga yem bo'lgan, hayotdan mahrum jasadlar joyi edi. Endi men bu chirishning sababi va borishini tekshirishga undaldim va kunlab, kechalab sag'analar va murdaxonalarda o'tkazishga majbur bo'ldim. Diqqatim inson his-tuyg'ularining nozikligiga eng chidab bo'lmaydigan har bir narsaga qadaldi. Men insonning go'zal qiyofasi qanday xorlanib, yemirilishini ko'rdim;

paras.en: I beheld the corruption of death succeed to the blooming cheek of life; I saw how the worm inherited the wonders of the eye and brain. I paused, examining and analysing all the minutiae of causation, as exemplified in the change from life to death, and death to life, until from the midst of this darkness a sudden light broke in upon me—a light so brilliant and wondrous, yet so simple, that while I became dizzy with the immensity of the prospect which it illustrated, I was surprised that among so many men of genius who had directed their inquiries towards the same science, that I alone should be reserved to discover so astonishing a secret.
paras.uz: hayotning gullagan yonog'i o'rnini o'limning chirishi egallaganini ko'rdim; qurt ko'z va miyaning mo''jizalariga qanday merosxo'r bo'lishini ko'rdim. Men to'xtab, hayotdan o'limga va o'limdan hayotga o'tishda namoyon bo'ladigan sababiyatning barcha mayda tafsilotlarini tekshirib, tahlil qildim, toki bu zulmat o'rtasidan birdan menga nur yog'ilmaguncha — shunchalik yorqin va ajoyib, shu bilan birga shunchalik oddiy nurki, u ochgan manzaraning ulkanligidan boshim aylanib qolgan bo'lsa ham, xuddi shu fanga izlanishlarini qaratgan shuncha daho odamlar orasida aynan menga shunday hayratlanarli sirni kashf etish nasib etganiga hayron bo'ldim.

paras.en: Remember, I am not recording the vision of a madman. The sun does not more certainly shine in the heavens than that which I now affirm is true. Some miracle might have produced it, yet the stages of the discovery were distinct and probable. After days and nights of incredible labour and fatigue, I succeeded in discovering the cause of generation and life; nay, more, I became myself capable of bestowing animation upon lifeless matter.
paras.uz: Unutmang, men telbaning xayolini yozib qo'ymayapman. Quyosh osmonda men hozir tasdiqlayotgan narsa haqiqat ekanidan ko'ra aniqroq porlamaydi. Uni qandaydir mo''jiza vujudga keltirgan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin kashfiyot bosqichlari aniq va ehtimolli edi. Aql bovar qilmas mehnat va charchoqli kunlar va kechalardan keyin men nasl va hayot sababini kashf etishga muvaffaq bo'ldim; yo'q, bundan ham ko'proq — o'zim jonsiz moddaga jon ato eta oladigan bo'ldim.

paras.en: The astonishment which I had at first experienced on this discovery soon gave place to delight and rapture. After so much time spent in painful labour, to arrive at once at the summit of my desires was the most gratifying consummation of my toils. But this discovery was so great and overwhelming that all the steps by which I had been progressively led to it were obliterated, and I beheld only the result. What had been the study and desire of the wisest men since the creation of the world was now within my grasp. Not that, like a magic scene, it all opened upon me at once: the information I had obtained was of a nature rather to direct my endeavours so soon as I should point them towards the object of my search than to exhibit that object already accomplished. I was like the Arabian who had been buried with the dead and found a passage to life, aided only by one glimmering and seemingly ineffectual light.
paras.uz: Bu kashfiyotdan dastlab boshdan kechirgan hayratim tez orada zavq va vajdga o'rin berdi. Og'riqli mehnatga shuncha vaqt sarflagandan keyin birdaniga istaklarimning cho'qqisiga erishish mehnatlarimning eng qoniqarli yakuni edi. Lekin bu kashfiyot shunchalik buyuk va hayratlanarli ediki, meni unga bosqichma-bosqich olib kelgan barcha qadamlar o'chib ketdi va men faqat natijani ko'rdim. Dunyo yaratilganidan beri eng dono odamlarning izlanishi va orzusi bo'lgan narsa endi qo'limda edi. Hammasi sehrli manzara kabi birdaniga menga ochildi demoqchi emasman: men olgan ma'lumot o'sha maqsadni allaqachon amalga oshirilgan holda ko'rsatishdan ko'ra, harakatlarimni izlanishim maqsadiga qaratishim bilan ularni yo'naltiradigan xususiyatda edi. Men o'liklar bilan birga ko'mib yuborilgan va faqat bitta xira va samarasizdek ko'ringan nur yordamida hayotga yo'l topgan arabga o'xshardim.

paras.en: I see by your eagerness and the wonder and hope which your eyes express, my friend, that you expect to be informed of the secret with which I am acquainted; that cannot be; listen patiently until the end of my story, and you will easily perceive why I am reserved upon that subject. I will not lead you on, unguarded and ardent as I then was, to your destruction and infallible misery. Learn from me, if not by my precepts, at least by my example, how dangerous is the acquirement of knowledge and how much happier that man is who believes his native town to be the world, than he who aspires to become greater than his nature will allow.
paras.uz: Ishtiyoqingizdan va ko'zlaringiz ifodalayotgan hayrat va umiddan ko'ryapman, do'stim, siz men bilgan sirdan xabardor bo'lishni kutyapsiz; bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas; hikoyamning oxirigacha sabr bilan tinglang va nega bu mavzuda tilimni tiyayotganimni osongina tushunasiz. Men sizni, o'shanda men qanday ehtiyotsiz va qizg'in bo'lgan bo'lsam, shunday holda halokatingizga va muqarrar baxtsizligingizga boshlamayman. Mendan, agar nasihatlarim orqali bo'lmasa, hech bo'lmasa namunam orqali bilim olish qanchalik xavfli ekanini va ona shahrini butun dunyo deb biladigan odam tabiati ruxsat berganidan ulug'roq bo'lishga intilgan odamdan qanchalik baxtliroq ekanini o'rganing.

paras.en: When I found so astonishing a power placed within my hands, I hesitated a long time concerning the manner in which I should employ it. Although I possessed the capacity of bestowing animation, yet to prepare a frame for the reception of it, with all its intricacies of fibres, muscles, and veins, still remained a work of inconceivable difficulty and labour. I doubted at first whether I should attempt the creation of a being like myself, or one of simpler organization; but my imagination was too much exalted by my first success to permit me to doubt of my ability to give life to an animal as complex and wonderful as man. The materials at present within my command hardly appeared adequate to so arduous an undertaking, but I doubted not that I should ultimately succeed.
paras.uz: Qo'limga shunday hayratlanarli qudrat berilganini ko'rib, uni qanday ishlatishim haqida uzoq ikkilandim. Garchi jon ato etish qobiliyatiga ega bo'lsam ham, uni qabul qilish uchun barcha murakkab tolalari, mushaklari va tomirlari bilan vujud tayyorlash hali ham tasavvur qilib bo'lmas qiyinchilik va mehnat talab qiladigan ish edi. Dastlab o'zimga o'xshash mavjudotni yaratishga urinishim kerakmi yoki soddaroq tuzilishdagisinimi, deb ikkilandim; lekin birinchi muvaffaqiyatim tasavvurimni shunchalik yuksaltirgan ediki, inson kabi murakkab va ajoyib hayvonga hayot bera olishimga shubha qilishga yo'l qo'ymadi. Hozir ixtiyorimdagi materiallar bunday mashaqqatli ish uchun zo'rg'a yetarli tuyulardi, lekin oxir-oqibat muvaffaqiyat qozonishimga shubha qilmasdim.

paras.en: I prepared myself for a multitude of reverses; my operations might be incessantly baffled, and at last my work be imperfect, yet when I considered the improvement which every day takes place in science and mechanics, I was encouraged to hope my present attempts would at least lay the foundations of future success. Nor could I consider the magnitude and complexity of my plan as any argument of its impracticability. It was with these feelings that I began the creation of a human being. As the minuteness of the parts formed a great hindrance to my speed, I resolved, contrary to my first intention, to make the being of a gigantic stature, that is to say, about eight feet in height, and proportionably large. After having formed this determination and having spent some months in successfully collecting and arranging my materials, I began.
paras.uz: Men ko'plab muvaffaqiyatsizliklarga tayyorlandim; harakatlarim tinimsiz barbod bo'lishi va oxir-oqibat ishim nomukammal chiqishi mumkin edi, lekin har kuni ilm va mexanikada yuz berayotgan taraqqiyotni o'ylab, hozirgi urinishlarim hech bo'lmasa kelajakdagi muvaffaqiyatga poydevor qo'yadi, degan umid bilan ruhlandim. Rejamning ulkanligi va murakkabligini ham uning amalga oshmasligiga dalil deb hisoblay olmasdim. Shu tuyg'ular bilan men inson yaratishni boshladim. Qismlarning mayda bo'lishi tezligimga katta to'siq bo'lgani uchun, dastlabki niyatimga zid ravishda, mavjudotni ulkan bo'yli, ya'ni taxminan sakkiz fut balandlikda va mutanosib ravishda katta qilishga qaror qildim. Bu qarorga kelib, bir necha oy materiallarimni muvaffaqiyatli to'plab, tartibga solgach, ishga kirishdim.

paras.en: No one can conceive the variety of feelings which bore me onwards, like a hurricane, in the first enthusiasm of success. Life and death appeared to me ideal bounds, which I should first break through, and pour a torrent of light into our dark world. A new species would bless me as its creator and source; many happy and excellent natures would owe their being to me. No father could claim the gratitude of his child so completely as I should deserve theirs. Pursuing these reflections, I thought that if I could bestow animation upon lifeless matter, I might in process of time (although I now found it impossible) renew life where death had apparently devoted the body to corruption.
paras.uz: Muvaffaqiyatning ilk ishtiyoqida meni bo'rondek oldinga olib borgan turli his-tuyg'ularni hech kim tasavvur qila olmaydi. Hayot va o'lim menga avval yorib o'tishim va qorong'i dunyomizga nur selini to'kishim kerak bo'lgan xayoliy chegaralardek tuyulardi. Yangi bir zot meni o'z yaratuvchisi va manbai sifatida duo qiladi; ko'plab baxtli va ajoyib tabiatlar borliqlari uchun mendan qarzdor bo'ladi.
