Hech bir ota o'z farzandining minnatdorligini men ularnikiga loyiq bo'lganimdek to'liq talab qila olmasdi. Bu mulohazalarni davom ettirib, agar jonsiz moddaga jon ato eta olsam, vaqt o'tishi bilan (garchi endi buni imkonsiz deb bilsam ham) o'lim aftidan chirishga topshirgan tanada hayotni yangilashim mumkin, deb o'yladim.

paras.en: These thoughts supported my spirits, while I pursued my undertaking with unremitting ardour. My cheek had grown pale with study, and my person had become emaciated with confinement. Sometimes, on the very brink of certainty, I failed; yet still I clung to the hope which the next day or the next hour might realise. One secret which I alone possessed was the hope to which I had dedicated myself; and the moon gazed on my midnight labours, while, with unrelaxed and breathless eagerness, I pursued nature to her hiding-places. Who shall conceive the horrors of my secret toil as I dabbled among the unhallowed damps of the grave or tortured the living animal to animate the lifeless clay? My limbs now tremble, and my eyes swim with the remembrance; but then a resistless and almost frantic impulse urged me forward;
paras.uz: Bu fikrlar ishimni tinimsiz ishtiyoq bilan davom ettirarkanman, ruhimni qo'llab-quvvatlardi. Yonog'im mashg'ulotdan oqarib ketgan, qamalib o'tirishdan vujudim ozib ketgan edi. Ba'zan aniqlikning qoq yoqasida muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrardim; lekin baribir keyingi kun yoki keyingi soat ro'yobga chiqarishi mumkin bo'lgan umidga yopishib olardim. Faqat men ega bo'lgan bitta sir o'zimni bag'ishlagan umid edi; va men bo'shashmas va nafasim tiqilgan ishtiyoq bilan tabiatni yashirin joylarigacha ta'qib qilarkanman, oy mening yarim tungi mehnatlarimga tikilib turardi. Qabrning nopok namliklari orasida kovlashganimda yoki jonsiz loyga jon kiritish uchun tirik hayvonni qiynaganimda yashirin mehnatimning dahshatlarini kim tasavvur qila oladi? Endi esga olsam, a'zolarim titraydi va ko'zlarim jimirlaydi; lekin o'shanda to'xtatib bo'lmas va deyarli telbalarcha turtki meni oldinga undardi;

paras.en: I seemed to have lost all soul or sensation but for this one pursuit. It was indeed but a passing trance, that only made me feel with renewed acuteness so soon as, the unnatural stimulus ceasing to operate, I had returned to my old habits. I collected bones from charnel-houses and disturbed, with profane fingers, the tremendous secrets of the human frame. In a solitary chamber, or rather cell, at the top of the house, and separated from all the other apartments by a gallery and staircase, I kept my workshop of filthy creation; my eyeballs were starting from their sockets in attending to the details of my employment. The dissecting room and the slaughter-house furnished many of my materials; and often did my human nature turn with loathing from my occupation, whilst, still urged on by an eagerness which perpetually increased, I brought my work near to a conclusion.
paras.uz: go'yo bu yagona izlanishdan boshqa barcha ruh va hissiyotni yo'qotgandek edim. Bu aslida o'tkinchi bir mastlik edi, g'ayritabiiy turtki ta'sir qilishni to'xtatib, eski odatlarimga qaytishim bilanoq, u meni yangilangan o'tkirlik bilan his qilishga majbur qildi. Men murdaxonalardan suyaklar yig'dim va inson vujudining dahshatli sirlarini nopok barmoqlar bilan bezovta qildim. Uyning eng tepasida, galereya va zinapoya bilan boshqa barcha xonalardan ajratilgan yolg'iz xonada, yaxshisi kamerada men iflos ijod ustaxonamni saqlardim; ishimning tafsilotlariga e'tibor berarkanman, ko'z qorachiqlarim kosalaridan chiqib ketay derdi. Yorib ko'rish xonasi va qassobxona materiallarimning ko'pini yetkazib berardi; va ko'pincha insoniy tabiatim mashg'ulotimdan jirkanib yuz o'girardi, lekin doimo ortib borayotgan ishtiyoq bilan undalgan holda ishimni yakuniga yaqinlashtirdim.

paras.en: The summer months passed while I was thus engaged, heart and soul, in one pursuit. It was a most beautiful season; never did the fields bestow a more plentiful harvest or the vines yield a more luxuriant vintage, but my eyes were insensible to the charms of nature. And the same feelings which made me neglect the scenes around me caused me also to forget those friends who were so many miles absent, and whom I had not seen for so long a time. I knew my silence disquieted them, and I well remembered the words of my father: “I know that while you are pleased with yourself you will think of us with affection, and we shall hear regularly from you. You must pardon me if I regard any interruption in your correspondence as a proof that your other duties are equally neglected.”
paras.uz: Men shu tarzda jonu dil bilan bitta izlanishga berilganimda yoz oylari o'tdi. Bu eng go'zal fasl edi; dalalar hech qachon bundan mo'lroq hosil bermagan, uzumzorlar bundan serobroq uzum bermagan edi, lekin ko'zlarim tabiatning jozibalarini sezmasdi. Atrofimdagi manzaralarni e'tiborsiz qoldirishimga sabab bo'lgan o'sha tuyg'ular meni shuncha mil uzoqda bo'lgan va shuncha vaqt ko'rmagan do'stlarimni ham unutishga majbur qildi. Jimligim ularni bezovta qilayotganini bilardim va otamning so'zlarini yaxshi eslardim: «Bilaman, o'zingdan mamnun bo'lsang, bizni mehr bilan eslaysan va sendan muntazam xabar olib turamiz. Agar yozishmalaringdagi har qanday uzilishni boshqa burchlaringni ham xuddi shunday e'tiborsiz qoldirayotganingning isboti deb bilsam, meni kechirishing kerak.»

paras.en: I knew well therefore what would be my father’s feelings, but I could not tear my thoughts from my employment, loathsome in itself, but which had taken an irresistible hold of my imagination. I wished, as it were, to procrastinate all that related to my feelings of affection until the great object, which swallowed up every habit of my nature, should be completed.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun otamning his-tuyg'ulari qanday bo'lishini yaxshi bilardim, lekin fikrlarimni o'z-o'zidan jirkanch bo'lgan, ammo tasavvurimni qarshi turib bo'lmas darajada egallab olgan mashg'ulotimdan uzib ololmasdim. Go'yo tabiatimning har bir odatini yutib yuborgan buyuk maqsad tugallanmaguncha, mehr tuyg'ularimga tegishli hamma narsani kechiktirmoqchi edim.

paras.en: I then thought that my father would be unjust if he ascribed my neglect to vice or faultiness on my part, but I am now convinced that he was justified in conceiving that I should not be altogether free from blame. A human being in perfection ought always to preserve a calm and peaceful mind and never to allow passion or a transitory desire to disturb his tranquillity. I do not think that the pursuit of knowledge is an exception to this rule. If the study to which you apply yourself has a tendency to weaken your affections and to destroy your taste for those simple pleasures in which no alloy can possibly mix, then that study is certainly unlawful, that is to say, not befitting the human mind. If this rule were always observed; if no man allowed any pursuit whatsoever to interfere with the tranquillity of his domestic affections, Greece had not been enslaved, Cæsar would have spared his country, America would have been discovered more gradually, and the empires of Mexico and Peru had not been destroyed.
paras.uz: O'shanda men, agar otam beparvoligimni mening illatim yoki aybimga nisbat bersa, adolatsizlik qilgan bo'ladi, deb o'ylardim, lekin endi men butunlay aybsiz bo'lmasligim kerak deb o'ylashga haqli bo'lganiga aminman. Mukammal inson doimo xotirjam va osoyishta aqlni saqlashi va hech qachon ehtiros yoki o'tkinchi istakning xotirjamligini buzishiga yo'l qo'ymasligi kerak. Bilim izlash bu qoidadan istisno deb o'ylamayman. Agar siz shug'ullanayotgan fan mehringizni zaiflashtirishga va hech qanday aralashma qo'shilishi mumkin bo'lmagan o'sha oddiy zavqlarga didingizni yo'q qilishga moyil bo'lsa, unda bu fan, albatta, nojoiz, ya'ni inson aqliga munosib emas. Agar bu qoidaga doimo rioya qilinganida; agar hech bir inson har qanday mashg'ulotning oilaviy mehrining xotirjamligiga aralashishiga yo'l qo'ymaganida, Yunoniston qul qilinmagan, Sezar o'z mamlakatini ayagan, Amerika asta-sekinroq kashf etilgan va Meksika va Peru imperiyalari vayron qilinmagan bo'lardi.

paras.en: But I forget that I am moralizing in the most interesting part of my tale, and your looks remind me to proceed.
paras.uz: Lekin hikoyamning eng qiziq joyida nasihat o'qiyotganimni unutibman, nigohlaringiz esa davom etishimni eslatyapti.

paras.en: My father made no reproach in his letters and only took notice of my silence by inquiring into my occupations more particularly than before. Winter, spring, and summer passed away during my labours; but I did not watch the blossom or the expanding leaves—sights which before always yielded me supreme delight—so deeply was I engrossed in my occupation. The leaves of that year had withered before my work drew near to a close, and now every day showed me more plainly how well I had succeeded. But my enthusiasm was checked by my anxiety, and I appeared rather like one doomed by slavery to toil in the mines, or any other unwholesome trade than an artist occupied by his favourite employment.
paras.uz: Otam maktublarida hech qanday ta'na qilmadi va jimligimni faqat mashg'ulotlarim haqida avvalgidan ko'ra batafsilroq so'rash bilan bildirib qo'ydi. Mehnatlarim davomida qish, bahor va yoz o'tib ketdi; lekin men gullashni yoki yoyilayotgan barglarni — ilgari doimo menga cheksiz zavq bag'ishlagan manzaralarni kuzatmadim, chunki mashg'ulotimga shunchalik chuqur berilgan edim. O'sha yilning barglari ishim yakuniga yaqinlashmasdan oldin so'lib bo'lgan edi va endi har kuni menga qanchalik yaxshi muvaffaqiyat qozonganimni tobora aniqroq ko'rsatardi. Lekin ishtiyoqimni xavotirim jilovlab turardi va men sevimli mashg'uloti bilan band san'atkordan ko'ra ko'proq qullik bilan konlarda yoki boshqa biror nosog'lom hunarda mehnat qilishga mahkum etilgan odamga o'xshardim.

paras.en: Every night I was oppressed by a slow fever, and I became nervous to a most painful degree; the fall of a leaf startled me, and I shunned my fellow creatures as if I had been guilty of a crime. Sometimes I grew alarmed at the wreck I perceived that I had become; the energy of my purpose alone sustained me: my labours would soon end, and I believed that exercise and amusement would then drive away incipient disease; and I promised myself both of these when my creation should be complete.
paras.uz: Har kecha meni sekin isitma ezardi va men eng og'riqli darajada asabiy bo'lib qoldim; bargning tushishi meni cho'chitardi va go'yo jinoyat qilgandek hamjinslarimdan qochardim. Ba'zan o'zim aylangan xarobani ko'rib xavotirga tushardim; meni faqat maqsadimning kuchi ushlab turardi: mehnatlarim tez orada tugaydi va shunda jismoniy mashq va ko'ngilxushlik boshlanayotgan kasallikni haydab yuboradi, deb ishonardim; ijodim tugallanganda o'zimga ikkalasini ham va'da qilardim.

paras.en: It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils. With an anxiety that almost amounted to agony, I collected the instruments of life around me, that I might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing that lay at my feet. It was already one in the morning; the rain pattered dismally against the panes, and my candle was nearly burnt out, when, by the glimmer of the half-extinguished light, I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.
paras.uz: Mehnatlarimning yakunini noyabrning ma'yus bir kechasida ko'rdim. Deyarli azobga yetgan xavotir bilan oyog'im ostida yotgan jonsiz narsaga borliq uchqunini kiritish uchun atrofimga hayot asboblarini to'pladim. Soat allaqachon tungi bir edi; yomg'ir derazalarga g'amgin chertardi, shamim esa deyarli yonib bitgan edi, shunda yarim o'chgan nurning xira yog'dusida maxluqning xira sariq ko'zi ochilganini ko'rdim; u og'ir nafas oldi va a'zolarini talvasali harakat titratdi.

paras.en: How can I describe my emotions at this catastrophe, or how delineate the wretch whom with such infinite pains and care I had endeavoured to form? His limbs were in proportion, and I had selected his features as beautiful. Beautiful! Great God! His yellow skin scarcely covered the work of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing; his teeth of a pearly whiteness; but these luxuriances only formed a more horrid contrast with his watery eyes, that seemed almost of the same colour as the dun-white sockets in which they were set, his shrivelled complexion and straight black lips.
paras.uz: Bu falokatdagi his-tuyg'ularimni qanday ta'riflay, cheksiz mashaqqat va g'amxo'rlik bilan yaratishga uringan bu bechorani qanday tasvirlay? Uning a'zolari mutanosib edi va men uning yuz chiziqlarini go'zal deb tanlagan edim. Go'zal! Buyuk Xudo! Uning sariq terisi ostidagi mushak va tomirlar to'rini zo'rg'a yopib turardi; sochlari yaltiroq qora va to'lqinli edi; tishlari marvariddek oppoq edi; lekin bu hashamatlar uning o'zlari joylashgan xira oq kosalar bilan deyarli bir xil rangdagi suvli ko'zlari, burishgan terisi va to'g'ri qora lablari bilan yanada dahshatli qarama-qarshilik hosil qilardi.

paras.en: The different accidents of life are not so changeable as the feelings of human nature. I had worked hard for nearly two years, for the sole purpose of infusing life into an inanimate body. For this I had deprived myself of rest and health. I had desired it with an ardour that far exceeded moderation; but now that I had finished, the beauty of the dream vanished, and breathless horror and disgust filled my heart. Unable to endure the aspect of the being I had created, I rushed out of the room and continued a long time traversing my bed-chamber, unable to compose my mind to sleep. At length lassitude succeeded to the tumult I had before endured, and I threw myself on the bed in my clothes, endeavouring to seek a few moments of forgetfulness. But it was in vain;
paras.uz: Hayotning turli hodisalari inson tabiatining his-tuyg'ulari kabi o'zgaruvchan emas. Men deyarli ikki yil faqat jonsiz tanaga hayot kiritish maqsadida qattiq mehnat qildim. Buning uchun o'zimni dam olish va sog'liqdan mahrum qildim. Men buni me'yordan ancha oshib ketgan ishtiyoq bilan istagan edim; lekin endi tugatgach, orzuning go'zalligi g'oyib bo'ldi va yuragimni nafasni bo'g'uvchi dahshat va jirkanish to'ldirdi. O'zim yaratgan mavjudotning qiyofasiga chiday olmay, xonadan otilib chiqdim va uzoq vaqt yotoqxonamda u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurdim, aqlimni uyquga tinchlantira olmadim. Nihoyat oldin boshdan kechirgan g'alayon o'rnini holsizlik egalladi va men bir necha lahzalik unutish izlab, kiyimim bilan karavotga o'zimni tashladim. Lekin bu behuda edi;

paras.en: I slept, indeed, but I was disturbed by the wildest dreams. I thought I saw Elizabeth, in the bloom of health, walking in the streets of Ingolstadt. Delighted and surprised, I embraced her, but as I imprinted the first kiss on her lips, they became livid with the hue of death; her features appeared to change, and I thought that I held the corpse of my dead mother in my arms; a shroud enveloped her form, and I saw the grave-worms crawling in the folds of the flannel. I started from my sleep with horror; a cold dew covered my forehead, my teeth chattered, and every limb became convulsed; when, by the dim and yellow light of the moon, as it forced its way through the window shutters, I beheld the wretch—the miserable monster whom I had created.
paras.uz: haqiqatan ham uxladim, lekin eng yovvoyi tushlar meni bezovta qildi. Men Elizabetni sog'lig'i gullab-yashnagan holda Ingolshtadt ko'chalarida yurganini ko'rgandek bo'ldim. Xursand va hayratda uni quchoqladim, lekin lablariga birinchi bo'sani qo'yganimda, ular o'lim tusidek ko'karib ketdi; uning yuz chiziqlari o'zgarganday tuyuldi va men qo'llarimda marhum onamning jasadini ushlab turgandek bo'ldim; uning qomatini kafan o'rab olgan edi va flanel burmalarida qabr qurtlari o'rmalab yurganini ko'rdim. Dahshat bilan uyqudan sakrab turdim; peshonamni sovuq ter qopladi, tishlarim taqillab, har bir a'zoyim talvasaga tushdi; shunda deraza qopqoqlari orasidan yorib kirgan oyning xira va sarg'ish nurida men o'sha bechorani — o'zim yaratgan ayanchli yirtqichni ko'rdim.

paras.en: He held up the curtain of the bed; and his eyes, if eyes they may be called, were fixed on me. His jaws opened, and he muttered some inarticulate sounds, while a grin wrinkled his cheeks. He might have spoken, but I did not hear; one hand was stretched out, seemingly to detain me, but I escaped and rushed downstairs. I took refuge in the courtyard belonging to the house which I inhabited, where I remained during the rest of the night, walking up and down in the greatest agitation, listening attentively, catching and fearing each sound as if it were to announce the approach of the demoniacal corpse to which I had so miserably given life.
paras.uz: U karavot pardasini ko'tarib turardi; uning ko'zlari, agar ularni ko'z deb atash mumkin bo'lsa, menga qadalgan edi. Jag'lari ochildi va u qandaydir tushunarsiz tovushlar g'o'ldiradi, yonoqlarini esa irjayish burishtirdi. U gapirgan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin men eshitmadim; bir qo'li, aftidan meni ushlab qolish uchun cho'zilgan edi, lekin men qochib, zinadan pastga otildim. Men yashayotgan uyga tegishli hovliga panoh topdim va tunning qolgan qismini o'sha yerda o'tkazdim, eng katta hayajonda u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurib, diqqat bilan tinglab, har bir tovushni go'yo u men shunchalik ayanchli tarzda hayot bergan iblisona jasadning yaqinlashayotganini e'lon qiladigandek ilib olib, undan qo'rqib turdim.

paras.en: Oh! No mortal could support the horror of that countenance. A mummy again endued with animation could not be so hideous as that wretch. I had gazed on him while unfinished; he was ugly then, but when those muscles and joints were rendered capable of motion, it became a thing such as even Dante could not have conceived.
paras.uz: Oh! Hech bir o'lar jon u chehraning dahshatiga bardosh bera olmasdi. Yana jon kiritilgan mumiyo ham o'sha bechoradek xunuk bo'la olmasdi. Men unga tugallanmagan holida tikilgan edim; u o'shanda ham xunuk edi, lekin o'sha mushaklar va bo'g'imlar harakatga qodir bo'lgach, u hatto Dante ham tasavvur qila olmaydigan narsaga aylandi.

paras.en: I passed the night wretchedly. Sometimes my pulse beat so quickly and hardly that I felt the palpitation of every artery; at others, I nearly sank to the ground through languor and extreme weakness. Mingled with this horror, I felt the bitterness of disappointment; dreams that had been my food and pleasant rest for so long a space were now become a hell to me; and the change was so rapid, the overthrow so complete!
paras.uz: Tunni ayanchli o'tkazdim. Ba'zan tomirim shunchalik tez va qattiq urardiki, har bir arteriyaning tepishini his qilardim; boshqa paytlarda holsizlik va haddan tashqari zaiflikdan yerga yiqilishimga sal qolardi. Bu dahshatga umidsizlikning achchig'i aralashib ketdi; shuncha vaqt mening ozuqam va yoqimli orom bo'lgan orzular endi men uchun do'zaxga aylangan edi; va o'zgarish shunchalik tez, ag'darilish shunchalik to'liq edi!

paras.en: Morning, dismal and wet, at length dawned and discovered to my sleepless and aching eyes the church of Ingolstadt, its white steeple and clock, which indicated the sixth hour. The porter opened the gates of the court, which had that night been my asylum, and I issued into the streets, pacing them with quick steps, as if I sought to avoid the wretch whom I feared every turning of the street would present to my view. I did not dare return to the apartment which I inhabited, but felt impelled to hurry on, although drenched by the rain which poured from a black and comfortless sky.
paras.uz: Nihoyat g'amgin va nam tong otdi va uyqusiz, og'riyotgan ko'zlarimga Ingolshtadt cherkovini, uning oltinchi soatni ko'rsatib turgan oq qo'ng'iroqxonasi va soatini ochib berdi. Darvozabon o'sha tun mening boshpanam bo'lgan hovlining darvozasini ochdi va men ko'chalarga chiqib, go'yo ko'chaning har bir burilishi ko'z oldimga keltiradi deb qo'rqqan bechoradan qochishga urinayotgandek tez qadamlar bilan yura boshladim. Yashayotgan xonamga qaytishga jur'at etmadim, lekin qora va ma'yus osmondan quyilayotgan yomg'irda ivib ketgan bo'lsam ham, shoshib oldinga borishga undalganini his qildim.

paras.en: I continued walking in this manner for some time, endeavouring by bodily exercise to ease the load that weighed upon my mind. I traversed the streets without any clear conception of where I was or what I was doing. My heart palpitated in the sickness of fear, and I hurried on with irregular steps, not daring to look about me:
paras.uz: Bir muddat shu tarzda yurishda davom etib, jismoniy harakat bilan aqlimni ezayotgan yukni yengillashtirishga urindim. Qayerda ekanim yoki nima qilayotganim haqida hech qanday aniq tasavvursiz ko'chalarni kezib chiqdim. Yuragim qo'rquv xastaligida urardi va atrofimga qarashga jur'at etmay, notekis qadamlar bilan shoshilardim:

paras.en: Like one who, on a lonely road, Doth walk in fear and dread, And, having once turned round, walks on, And turns no more his head; Because he knows a frightful fiend Doth close behind him tread.
paras.uz: Yolg'iz yo'lda qo'rquv-u / Dahshat ichra yurgan kabi, / Bir bor ortga qarab, so'ng / Boshin boshqa burmagan kabi; / Chunki u biladi: qo'rqinchli / Iblis izma-iz kelar uning.

paras.en: [Coleridge’s “Ancient Mariner.”]
paras.uz: [Kolrijning «Keksa dengizchi» dostonidan.]

paras.en: Continuing thus, I came at length opposite to the inn at which the various diligences and carriages usually stopped. Here I paused, I knew not why; but I remained some minutes with my eyes fixed on a coach that was coming towards me from the other end of the street. As it drew nearer I observed that it was the Swiss diligence; it stopped just where I was standing, and on the door being opened, I perceived Henry Clerval, who, on seeing me, instantly sprung out. “My dear Frankenstein,” exclaimed he, “how glad I am to see you! How fortunate that you should be here at the very moment of my alighting!”
paras.uz: Shu tarzda davom etib, nihoyat turli pochta aravalari va kareta odatda to'xtaydigan mehmonxona ro'parasiga keldim. Bu yerda nega ekanini bilmay to'xtadim; lekin bir necha daqiqa ko'chaning narigi chetidan men tomon kelayotgan karetaga ko'zimni qadab turdim. U yaqinlashganda, bu Shveytsariya pochta aravasi ekanini payqadim; u aynan men turgan joyda to'xtadi va eshik ochilgach, meni ko'rib darhol sakrab tushgan Genri Klervalni ko'rdim. «Aziz Frankenshteyn, — deb xitob qildi u, — seni ko'rganimdan qanchalik xursandman! Men tushayotgan aynan shu lahzada bu yerda bo'lganing qanday omad!»

paras.en: Nothing could equal my delight on seeing Clerval; his presence brought back to my thoughts my father, Elizabeth, and all those scenes of home so dear to my recollection. I grasped his hand, and in a moment forgot my horror and misfortune; I felt suddenly, and for the first time during many months, calm and serene joy. I welcomed my friend, therefore, in the most cordial manner, and we walked towards my college. Clerval continued talking for some time about our mutual friends and his own good fortune in being permitted to come to Ingolstadt. “You may easily believe,” said he, “how great was the difficulty to persuade my father that all necessary knowledge was not comprised in the noble art of book-keeping; and, indeed, I believe I left him incredulous to the last, for his constant answer to my unwearied entreaties was the same as that of the Dutch schoolmaster in The Vicar of Wakefield: ‘I have ten thousand florins a year without Greek, I eat heartily without Greek.’ But his affection for me at length overcame his dislike of learning, and he has permitted me to undertake a voyage of discovery to the land of knowledge.”
paras.uz: Klervalni ko'rgandagi quvonchimga hech narsa teng kela olmasdi; uning borligi xayolimga otamni, Elizabetni va xotiramga shunchalik aziz bo'lgan uyning barcha manzaralarini qaytarib olib keldi. Men uning qo'lini ushladim va bir lahzada dahshatim va baxtsizligimni unutdim; birdan, ko'p oylardan beri birinchi marta, sokin va osoyishta quvonch his qildim. Shuning uchun do'stimni eng samimiy tarzda kutib oldim va biz kollejim tomon yo'l oldik. Klerval bir muddat umumiy do'stlarimiz va Ingolshtadtga kelishiga ruxsat berilgani bilan bog'liq o'z omadi haqida gapirishda davom etdi. «Osongina ishonishing mumkin, — dedi u, — otamni barcha zarur bilimlar buxgalteriyaning olijanob san'atida jamlanmaganiga ishontirish qanchalik qiyin bo'lganiga; aslida, menimcha, men uni oxirigacha ishonmagan holda qoldirdim, chunki uning tinimsiz iltijolarimga doimiy javobi «Ueykfild vikariy»dagi gollandiyalik maktab o'qituvchisining javobi bilan bir xil edi: «Yunon tilisiz ham yiliga o'n ming florinim bor, yunon tilisiz ham to'yib ovqatlanaman.» Lekin menga bo'lgan mehri nihoyat ilmni yoqtirmasligidan ustun keldi va u menga bilim yurtiga kashfiyot safariga chiqishga ruxsat berdi.»

paras.en: “It gives me the greatest delight to see you; but tell me how you left my father, brothers, and Elizabeth.”
paras.uz: «Seni ko'rganimdan juda xursandman; lekin ayt-chi, otamni, ukalarimni va Elizabetni qanday holda qoldirding?»

paras.en: “Very well, and very happy, only a little uneasy that they hear from you so seldom. By the by, I mean to lecture you a little upon their account myself. But, my dear Frankenstein,” continued he, stopping short and gazing full in my face, “I did not before remark how very ill you appear; so thin and pale; you look as if you had been watching for several nights.”
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi va juda baxtli, faqat sendan kamdan-kam xabar olishayotgani uchun biroz bezovta. Aytgancha, men o'zim ham ular nomidan senga biroz nasihat qilmoqchiman. Lekin, aziz Frankenshteyn, — davom etdi u birdan to'xtab, yuzimga tik qarab, — qanchalik kasal ko'rinayotganingni oldin payqamabman; shunchalik ozg'in va rangpar; go'yo bir necha kecha bedor o'tirgandek ko'rinasan.»

paras.en: “You have guessed right; I have lately been so deeply engaged in one occupation that I have not allowed myself sufficient rest, as you see; but I hope, I sincerely hope, that all these employments are now at an end and that I am at length free.”
paras.uz: «To'g'ri topding; yaqinda bitta mashg'ulot bilan shunchalik chuqur band bo'ldimki, ko'rib turganingdek, o'zimga yetarlicha dam olishga yo'l qo'ymadim; lekin umid qilamanki, chin dildan umid qilamanki, bu ishlarning hammasi endi tugadi va nihoyat ozodman.»

paras.en: I trembled excessively; I could not endure to think of, and far less to allude to, the occurrences of the preceding night. I walked with a quick pace, and we soon arrived at my college. I then reflected, and the thought made me shiver, that the creature whom I had left in my apartment might still be there, alive and walking about. I dreaded to behold this monster, but I feared still more that Henry should see him. Entreating him, therefore, to remain a few minutes at the bottom of the stairs, I darted up towards my own room. My hand was already on the lock of the door before I recollected myself. I then paused, and a cold shivering came over me.
paras.uz: Men qattiq titrardim; o'tgan kechaning voqealari haqida o'ylashga, ularga ishora qilish u yoqda tursin, chiday olmasdim. Tez qadamlar bilan yurdim va biz tez orada kollejimga yetib keldik. Shunda o'yladim va bu fikr meni titratib yubordi: xonamda qoldirib ketgan maxluq hali ham u yerda, tirik holda yurgan bo'lishi mumkin. Men bu yirtqichni ko'rishdan qo'rqardim, lekin Genri uni ko'rib qolishidan undan ham ko'proq qo'rqardim. Shuning uchun undan bir necha daqiqa zinaning pastida kutib turishini iltimos qilib, o'z xonamga otilib chiqdim. Esimni yig'ib olgunimcha qo'lim allaqachon eshik qulfida edi. Keyin to'xtadim va meni sovuq titroq bosdi.

paras.en: I threw the door forcibly open, as children are accustomed to do when they expect a spectre to stand in waiting for them on the other side; but nothing appeared. I stepped fearfully in: the apartment was empty, and my bedroom was also freed from its hideous guest. I could hardly believe that so great a good fortune could have befallen me, but when I became assured that my enemy had indeed fled, I clapped my hands for joy and ran down to Clerval.
paras.uz: Men eshikni, bolalar narigi tomonda arvoh kutib turgan deb kutganlarida qilganlaridek, kuch bilan lang ochdim; lekin hech narsa ko'rinmadi. Qo'rqa-pisa ichkariga qadam qo'ydim: xona bo'sh edi, yotoqxonam ham xunuk mehmonidan xoli edi. Boshimga shunchalik katta omad tushganiga zo'rg'a ishonardim, lekin dushmanim haqiqatan ham qochib ketganiga ishonch hosil qilgach, quvonchdan qarsak chalib, Klerval oldiga yugurib tushdim.

paras.en: We ascended into my room, and the servant presently brought breakfast; but I was unable to contain myself. It was not joy only that possessed me; I felt my flesh tingle with excess of sensitiveness, and my pulse beat rapidly. I was unable to remain for a single instant in the same place; I jumped over the chairs, clapped my hands, and laughed aloud. Clerval at first attributed my unusual spirits to joy on his arrival, but when he observed me more attentively, he saw a wildness in my eyes for which he could not account, and my loud, unrestrained, heartless laughter frightened and astonished him.
paras.uz: Biz xonamga chiqdik va ko'p o'tmay xizmatkor nonushta olib keldi; lekin men o'zimni tuta olmadim. Meni faqat quvonch qamrab olmagan edi; haddan tashqari ta'sirchanlikdan badanim jimirlayotganini, tomirim tez urayotganini his qilardim. Bir lahza ham bir joyda tura olmasdim; kursilar ustidan sakrardim, qarsak chalardim va baland ovozda kulardim. Klerval dastlab g'ayrioddiy kayfiyatimni uning kelganidan quvonish deb bildi, lekin menga diqqat bilan qaraganda, ko'zlarimda u tushuntira olmaydigan yovvoyilikni ko'rdi va mening baland, jilovsiz, yuraksiz kulgim uni qo'rqitib, hayratga soldi.

paras.en: “My dear Victor,” cried he, “what, for God’s sake, is the matter? Do not laugh in that manner. How ill you are! What is the cause of all this?”
paras.uz: «Aziz Viktor, — deb qichqirdi u, — Xudo haqqi, senga nima bo'ldi? Bunday kulma. Qanchalik kasalsan! Bularning hammasining sababi nima?»

paras.en: “Do not ask me,” cried I, putting my hands before my eyes, for I thought I saw the dreaded spectre glide into the room; “he can tell. Oh, save me! Save me!” I imagined that the monster seized me; I struggled furiously and fell down in a fit.
paras.uz: «Mendan so'rama, — deb qichqirdim qo'llarimni ko'zlarimga qo'yib, chunki o'sha qo'rqinchli arvoh xonaga sirg'alib kirganini ko'rgandek bo'ldim, — u aytib bera oladi. Oh, meni qutqar! Qutqar!» Yirtqich meni ushlab olgandek tasavvur qildim; g'azab bilan olishdim va tutqanoq tutib yiqildim.

paras.en: Poor Clerval! What must have been his feelings? A meeting, which he anticipated with such joy, so strangely turned to bitterness. But I was not the witness of his grief, for I was lifeless and did not recover my senses for a long, long time.
paras.uz: Bechora Klerval! Uning his-tuyg'ulari qanday bo'lgan ekan? U shunchalik quvonch bilan kutgan uchrashuv g'alati tarzda achchiqqa aylandi. Lekin men uning qayg'usiga guvoh bo'lmadim, chunki jonsiz edim va uzoq, uzoq vaqt hushimga kelmadim.

paras.en: This was the commencement of a nervous fever which confined me for several months. During all that time Henry was my only nurse. I afterwards learned that, knowing my father’s advanced age and unfitness for so long a journey, and how wretched my sickness would make Elizabeth, he spared them this grief by concealing the extent of my disorder. He knew that I could not have a more kind and attentive nurse than himself; and, firm in the hope he felt of my recovery, he did not doubt that, instead of doing harm, he performed the kindest action that he could towards them.
paras.uz: Bu meni bir necha oy to'shakka mixlab qo'ygan asab isitmasining boshlanishi edi. Butun shu vaqt davomida Genri mening yagona hamshiram bo'ldi. Keyinroq bildimki, u otamning keksa yoshini va bunday uzoq safarga yaroqsizligini, kasalligim Elizabetni qanchalik baxtsiz qilishini bilib, xastaligimning darajasini yashirib, ularni bu qayg'udan asragan ekan. U o'zidan ko'ra mehribonroq va e'tiborliroq hamshiram bo'lmasligini bilardi; va tuzalishimga bo'lgan umidida qat'iy bo'lib, zarar yetkazish o'rniga ularga nisbatan qo'lidan kelgan eng mehribon ishni qilayotganiga shubha qilmadi.

paras.en: But I was in reality very ill, and surely nothing but the unbounded and unremitting attentions of my friend could have restored me to life. The form of the monster on whom I had bestowed existence was for ever before my eyes, and I raved incessantly concerning him. Doubtless my words surprised Henry; he at first believed them to be the wanderings of my disturbed imagination, but the pertinacity with which I continually recurred to the same subject persuaded him that my disorder indeed owed its origin to some uncommon and terrible event.
paras.uz: Lekin aslida men juda kasal edim va, shubhasiz, do'stimning cheksiz va tinimsiz g'amxo'rligidan boshqa hech narsa meni hayotga qaytara olmasdi. Men borliq ato etgan yirtqichning qiyofasi abadiy ko'z oldimda edi va men u haqda tinimsiz alahsirardim. Shubhasiz, so'zlarim Genrini hayratga solardi; u dastlab ularni bezovta tasavvurimning adashuvlari deb o'yladi, lekin doimo bir xil mavzuga qaytishimdagi qat'iylik uni kasalligim haqiqatan ham qandaydir g'ayrioddiy va dahshatli voqeadan kelib chiqqaniga ishontirdi.

paras.en: By very slow degrees, and with frequent relapses that alarmed and grieved my friend, I recovered. I remember the first time I became capable of observing outward objects with any kind of pleasure, I perceived that the fallen leaves had disappeared and that the young buds were shooting forth from the trees that shaded my window. It was a divine spring, and the season contributed greatly to my convalescence. I felt also sentiments of joy and affection revive in my bosom; my gloom disappeared, and in a short time I became as cheerful as before I was attacked by the fatal passion.
paras.uz: Juda sekin-asta, do'stimni xavotirga solgan va qayg'uga botirgan tez-tez qaytalanishlar bilan tuzaldim. Eslayman, tashqi narsalarni qandaydir zavq bilan kuzatishga birinchi marta qodir bo'lganimda, to'kilgan barglar yo'qolganini va derazamga soya solib turgan daraxtlardan yosh kurtaklar o'sib chiqayotganini payqadim. Ilohiy bahor edi va fasl tuzalishimga katta hissa qo'shdi. Ko'kragimda quvonch va mehr tuyg'ulari ham qayta jonlanganini his qildim; g'amginligim yo'qoldi va qisqa vaqt ichida halokatli ehtirosga chalinishimdan oldingidek quvnoq bo'ldim.

paras.en: “Dearest Clerval,” exclaimed I, “how kind, how very good you are to me. This whole winter, instead of being spent in study, as you promised yourself, has been consumed in my sick room. How shall I ever repay you? I feel the greatest remorse for the disappointment of which I have been the occasion, but you will forgive me.”
paras.uz: «Eng aziz Klerval, — deb xitob qildim, — menga qanchalik mehribon, qanchalik yaxshisan. Bu butun qish o'zingga va'da qilganingdek o'qishga sarflanish o'rniga mening bemorxonamda o'tib ketdi. Senga qanday qilib qarzimni uzaman? Sabab bo'lgan umidsizligingdan qattiq pushaymonman, lekin meni kechirasan.»

paras.en: “You will repay me entirely if you do not discompose yourself, but get well as fast as you can; and since you appear in such good spirits, I may speak to you on one subject, may I not?”
paras.uz: «Agar o'zingni bezovta qilmasang va iloji boricha tez tuzalsang, qarzingni to'liq uzgan bo'lasan; kayfiyating shunchalik yaxshi ko'rinayotgan ekan, sen bilan bitta mavzuda gaplashsam bo'ladimi, a?»

paras.en: I trembled. One subject! What could it be? Could he allude to an object on whom I dared not even think?
paras.uz: Men titrab ketdim. Bitta mavzu! U nima bo'lishi mumkin? U men hatto o'ylashga ham jur'at etmaydigan mavjudotga ishora qilayotgan bo'lishi mumkinmi?

paras.en: “Compose yourself,” said Clerval, who observed my change of colour, “I will not mention it if it agitates you; but your father and cousin would be very happy if they received a letter from you in your own handwriting. They hardly know how ill you have been and are uneasy at your long silence.”
paras.uz: «O'zingni bos, — dedi rangim o'zgarganini payqagan Klerval, — agar seni hayajonga solsa, tilga olmayman; lekin agar otang va amakivachchang sendan o'z qo'ling bilan yozilgan maktub olsalar, juda xursand bo'lishardi. Ular qanchalik kasal bo'lganingni deyarli bilishmaydi va uzoq jimliging uchun bezovta.»

paras.en: “Is that all, my dear Henry? How could you suppose that my first thought would not fly towards those dear, dear friends whom I love and who are so deserving of my love?”
paras.uz: «Hammasi shumi, aziz Genri? Birinchi fikrim men sevgan va muhabbatimga shunchalik loyiq bo'lgan o'sha aziz, aziz do'stlarim tomon uchmaydi deb qanday o'ylay olding?»

paras.en: “If this is your present temper, my friend, you will perhaps be glad to see a letter that has been lying here some days for you; it is from your cousin, I believe.”
paras.uz: «Agar hozirgi kayfiyating shunday bo'lsa, do'stim, bu yerda bir necha kundan beri seni kutib yotgan maktubni ko'rishdan xursand bo'larsan; menimcha, u amakivachchangdan.»

paras.en: Clerval then put the following letter into my hands. It was from my own Elizabeth:
paras.uz: Shunda Klerval qo'limga quyidagi maktubni berdi. U mening Elizabetimdan edi:

paras.en: “My dearest Cousin,
paras.uz: «Eng aziz amakivachcham,

paras.en: “You have been ill, very ill, and even the constant letters of dear kind Henry are not sufficient to reassure me on your account. You are forbidden to write—to hold a pen; yet one word from you, dear Victor, is necessary to calm our apprehensions. For a long time I have thought that each post would bring this line, and my persuasions have restrained my uncle from undertaking a journey to Ingolstadt. I have prevented his encountering the inconveniences and perhaps dangers of so long a journey, yet how often have I regretted not being able to perform it myself! I figure to myself that the task of attending on your sickbed has devolved on some mercenary old nurse, who could never guess your wishes nor minister to them with the care and affection of your poor cousin. Yet that is over now: Clerval writes that indeed you are getting better. I eagerly hope that you will confirm this intelligence soon in your own handwriting.
paras.uz: Sen kasal bo'lding, juda kasal bo'lding va hatto aziz, mehribon Genrining doimiy maktublari ham sen haqingda meni tinchlantirishga yetmaydi. Senga yozish — qalam ushlash taqiqlangan; lekin sendan bir og'iz so'z, aziz Viktor, xavotirlarimizni bosish uchun zarur. Uzoq vaqtdan beri har bir pochta shu satrni olib keladi deb o'ylab keldim va ko'ndirishlarim amakimni Ingolshtadtga safar qilishdan to'xtatib qoldi. Men uni bunday uzoq safarning noqulayliklari va balki xavflariga duch kelishdan saqlab qoldim, lekin uni o'zim amalga oshira olmaganimdan qanchalik tez-tez afsuslandim! Tasavvur qilaman, bemor to'shagingga qarash vazifasi qandaydir yollanma keksa enagaga tushgandir, u hech qachon istaklaringni seza olmaydi va bechora amakivachchangning g'amxo'rligi va mehri bilan ularni bajara olmaydi. Lekin endi bu o'tdi: Klerval haqiqatan ham tuzalayotganingni yozyapti. Bu xabarni tez orada o'z qo'ling bilan tasdiqlashingni intiqib kutaman.

paras.en: “Get well—and return to us. You will find a happy, cheerful home and friends who love you dearly. Your father’s health is vigorous, and he asks but to see you, but to be assured that you are well; and not a care will ever cloud his benevolent countenance. How pleased you would be to remark the improvement of our Ernest! He is now sixteen and full of activity and spirit. He is desirous to be a true Swiss and to enter into foreign service, but we cannot part with him, at least until his elder brother returns to us. My uncle is not pleased with the idea of a military career in a distant country, but Ernest never had your powers of application. He looks upon study as an odious fetter; his time is spent in the open air, climbing the hills or rowing on the lake. I fear that he will become an idler unless we yield the point and permit him to enter on the profession which he has selected.
paras.uz: Tuzal — va bizga qayt. Sen baxtli, quvnoq uyni va seni chin dildan sevadigan do'stlarni topasan. Otangning sog'lig'i baquvvat va u faqat seni ko'rishni, sog' ekaningga ishonch hosil qilishni so'raydi; shunda hech qanday tashvish uning mehribon chehrasini bulutlamaydi. Ernestimizning qanchalik o'sganini ko'rib, qanchalik xursand bo'larding! U endi o'n olti yoshda, faollik va g'ayratga to'la. U haqiqiy shveytsariyalik bo'lib, chet el xizmatiga kirishni istaydi, lekin biz u bilan ajrala olmaymiz, hech bo'lmasa akasi bizga qaytguncha. Amakim uzoq mamlakatdagi harbiy martaba g'oyasidan mamnun emas, lekin Ernestda hech qachon sening tirishqoqlik qobiliyating bo'lmagan. U o'qishga jirkanch kishan deb qaraydi; vaqti ochiq havoda, tepaliklarga chiqib yoki ko'lda qayiqda eshkak eshib o'tadi. Qo'rqamanki, agar biz yon berib, u tanlagan kasbga kirishiga ruxsat bermasak, u bekorchiga aylanadi.

paras.en: “Little alteration, except the growth of our dear children, has taken place since you left us. The blue lake and snow-clad mountains—they never change; and I think our placid home and our contented hearts are regulated by the same immutable laws. My trifling occupations take up my time and amuse me, and I am rewarded for any exertions by seeing none but happy, kind faces around me. Since you left us, but one change has taken place in our little household. Do you remember on what occasion Justine Moritz entered our family? Probably you do not; I will relate her history, therefore in a few words. Madame Moritz, her mother, was a widow with four children, of whom Justine was the third.
paras.uz: Sen bizdan ketganingdan beri aziz bolalarimizning o'sishidan boshqa deyarli o'zgarish bo'lmadi. Moviy ko'l va qorli tog'lar — ular hech qachon o'zgarmaydi; menimcha, osoyishta uyimiz va mamnun yuraklarimiz ham xuddi shu o'zgarmas qonunlar bilan boshqariladi. Arzimas mashg'ulotlarim vaqtimni oladi va ko'nglimni ochadi va har qanday harakatim uchun atrofimda faqat baxtli, mehribon chehralarni ko'rish bilan mukofotlanaman. Sen ketganingdan beri kichik xonadonimizda faqat bitta o'zgarish bo'ldi. Jastin Morits oilamizga qanday holatda kirganini eslaysanmi? Ehtimol, eslamassan; shuning uchun uning tarixini bir necha so'z bilan aytib beraman. Uning onasi Morits xonim to'rt farzandli beva edi, Jastin ulardan uchinchisi edi.

paras.en: This girl had always been the favourite of her father, but through a strange perversity, her mother could not endure her, and after the death of M. Moritz, treated her very ill. My aunt observed this, and when Justine was twelve years of age, prevailed on her mother to allow her to live at our house. The republican institutions of our country have produced simpler and happier manners than those which prevail in the great monarchies that surround it. Hence there is less distinction between the several classes of its inhabitants; and the lower orders, being neither so poor nor so despised, their manners are more refined and moral. A servant in Geneva does not mean the same thing as a servant in France and England. Justine, thus received in our family, learned the duties of a servant, a condition which, in our fortunate country, does not include the idea of ignorance and a sacrifice of the dignity of a human being.
paras.uz: Bu qiz doim otasining erkatoyi bo'lgan, lekin qandaydir g'alati injiqlik tufayli onasi unga toqat qila olmasdi va janob Morits vafotidan keyin unga juda yomon muomala qildi. Xolam buni payqadi va Jastin o'n ikki yoshga to'lganda, onasini uning bizning uyimizda yashashiga ruxsat berishga ko'ndirdi. Mamlakatimizning respublika muassasalari uni o'rab turgan buyuk monarxiyalarda hukm surganlardan ko'ra soddaroq va baxtliroq urf-odatlarni vujudga keltirgan. Shuning uchun aholining turli tabaqalari o'rtasida farq kamroq; quyi tabaqalar esa unchalik kambag'al ham, unchalik nafratlangan ham bo'lmagani uchun, ularning odob-axloqi nafisroq va axloqliroq. Jenevadagi xizmatkor Fransiya va Angliyadagi xizmatkor bilan bir xil ma'noni anglatmaydi. Shu tarzda oilamizga qabul qilingan Jastin xizmatkorning burchlarini o'rgandi — bu holat bizning baxtli mamlakatimizda nodonlik va inson qadr-qimmatini qurbon qilish g'oyasini o'z ichiga olmaydi.

paras.en: “Justine, you may remember, was a great favourite of yours; and I recollect you once remarked that if you were in an ill humour, one glance from Justine could dissipate it, for the same reason that Ariosto gives concerning the beauty of Angelica—she looked so frank-hearted and happy. My aunt conceived a great attachment for her, by which she was induced to give her an education superior to that which she had at first intended. This benefit was fully repaid; Justine was the most grateful little creature in the world: I do not mean that she made any professions I never heard one pass her lips, but you could see by her eyes that she almost adored her protectress. Although her disposition was gay and in many respects inconsiderate, yet she paid the greatest attention to every gesture of my aunt. She thought her the model of all excellence and endeavoured to imitate her phraseology and manners, so that even now she often reminds me of her.
paras.uz: Jastin, eslasang kerak, sening katta erkatoying edi; eslayman, bir marta sen agar kayfiyating yomon bo'lsa, Jastinning bir nigohi uni tarqatib yuborishi mumkinligini aytgan eding — Ariosto Anjelikaning go'zalligi haqida keltirgan sabab bilan — u shunchalik ochiqko'ngil va baxtli ko'rinardi. Xolam unga katta mehr qo'ydi va shu tufayli unga dastlab niyat qilganidan ko'ra yuqoriroq ta'lim berishga undaldi. Bu yaxshilik to'liq qaytarildi; Jastin dunyodagi eng minnatdor kichkina jonzot edi: u qandaydir izhor qilardi demoqchi emasman — uning labidan birorta ham bunday so'z chiqqanini eshitmaganman — lekin ko'zlaridan uning o'z homiyasiga deyarli sig'inishini ko'rish mumkin edi. Fe'li quvnoq va ko'p jihatdan o'ylamasdan ish qiladigan bo'lsa ham, u xolamning har bir imo-ishorasiga eng katta e'tibor berardi. U uni barcha fazilatlarning namunasi deb bilardi va uning so'z boyligi va muomalasiga taqlid qilishga harakat qilardi, shuning uchun hatto hozir ham u menga ko'pincha xolamni eslatadi.

paras.en: “When my dearest aunt died every one was too much occupied in their own grief to notice poor Justine, who had attended her during her illness with the most anxious affection. Poor Justine was very ill; but other trials were reserved for her.
paras.uz: Eng aziz xolam vafot etganda, hamma o'z qayg'usi bilan shunchalik band ediki, uning kasalligi davomida eng xavotirli mehr bilan unga qaragan bechora Jastinni hech kim payqamadi. Bechora Jastin juda kasal bo'ldi; lekin uni boshqa sinovlar kutib turardi.

paras.en: “One by one, her brothers and sister died; and her mother, with the exception of her neglected daughter, was left childless. The conscience of the woman was troubled; she began to think that the deaths of her favourites was a judgement from heaven to chastise her partiality. She was a Roman Catholic; and I believe her confessor confirmed the idea which she had conceived. Accordingly, a few months after your departure for Ingolstadt, Justine was called home by her repentant mother. Poor girl! She wept when she quitted our house; she was much altered since the death of my aunt; grief had given softness and a winning mildness to her manners, which had before been remarkable for vivacity. Nor was her residence at her mother’s house of a nature to restore her gaiety. The poor woman was very vacillating in her repentance.
paras.uz: Birin-ketin uning akalari va singlisi vafot etdi; onasi esa e'tibordan chetda qolgan qizidan tashqari farzandsiz qoldi. Ayolning vijdoni bezovtalandi; u sevimlilarining o'limi uning tarafkashligini jazolash uchun osmondan kelgan hukm deb o'ylay boshladi. U Rim katoligi edi; va menimcha, tavba tinglovchisi uning bu fikrini tasdiqladi. Shunga ko'ra, sen Ingolshtadtga ketganingdan bir necha oy o'tib, pushaymon onasi Jastinni uyga chaqirib oldi. Bechora qiz! U uyimizni tark etayotganda yig'ladi; xolam vafotidan keyin u ancha o'zgargan edi; qayg'u ilgari jonliligi bilan ajralib turgan muomalasiga yumshoqlik va maftunkor muloyimlik bergan edi. Onasining uyida yashashi ham uning quvnoqligini tiklaydigan xususiyatda emas edi. Bechora ayol pushaymonligida juda o'zgaruvchan edi.

paras.en: She sometimes begged Justine to forgive her unkindness, but much oftener accused her of having caused the deaths of her brothers and sister. Perpetual fretting at length threw Madame Moritz into a decline, which at first increased her irritability, but she is now at peace for ever. She died on the first approach of cold weather, at the beginning of this last winter. Justine has just returned to us; and I assure you I love her tenderly. She is very clever and gentle, and extremely pretty; as I mentioned before, her mien and her expression continually remind me of my dear aunt.
paras.uz: U ba'zan Jastindan qilgan noxushliklari uchun kechirim so'rardi, lekin ancha tez-tez uni akalari va singlisining o'limiga sababchi bo'lganlikda ayblardi. Doimiy xafagarchilik oxir-oqibat Morits xonimni so'lishga olib keldi, bu dastlab uning jizzakiligini kuchaytirdi, lekin endi u abadiy tinchlikda. U sovuq havo endi boshlanganda, o'tgan qishning boshida vafot etdi. Jastin endigina bizga qaytdi; ishontirib aytamanki, men uni nozik sevaman. U juda aqlli va muloyim, nihoyatda chiroyli; oldin aytganimdek, uning qiyofasi va ifodasi menga doimo aziz xolamni eslatadi.

paras.en: “I must say also a few words to you, my dear cousin, of little darling William. I wish you could see him; he is very tall of his age, with sweet laughing blue eyes, dark eyelashes, and curling hair. When he smiles, two little dimples appear on each cheek, which are rosy with health. He has already had one or two little wives, but Louisa Biron is his favourite, a pretty little girl of five years of age.
paras.uz: Aziz amakivachcham, senga kichkina jonajon Uilyam haqida ham bir necha so'z aytishim kerak. Qaniydi uni ko'rsang; u yoshiga nisbatan juda baland bo'yli, shirin kulib turadigan moviy ko'zlari, qora kipriklari va jingalak sochlari bor. U jilmayganda, sog'lomlikdan qizarib turgan har bir yonog'ida ikkitadan kichkina chuqurcha paydo bo'ladi. Uning allaqachon bir-ikkita kichkina «xotini» bo'lgan, lekin besh yoshli chiroyli qizcha Luiza Biron uning sevimlisi.

paras.en: “Now, dear Victor, I dare say you wish to be indulged in a little gossip concerning the good people of Geneva. The pretty Miss Mansfield has already received the congratulatory visits on her approaching marriage with a young Englishman, John Melbourne, Esq. Her ugly sister, Manon, married M. Duvillard, the rich banker, last autumn. Your favourite schoolfellow, Louis Manoir, has suffered several misfortunes since the departure of Clerval from Geneva. But he has already recovered his spirits, and is reported to be on the point of marrying a lively pretty Frenchwoman, Madame Tavernier. She is a widow, and much older than Manoir; but she is very much admired, and a favourite with everybody.
paras.uz: Endi, aziz Viktor, Jenevaning yaxshi odamlari haqida biroz g'iybatdan bahramand bo'lishni istasang kerak. Chiroyli miss Mansfild yosh ingliz janob Jon Melburn bilan yaqinlashib kelayotgan to'yi munosabati bilan allaqachon tabrik tashriflarini qabul qildi. Uning xunuk singlisi Manon o'tgan kuzda boy bankir janob Duvilyarga turmushga chiqdi. Sening sevimli maktabdoshing Lui Manuar Klerval Jenevadan ketganidan beri bir nechta baxtsizlikni boshdan kechirdi. Lekin u allaqachon ruhini tiklab oldi va aytishlaricha, jonli, chiroyli fransuz ayoli Tavernye xonimga uylanish arafasida ekan. U beva va Manuardan ancha katta; lekin unga hamma qoyil qoladi va hammaning erkatoyi.

paras.en: “I have written myself into better spirits, dear cousin; but my anxiety returns upon me as I conclude. Write, dearest Victor,—one line—one word will be a blessing to us. Ten thousand thanks to Henry for his kindness, his affection, and his many letters; we are sincerely grateful. Adieu! my cousin; take care of yourself; and, I entreat you, write!
paras.uz: Yozib-yozib kayfiyatim ko'tarildi, aziz amakivachcham; lekin tugatarkanman, xavotirim qaytib keladi. Yoz, eng aziz Viktor, — bir satr — bir so'z biz uchun baraka bo'ladi. Genriga mehribonligi, mehri va ko'p maktublari uchun o'n ming rahmat; biz chin dildan minnatdormiz. Xayr! amakivachcham; o'zingni ehtiyot qil; va, yolvoraman, yoz!

paras.en: “Elizabeth Lavenza.
paras.uz: Elizabet Lavenza.

paras.en: “Geneva, March 18th, 17—.”
paras.uz: Jeneva, 18-mart, 17—.»

paras.en: “Dear, dear Elizabeth!” I exclaimed, when I had read her letter: “I will write instantly and relieve them from the anxiety they must feel.” I wrote, and this exertion greatly fatigued me; but my convalescence had commenced, and proceeded regularly. In another fortnight I was able to leave my chamber.
paras.uz: «Aziz, aziz Elizabet! — deb xitob qildim uning maktubini o'qib bo'lgach. — Darhol yozaman va ularni his qilayotgan xavotirdan xalos qilaman.» Men yozdim va bu harakat meni juda charchatdi; lekin tuzalishim boshlangan edi va muntazam davom etdi. Yana ikki haftadan keyin xonamdan chiqa oladigan bo'ldim.

paras.en: One of my first duties on my recovery was to introduce Clerval to the several professors of the university. In doing this, I underwent a kind of rough usage, ill befitting the wounds that my mind had sustained. Ever since the fatal night, the end of my labours, and the beginning of my misfortunes, I had conceived a violent antipathy even to the name of natural philosophy. When I was otherwise quite restored to health, the sight of a chemical instrument would renew all the agony of my nervous symptoms. Henry saw this, and had removed all my apparatus from my view. He had also changed my apartment; for he perceived that I had acquired a dislike for the room which had previously been my laboratory. But these cares of Clerval were made of no avail when I visited the professors.
paras.uz: Tuzalgach, birinchi burchlarimdan biri Klervalni universitetning bir nechta professorlari bilan tanishtirish edi. Buni qilishda men aqlim olgan yaralarga sira mos kelmaydigan qo'pol muomalaga duch keldim. O'sha halokatli tundan — mehnatlarimning oxiri va baxtsizliklarimning boshlanishidan beri men hatto tabiat falsafasi nomiga ham kuchli nafrat paydo qilgan edim. Boshqa jihatdan sog'lig'im butunlay tiklangan bo'lsa ham, kimyoviy asbobni ko'rish asab alomatlarimning butun azobini yangilardi. Genri buni ko'rdi va barcha asboblarimni ko'zimdan olib tashlagan edi. U xonamni ham almashtirgan edi; chunki ilgari laboratoriyam bo'lgan xonani yomon ko'rib qolganimni payqagan edi. Lekin men professorlarga borganimda Klervalning bu g'amxo'rliklari befoyda bo'ldi.

paras.en: M. Waldman inflicted torture when he praised, with kindness and warmth, the astonishing progress I had made in the sciences. He soon perceived that I disliked the subject; but not guessing the real cause, he attributed my feelings to modesty, and changed the subject from my improvement, to the science itself, with a desire, as I evidently saw, of drawing me out. What could I do? He meant to please, and he tormented me. I felt as if he had placed carefully, one by one, in my view those instruments which were to be afterwards used in putting me to a slow and cruel death. I writhed under his words, yet dared not exhibit the pain I felt. Clerval, whose eyes and feelings were always quick in discerning the sensations of others, declined the subject, alleging, in excuse, his total ignorance; and the conversation took a more general turn.
paras.uz: Janob Valdman fanlarda erishgan hayratlanarli yutuqlarimni mehribonlik va iliqlik bilan maqtab, menga azob berdi. U tez orada bu mavzuni yoqtirmasligimni payqadi; lekin haqiqiy sababni taxmin qilmay, his-tuyg'ularimni kamtarlikka nisbat berdi va, aniq ko'rganimdek, meni gapga solish istagi bilan mavzuni mening yutuqlarimdan fanning o'ziga o'zgartirdi. Nima qila olardim? U xursand qilmoqchi edi, lekin meni qiynardi. Go'yo u keyinchalik meni sekin va shafqatsiz o'limga mahkum etishda ishlatiladigan asboblarni birma-bir ehtiyotkorlik bilan ko'z oldimga qo'yayotgandek his qildim. Uning so'zlari ostida to'lg'anardim, lekin his qilayotgan og'riqni ko'rsatishga jur'at etmasdim. Ko'zlari va his-tuyg'ulari boshqalarning holatini sezishda doimo tez bo'lgan Klerval o'zining butunlay nodonligini bahona qilib, mavzudan voz kechdi va suhbat umumiyroq tus oldi.

paras.en: I thanked my friend from my heart, but I did not speak. I saw plainly that he was surprised, but he never attempted to draw my secret from me; and although I loved him with a mixture of affection and reverence that knew no bounds, yet I could never persuade myself to confide in him that event which was so often present to my recollection, but which I feared the detail to another would only impress more deeply.
paras.uz: Men do'stimga chin yurakdan minnatdorchilik bildirdim, lekin gapirmadim. Uning hayron bo'lganini aniq ko'rdim, lekin u hech qachon sirimni mendan sug'urib olishga urinmadi; va men uni chegara bilmas mehr va ehtirom aralash sevgan bo'lsam ham, xotiramda shunchalik tez-tez paydo bo'ladigan, lekin boshqaga batafsil aytsam, faqat chuqurroq o'rnashib qolishidan qo'rqqan o'sha voqeani unga ishonishga hech qachon o'zimni ko'ndira olmadim.

paras.en: M. Krempe was not equally docile; and in my condition at that time, of almost insupportable sensitiveness, his harsh blunt encomiums gave me even more pain than the benevolent approbation of M. Waldman. “D—n the fellow!” cried he; “why, M. Clerval, I assure you he has outstript us all. Ay, stare if you please; but it is nevertheless true. A youngster who, but a few years ago, believed in Cornelius Agrippa as firmly as in the gospel, has now set himself at the head of the university; and if he is not soon pulled down, we shall all be out of countenance.—Ay, ay,” continued he, observing my face expressive of suffering, “M. Frankenstein is modest; an excellent quality in a young man. Young men should be diffident of themselves, you know, M. Clerval: I was myself when young; but that wears out in a very short time.”
paras.uz: Janob Krempe unchalik yuvosh emas edi; va o'sha paytdagi deyarli chidab bo'lmas ta'sirchanlik holatimda uning qo'pol, to'mtoq maqtovlari menga janob Valdmanning xayrixoh ma'qullashidan ham ko'proq og'riq berdi. «La'nati yigit! — deb qichqirdi u. — Ha, janob Klerval, ishontirib aytaman, u hammamizdan o'zib ketdi. Ha, xohlasangiz, ko'zingizni chaqchaytiring; lekin baribir bu haqiqat. Bir necha yil oldin Korneliy Agrippaga Injilga ishongandek qattiq ishongan yigitcha endi universitetning boshiga chiqib oldi; va agar tez orada uni pastga tushirmasak, hammamiz uyatga qolamiz. — Ha, ha, — davom etdi u, yuzimdagi azob ifodasini payqab, — janob Frankenshteyn kamtar; yigit uchun a'lo fazilat. Yigitlar o'zlariga ishonchsiz bo'lishi kerak, bilasiz, janob Klerval: men ham yoshligimda shunday edim; lekin bu juda qisqa vaqtda o'tib ketadi.»

paras.en: M. Krempe had now commenced an eulogy on himself, which happily turned the conversation from a subject that was so annoying to me.
paras.uz: Endi janob Krempe o'zini maqtay boshladi, bu esa baxtimga suhbatni men uchun shunchalik noxush bo'lgan mavzudan burib yubordi.

paras.en: Clerval had never sympathised in my tastes for natural science; and his literary pursuits differed wholly from those which had occupied me. He came to the university with the design of making himself complete master of the oriental languages, and thus he should open a field for the plan of life he had marked out for himself. Resolved to pursue no inglorious career, he turned his eyes toward the East, as affording scope for his spirit of enterprise. The Persian, Arabic, and Sanskrit languages engaged his attention, and I was easily induced to enter on the same studies. Idleness had ever been irksome to me, and now that I wished to fly from reflection, and hated my former studies, I felt great relief in being the fellow-pupil with my friend, and found not only instruction but consolation in the works of the orientalists.
paras.uz: Klerval tabiatshunoslikka bo'lgan didimga hech qachon hamdard bo'lmagan; uning adabiy mashg'ulotlari meni band qilganlardan butunlay farq qilardi. U universitetga sharq tillarini to'liq egallash va shu bilan o'zi uchun belgilagan hayot rejasiga yo'l ochish niyatida kelgan edi. Sharafsiz martaba bilan shug'ullanmaslikka qaror qilib, u tashabbuskor ruhiga imkoniyat beradigan joy sifatida nigohini Sharqqa qaratdi. Fors, arab va sanskrit tillari uning diqqatini band qildi va meni ham xuddi shu mashg'ulotlarga kirishishga osongina ko'ndirdi. Bekorchilik doim men uchun malol kelardi, va endi mulohazadan qochmoqchi bo'lib, avvalgi mashg'ulotlarimdan nafratlanganimda, do'stim bilan birga o'qishdan katta yengillik his qildim va sharqshunoslarning asarlarida nafaqat ilm, balki tasalli ham topdim.

paras.en: I did not, like him, attempt a critical knowledge of their dialects, for I did not contemplate making any other use of them than temporary amusement. I read merely to understand their meaning, and they well repaid my labours. Their melancholy is soothing, and their joy elevating, to a degree I never experienced in studying the authors of any other country. When you read their writings, life appears to consist in a warm sun and a garden of roses,—in the smiles and frowns of a fair enemy, and the fire that consumes your own heart. How different from the manly and heroical poetry of Greece and Rome!
paras.uz: Men u kabi ularning shevalarini tanqidiy bilishga urinmadim, chunki ulardan vaqtinchalik ko'ngilxushlikdan boshqa maqsadda foydalanishni o'ylamasdim. Men faqat ma'nosini tushunish uchun o'qirdim va ular mehnatimni yaxshi qaytarishdi. Ularning g'amginligi taskin beradi, quvonchi esa ruhlantiradi — boshqa biror mamlakat mualliflarini o'rganganimda hech qachon boshdan kechirmagan darajada. Ularning asarlarini o'qiganingizda hayot iliq quyosh va atirgul bog'idan — go'zal dushmanning tabassumlari va qovoq solishlaridan va o'z yuragingizni yondiradigan olovdan iboratdek tuyuladi. Yunoniston va Rimning mardona va qahramonona she'riyatidan qanchalik farq qiladi!

paras.en: Summer passed away in these occupations, and my return to Geneva was fixed for the latter end of autumn; but being delayed by several accidents, winter and snow arrived, the roads were deemed impassable, and my journey was retarded until the ensuing spring. I felt this delay very bitterly; for I longed to see my native town and my beloved friends. My return had only been delayed so long, from an unwillingness to leave Clerval in a strange place, before he had become acquainted with any of its inhabitants. The winter, however, was spent cheerfully; and although the spring was uncommonly late, when it came its beauty compensated for its dilatoriness.
paras.uz: Yoz shu mashg'ulotlarda o'tib ketdi va Jenevaga qaytishim kuzning oxiriga belgilandi; lekin bir nechta tasodif tufayli kechikib, qish va qor keldi, yo'llar o'tib bo'lmas deb topildi va safarim keyingi bahorgacha kechiktirildi. Bu kechikishni juda achchiq his qildim; chunki ona shahrimni va sevimli do'stlarimni ko'rishni orzu qilardim. Qaytishim shunchalik kechikkanining yagona sababi Klervalni u yerning birorta aholisi bilan tanishmasidan oldin begona joyda qoldirishni istamaganim edi. Biroq qish quvnoq o'tdi; va bahor g'ayrioddiy kech kelgan bo'lsa ham, kelganda uning go'zalligi sustkashligining o'rnini qopladi.

paras.en: The month of May had already commenced, and I expected the letter daily which was to fix the date of my departure, when Henry proposed a pedestrian tour in the environs of Ingolstadt, that I might bid a personal farewell to the country I had so long inhabited. I acceded with pleasure to this proposition: I was fond of exercise, and Clerval had always been my favourite companion in the ramble of this nature that I had taken among the scenes of my native country.
paras.uz: May oyi allaqachon boshlangan edi va men har kuni jo'nash sanamni belgilaydigan maktubni kutayotgan edim, shunda Genri men shuncha vaqt yashagan yurt bilan shaxsan xayrlashishim uchun Ingolshtadt atrofiga piyoda sayohat qilishni taklif qildi. Men bu taklifga mamnuniyat bilan rozi bo'ldim: jismoniy harakatni yaxshi ko'rardim va Klerval ona yurtim manzaralari orasida qilgan shu kabi sayrlarimda doimo sevimli hamrohim bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: We passed a fortnight in these perambulations: my health and spirits had long been restored, and they gained additional strength from the salubrious air I breathed, the natural incidents of our progress, and the conversation of my friend. Study had before secluded me from the intercourse of my fellow-creatures, and rendered me unsocial; but Clerval called forth the better feelings of my heart; he again taught me to love the aspect of nature, and the cheerful faces of children. Excellent friend! how sincerely you did love me, and endeavour to elevate my mind until it was on a level with your own. A selfish pursuit had cramped and narrowed me, until your gentleness and affection warmed and opened my senses; I became the same happy creature who, a few years ago, loved and beloved by all, had no sorrow or care.
paras.uz: Biz bu sayrlarda ikki hafta o'tkazdik: sog'lig'im va ruhim allaqachon tiklangan edi va men nafas olgan shifobaxsh havo, yo'limizdagi tabiiy voqealar va do'stimning suhbatidan qo'shimcha kuch oldi. O'qish ilgari meni hamjinslarim bilan muloqotdan ajratib, kirishimsiz qilib qo'ygan edi; lekin Klerval yuragimning yaxshiroq tuyg'ularini uyg'otdi; u menga yana tabiat qiyofasini va bolalarning quvnoq chehralarini sevishni o'rgatdi. Ajoyib do'st! Sen meni qanchalik samimiy sevding va aqlimni o'z darajangga ko'tarishga harakat qilding. Xudbin intilish meni siqib, tor qilib qo'ygan edi, toki sening muloyimliging va mehring sezgilarimni isitib, ochmaguncha; men bir necha yil oldin hamma tomonidan sevilgan va hammani sevgan, hech qanday qayg'u yoki tashvishi bo'lmagan o'sha baxtli mavjudotga aylandim.

paras.en: When happy, inanimate nature had the power of bestowing on me the most delightful sensations. A serene sky and verdant fields filled me with ecstasy. The present season was indeed divine; the flowers of spring bloomed in the hedges, while those of summer were already in bud. I was undisturbed by thoughts which during the preceding year had pressed upon me, notwithstanding my endeavours to throw them off, with an invincible burden.
paras.uz: Baxtli bo'lganimda jonsiz tabiat menga eng yoqimli his-tuyg'ularni bag'ishlash qudratiga ega edi. Sokin osmon va yam-yashil dalalar meni vajdga to'ldirardi. Hozirgi fasl haqiqatan ham ilohiy edi; to'siqlarda bahor gullari ochilgan, yoz gullari esa allaqachon g'uncha bo'lgan edi. O'tgan yil davomida, ulardan qutulishga urinishlarimga qaramay, meni yengib bo'lmas yuk bilan ezib kelgan fikrlar endi meni bezovta qilmasdi.

paras.en: Henry rejoiced in my gaiety, and sincerely sympathised in my feelings: he exerted himself to amuse me, while he expressed the sensations that filled his soul. The resources of his mind on this occasion were truly astonishing: his conversation was full of imagination; and very often, in imitation of the Persian and Arabic writers, he invented tales of wonderful fancy and passion. At other times he repeated my favourite poems, or drew me out into arguments, which he supported with great ingenuity.
paras.uz: Genri quvnoqligimdan quvonar va his-tuyg'ularimga chin dildan hamdard edi: u ruhini to'ldirgan his-tuyg'ularni ifoda etar ekan, meni xursand qilishga harakat qilardi. Bu safar uning aql zaxiralari haqiqatan ham hayratlanarli edi: suhbati xayolga to'la edi; juda tez-tez fors va arab yozuvchilariga taqlid qilib, ajoyib xayol va ehtirosli hikoyalar to'qirdi. Boshqa paytlarda sevimli she'rlarimni takrorlar yoki meni bahsga tortib, uni katta topqirlik bilan qo'llab-quvvatlardi.

paras.en: We returned to our college on a Sunday afternoon: the peasants were dancing, and every one we met appeared gay and happy. My own spirits were high, and I bounded along with feelings of unbridled joy and hilarity.
paras.uz: Biz kollejimizga yakshanba kuni tushdan keyin qaytdik: dehqonlar raqs tushishar, biz uchratgan har kim quvnoq va baxtli ko'rinardi. Mening ham kayfiyatim baland edi va men jilovsiz quvonch va shodlik tuyg'ulari bilan sakrab-sakrab borardim.

paras.en: On my return, I found the following letter from my father:—
paras.uz: Qaytganimda otamdan quyidagi maktubni topdim:

paras.en: “My dear Victor,
paras.uz: «Aziz Viktorim,

paras.en: “You have probably waited impatiently for a letter to fix the date of your return to us; and I was at first tempted to write only a few lines, merely mentioning the day on which I should expect you. But that would be a cruel kindness, and I dare not do it. What would be your surprise, my son, when you expected a happy and glad welcome, to behold, on the contrary, tears and wretchedness? And how, Victor, can I relate our misfortune? Absence cannot have rendered you callous to our joys and griefs; and how shall I inflict pain on my long absent son? I wish to prepare you for the woeful news, but I know it is impossible; even now your eye skims over the page to seek the words which are to convey to you the horrible tidings.
paras.uz: Ehtimol, bizga qaytish sanangni belgilaydigan maktubni sabrsizlik bilan kutgandirsan; avvaliga faqat bir necha satr yozib, seni qaysi kuni kutishimni aytib qo'ya qolishga vasvasaga tushdim. Lekin bu shafqatsiz mehribonlik bo'lardi va men bunga jur'at eta olmayman. O'g'lim, baxtli va quvonchli kutib olishni kutganingda, aksincha, ko'z yoshlari va baxtsizlikni ko'rsang, qanchalik hayratlanarding? Va, Viktor, baxtsizligimizni qanday aytib beray? Uzoqlik seni quvonch va qayg'ularimizga befarq qilib qo'ygan bo'lishi mumkin emas; uzoq vaqt yo'q bo'lgan o'g'limga qanday qilib og'riq yetkazay? Seni qayg'uli xabarga tayyorlamoqchiman, lekin bu mumkin emasligini bilaman; hatto hozir ham ko'zing senga dahshatli xabarni yetkazadigan so'zlarni izlab sahifa bo'ylab yugurib bormoqda.

paras.en: “William is dead!—that sweet child, whose smiles delighted and warmed my heart, who was so gentle, yet so gay! Victor, he is murdered!
paras.uz: Uilyam o'ldi! — tabassumlari yuragimni quvontirib, isitgan, shunchalik muloyim, shu bilan birga shunchalik quvnoq o'sha shirin bola! Viktor, uni o'ldirishdi!

paras.en: “I will not attempt to console you; but will simply relate the circumstances of the transaction.
paras.uz: Seni yupatishga urinmayman; shunchaki voqeaning holatlarini hikoya qilib beraman.

paras.en: “Last Thursday (May 7th), I, my niece, and your two brothers, went to walk in Plainpalais. The evening was warm and serene, and we prolonged our walk farther than usual. It was already dusk before we thought of returning; and then we discovered that William and Ernest, who had gone on before, were not to be found. We accordingly rested on a seat until they should return. Presently Ernest came, and enquired if we had seen his brother; he said, that he had been playing with him, that William had run away to hide himself, and that he vainly sought for him, and afterwards waited for a long time, but that he did not return.
paras.uz: O'tgan payshanba kuni (7-may) men, jiyanim va ikki ukang Plenpaleda sayr qilgani chiqdik. Oqshom iliq va sokin edi, biz sayrimizni odatdagidan uzoqroqqa cho'zdik. Qaytishni o'ylaganimizda allaqachon qosh qoraygan edi; shunda oldinda ketgan Uilyam va Ernest topilmayotganini bildik. Shuning uchun ular qaytguncha o'rindiqda dam oldik. Ko'p o'tmay Ernest kelib, ukasini ko'rdingizmi, deb so'radi; u aytishicha, u bilan o'ynab yurgan ekan, Uilyam yashirinish uchun qochib ketgan, u esa uni behuda qidirgan, keyin uzoq kutgan, lekin u qaytmagan.

paras.en: “This account rather alarmed us, and we continued to search for him until night fell, when Elizabeth conjectured that he might have returned to the house. He was not there. We returned again, with torches; for I could not rest, when I thought that my sweet boy had lost himself, and was exposed to all the damps and dews of night; Elizabeth also suffered extreme anguish. About five in the morning I discovered my lovely boy, whom the night before I had seen blooming and active in health, stretched on the grass livid and motionless; the print of the murder’s finger was on his neck.
paras.uz: Bu hikoya bizni ancha xavotirga soldi va biz tun tushguncha uni qidirishda davom etdik, shunda Elizabet u uyga qaytgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb taxmin qildi. U u yerda yo'q edi. Biz mash'alalar bilan yana qaytdik; chunki shirin bolam adashib qolganini va tunning butun namligi va shudringiga duchor bo'lganini o'ylab, tinchlana olmasdim; Elizabet ham qattiq iztirob chekardi. Ertalab soat beshlarda men o'tgan oqshom sog'lom va gullab-yashnab, chaqqon holda ko'rgan yoqimtoy o'g'limni o't ustida ko'karib, qimirlamay cho'zilib yotgan holda topdim; uning bo'ynida qotilning barmoq izlari bor edi.

paras.en: “He was conveyed home, and the anguish that was visible in my countenance betrayed the secret to Elizabeth. She was very earnest to see the corpse. At first I attempted to prevent her but she persisted, and entering the room where it lay, hastily examined the neck of the victim, and clasping her hands exclaimed, ‘O God! I have murdered my darling child!’
paras.uz: Uni uyga olib kelishdi va chehramda ko'rinib turgan iztirob sirni Elizabetga oshkor qildi. U jasadni ko'rishni qattiq istadi. Avval men uni to'xtatishga urindim, lekin u qattiq turib oldi va jasad yotgan xonaga kirib, qurbonning bo'ynini shoshilib ko'zdan kechirdi va qo'llarini qovushtirib xitob qildi: «Ey Xudo! Men jonajon bolamni o'ldirdim!»

paras.en: “She fainted, and was restored with extreme difficulty. When she again lived, it was only to weep and sigh. She told me, that that same evening William had teased her to let him wear a very valuable miniature that she possessed of your mother. This picture is gone, and was doubtless the temptation which urged the murderer to the deed. We have no trace of him at present, although our exertions to discover him are unremitted; but they will not restore my beloved William!
paras.uz: U hushidan ketdi va uni nihoyatda qiyinchilik bilan o'ziga keltirishdi. U yana jonlanganda, faqat yig'lash va xo'rsinish uchun jonlandi. U menga o'sha oqshom Uilyam undan uning qo'lidagi onangning juda qimmatbaho miniatyura portretini taqib olishga ruxsat berishini so'rab xira qilganini aytdi. Bu surat yo'qolgan va, shubhasiz, qotilni bu ishga undagan vasvasa bo'lgan. Uni topish uchun tinimsiz harakat qilayotgan bo'lsak ham, hozircha undan hech qanday iz yo'q; lekin ular mening suyukli Uilyamimni qaytarib bermaydi!

paras.en: “Come, dearest Victor; you alone can console Elizabeth. She weeps continually, and accuses herself unjustly as the cause of his death; her words pierce my heart. We are all unhappy; but will not that be an additional motive for you, my son, to return and be our comforter? Your dear mother! Alas, Victor! I now say, Thank God she did not live to witness the cruel, miserable death of her youngest darling!
paras.uz: Kel, eng aziz Viktor; faqat sen Elizabetni yupata olasan. U tinimsiz yig'laydi va o'zini adolatsiz ravishda uning o'limiga sabab bo'lganlikda ayblaydi; uning so'zlari yuragimni teshib o'tadi. Hammamiz baxtsizmiz; lekin bu, o'g'lim, qaytib kelib bizga yupanch bo'lishing uchun qo'shimcha sabab bo'lmaydimi? Aziz onang! Afsus, Viktor! Endi aytaman: Xudoga shukr, u eng kichik erkatoyining shafqatsiz, ayanchli o'limini ko'rishga yashamadi!

paras.en: “Come, Victor; not brooding thoughts of vengeance against the assassin, but with feelings of peace and gentleness, that will heal, instead of festering, the wounds of our minds. Enter the house of mourning, my friend, but with kindness and affection for those who love you, and not with hatred for your enemies.
paras.uz: Kel, Viktor; qotilga qarshi qasos haqidagi o'ylar bilan emas, balki aqlimizdagi yaralarni yiringlatish o'rniga davolaydigan tinchlik va muloyimlik tuyg'ulari bilan kel. Motam uyiga kir, do'stim, lekin dushmanlaringga nafrat bilan emas, seni sevadiganlarga mehribonlik va mehr bilan kir.

paras.en: “Your affectionate and afflicted father,
paras.uz: Seni sevuvchi va qayg'uga botgan otang,

paras.en: “Alphonse Frankenstein.
paras.uz: Alfons Frankenshteyn.

paras.en: “Geneva, May 12th, 17—.”
paras.uz: Jeneva, 12-may, 17—.»

paras.en: Clerval, who had watched my countenance as I read this letter, was surprised to observe the despair that succeeded the joy I at first expressed on receiving new from my friends. I threw the letter on the table, and covered my face with my hands.
paras.uz: Men bu maktubni o'qiyotganimda chehramni kuzatib turgan Klerval do'stlarimdan yangi xabar olganimda dastlab bildirgan quvonchim o'rnini egallagan umidsizlikni ko'rib, hayron bo'ldi. Men maktubni stolga tashladim va yuzimni qo'llarim bilan yopdim.

paras.en: “My dear Frankenstein,” exclaimed Henry, when he perceived me weep with bitterness, “are you always to be unhappy? My dear friend, what has happened?”
paras.uz: «Aziz Frankenshteyn, — deb xitob qildi Genri, achchiq yig'layotganimni ko'rib, — sen doim baxtsiz bo'lishing kerakmi? Aziz do'stim, nima bo'ldi?»

paras.en: I motioned him to take up the letter, while I walked up and down the room in the extremest agitation. Tears also gushed from the eyes of Clerval, as he read the account of my misfortune.
paras.uz: Men unga maktubni olishga ishora qildim, o'zim esa eng kuchli hayajonda xonada u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurdim. Baxtsizligim haqidagi hikoyani o'qiganda Klervalning ko'zlaridan ham yosh otilib chiqdi.

paras.en: “I can offer you no consolation, my friend,” said he; “your disaster is irreparable. What do you intend to do?”
paras.uz: «Senga hech qanday tasalli bera olmayman, do'stim, — dedi u, — fojiang tuzatib bo'lmas. Nima qilmoqchisan?»

paras.en: “To go instantly to Geneva: come with me, Henry, to order the horses.”
paras.uz: «Darhol Jenevaga jo'nayman: men bilan yur, Genri, otlarni buyuramiz.»

paras.en: During our walk, Clerval endeavoured to say a few words of consolation; he could only express his heartfelt sympathy. “Poor William!” said he, “dear lovely child, he now sleeps with his angel mother! Who that had seen him bright and joyous in his young beauty, but must weep over his untimely loss! To die so miserably; to feel the murderer’s grasp! How much more a murdered that could destroy radiant innocence! Poor little fellow! one only consolation have we; his friends mourn and weep, but he is at rest. The pang is over, his sufferings are at an end for ever. A sod covers his gentle form, and he knows no pain. He can no longer be a subject for pity; we must reserve that for his miserable survivors.”
paras.uz: Yo'lda ketayotganimizda Klerval bir necha tasalli so'zlarini aytishga urindi; u faqat chin yurakdan hamdardligini bildira oldi. «Bechora Uilyam! — dedi u. — Aziz, yoqimtoy bola, u endi farishta onasi bilan uxlayapti! Uni yosh go'zalligida yorqin va quvnoq ko'rgan kim uning bevaqt ketishiga yig'lamaydi! Shunchalik ayanchli o'lish; qotilning changalini his qilish! Nurli beg'uborlikni yo'q qila olgan qotil qanchalik yovuz! Bechora kichkintoy! bizda faqat bitta tasalli bor: do'stlari qayg'urib yig'laydi, lekin u orom topdi.
