Go'yo men minglab odamlar to'planib, meni tubsizlikka itarib yuborishga urinayotgan jarlik yoqasida yurgandek his qilaman. Uilyam va Jastin o'ldirildi, qotil esa qochib qutulyapti; u dunyo bo'ylab ozod, balki hurmatda ham yuribdi. Lekin hatto xuddi shu jinoyatlar uchun dorda azob chekishga hukm qilingan taqdirimda ham, bunday bechora bilan o'rnimni almashtirmagan bo'lardim.»

paras.en: I listened to this discourse with the extremest agony. I, not in deed, but in effect, was the true murderer. Elizabeth read my anguish in my countenance, and kindly taking my hand, said, “My dearest friend, you must calm yourself. These events have affected me, God knows how deeply; but I am not so wretched as you are. There is an expression of despair, and sometimes of revenge, in your countenance that makes me tremble. Dear Victor, banish these dark passions. Remember the friends around you, who centre all their hopes in you. Have we lost the power of rendering you happy? Ah! While we love, while we are true to each other, here in this land of peace and beauty, your native country, we may reap every tranquil blessing—what can disturb our peace?”
paras.uz: Men bu nutqni eng kuchli iztirob bilan tingladim. Men, ish bilan emas, lekin oqibat jihatidan, haqiqiy qotil edim. Elizabet iztirobimni chehramdan o'qidi va mehr bilan qo'limni olib, dedi: «Eng aziz do'stim, o'zingni tinchlantirishing kerak. Bu voqealar menga ta'sir qildi, Xudo biladi, qanchalik chuqur; lekin men sendek baxtsiz emasman. Chehrangda umidsizlik, ba'zan esa qasos ifodasi bor, u meni titratadi. Aziz Viktor, bu qora ehtiroslarni quvib yubor. Atrofingdagi, barcha umidlarini senga bog'lagan do'stlaringni esla. Biz seni baxtli qilish qudratini yo'qotdikmi? Oh! Biz sevar ekanmiz, bir-birimizga sodiq ekanmiz, shu tinchlik va go'zallik yurtida, ona vataningda biz har qanday osoyishta ne'matni o'rishimiz mumkin — tinchligimizni nima buzishi mumkin?»

paras.en: And could not such words from her whom I fondly prized before every other gift of fortune suffice to chase away the fiend that lurked in my heart? Even as she spoke I drew near to her, as if in terror, lest at that very moment the destroyer had been near to rob me of her.
paras.uz: Taqdirning boshqa har qanday in'omidan ko'ra ko'proq qadrlagan qizning bunday so'zlari yuragimda yashiringan shaytonni quvib chiqarishga yetarli bo'lmasmidi? U gapirayotgan paytda ham men go'yo dahshatda, aynan o'sha lahzada vayron qiluvchi uni mendan tortib olish uchun yaqin turgandek, unga yaqinroq bordim.

paras.en: Thus not the tenderness of friendship, nor the beauty of earth, nor of heaven, could redeem my soul from woe; the very accents of love were ineffectual. I was encompassed by a cloud which no beneficial influence could penetrate. The wounded deer dragging its fainting limbs to some untrodden brake, there to gaze upon the arrow which had pierced it, and to die, was but a type of me.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, na do'stlikning nozikligi, na yerning, na osmonning go'zalligi ruhimni qayg'udan qutqara olmadi; hatto muhabbat ohanglari ham samarasiz edi. Meni hech qanday foydali ta'sir yorib o'ta olmaydigan bulut o'rab olgan edi. Holsiz a'zolarini qandaydir oyoq tegmagan butazorga sudrab borib, u yerda o'ziga sanchilgan o'qqa tikilib o'lish uchun yotgan yarador kiyik — mening timsolim edi.

paras.en: Sometimes I could cope with the sullen despair that overwhelmed me, but sometimes the whirlwind passions of my soul drove me to seek, by bodily exercise and by change of place, some relief from my intolerable sensations. It was during an access of this kind that I suddenly left my home, and bending my steps towards the near Alpine valleys, sought in the magnificence, the eternity of such scenes, to forget myself and my ephemeral, because human, sorrows. My wanderings were directed towards the valley of Chamounix. I had visited it frequently during my boyhood. Six years had passed since then: I was a wreck, but nought had changed in those savage and enduring scenes.
paras.uz: Ba'zan meni bosgan qovog'i soliq umidsizlik bilan kurasha olardim, lekin ba'zan ruhimning girdob ehtiroslari meni chidab bo'lmas his-tuyg'ularimdan jismoniy harakat va joy o'zgartirish orqali qandaydir yengillik izlashga undardi. Aynan shunday xurujlardan biri paytida men birdan uyimni tark etdim va qadamlarimni yaqin atrofdagi Alp vodiylariga qaratib, bunday manzaralarning ulug'vorligi va abadiyligida o'zimni va o'tkinchi, chunki insoniy, qayg'ularimni unutishni izladim. Sargardonligim Shamoni vodiysi tomon yo'naltirildi. Bolaligimda u yerga tez-tez borardim. O'shandan beri olti yil o'tgan edi: men xaroba edim, lekin o'sha yovvoyi va boqiy manzaralarda hech narsa o'zgarmagan edi.

paras.en: I performed the first part of my journey on horseback. I afterwards hired a mule, as the more sure-footed and least liable to receive injury on these rugged roads. The weather was fine; it was about the middle of the month of August, nearly two months after the death of Justine, that miserable epoch from which I dated all my woe. The weight upon my spirit was sensibly lightened as I plunged yet deeper in the ravine of Arve. The immense mountains and precipices that overhung me on every side, the sound of the river raging among the rocks, and the dashing of the waterfalls around spoke of a power mighty as Omnipotence—and I ceased to fear or to bend before any being less almighty than that which had created and ruled the elements, here displayed in their most terrific guise.
paras.uz: Safarimning birinchi qismini otda bosib o'tdim. Keyin bu notekis yo'llarda oyog'i mustahkamroq va shikast olishga kamroq moyil bo'lgani uchun xachir yolladim. Havo yaxshi edi; avgust oyining o'rtalari, Jastin o'limidan deyarli ikki oy o'tgan payt edi — men barcha qayg'ularimni hisoblaydigan o'sha ayanchli davr. Arve darasiga chuqurroq kirib borgan sari ruhimdagi yuk sezilarli yengillashdi. Har tomondan ustimga osilib turgan ulkan tog'lar va jarliklar, qoyalar orasida g'azablanayotgan daryoning shovqini va atrofdagi sharsharalarning gurillashi Qodiri mutlaqdek qudratli kuch haqida so'zlardi — va men bu yerda eng dahshatli qiyofasida namoyon bo'lgan unsurlarni yaratgan va boshqargan zotdan kamroq qudratli har qanday mavjudotdan qo'rqishni yoki uning oldida egilishni to'xtatdim.

paras.en: Still, as I ascended higher, the valley assumed a more magnificent and astonishing character. Ruined castles hanging on the precipices of piny mountains, the impetuous Arve, and cottages every here and there peeping forth from among the trees formed a scene of singular beauty. But it was augmented and rendered sublime by the mighty Alps, whose white and shining pyramids and domes towered above all, as belonging to another earth, the habitations of another race of beings.
paras.uz: Yanada balandroq ko'tarilgan sari vodiy yanada ulug'vorroq va hayratlanarliroq tus oldi. Qarag'ayli tog'larning jarliklarida osilib turgan vayron qal'alar, shiddatli Arve va daraxtlar orasidan u yer-bu yerda mo'ralab turgan kulbalar g'ayrioddiy go'zal manzara hosil qilardi. Lekin uni oq va yaltiroq piramidalari va gumbazlari go'yo boshqa yerga, boshqa mavjudotlar zotining maskaniga tegishlidek hamma narsadan baland ko'tarilib turgan qudratli Alplar yanada kuchaytirib, ulug'vor qilardi.

paras.en: I passed the bridge of Pélissier, where the ravine, which the river forms, opened before me, and I began to ascend the mountain that overhangs it. Soon after, I entered the valley of Chamounix. This valley is more wonderful and sublime, but not so beautiful and picturesque as that of Servox, through which I had just passed. The high and snowy mountains were its immediate boundaries, but I saw no more ruined castles and fertile fields. Immense glaciers approached the road; I heard the rumbling thunder of the falling avalanche and marked the smoke of its passage. Mont Blanc, the supreme and magnificent Mont Blanc, raised itself from the surrounding aiguilles, and its tremendous dôme overlooked the valley.
paras.uz: Men Pelisye ko'prigidan o'tdim, u yerda daryo hosil qilgan dara oldimda ochildi va men uning ustida osilib turgan tog'ga ko'tarila boshladim. Ko'p o'tmay Shamoni vodiysiga kirdim. Bu vodiy men hozirgina o'tgan Servoks vodiysidan ko'ra ajoyibroq va ulug'vorroq, lekin unchalik go'zal va manzarali emas. Baland va qorli tog'lar uning bevosita chegaralari edi, lekin men endi vayron qal'alar va serhosil dalalarni ko'rmadim. Ulkan muzliklar yo'lga yaqinlashardi; men qulayotgan ko'chkining gumburlagan momaqaldiroqini eshitdim va uning o'tgan joyidagi tutunni kuzatdim. Monblan, oliy va ulug'vor Monblan atrofdagi o'tkir cho'qqilardan ko'tarilib turardi va uning ulkan gumbazi vodiyga qarab turardi.

paras.en: A tingling long-lost sense of pleasure often came across me during this journey. Some turn in the road, some new object suddenly perceived and recognised, reminded me of days gone by, and were associated with the lighthearted gaiety of boyhood. The very winds whispered in soothing accents, and maternal Nature bade me weep no more. Then again the kindly influence ceased to act—I found myself fettered again to grief and indulging in all the misery of reflection. Then I spurred on my animal, striving so to forget the world, my fears, and more than all, myself—or, in a more desperate fashion, I alighted and threw myself on the grass, weighed down by horror and despair.
paras.uz: Bu safar davomida ko'pincha uzoq vaqtdan beri yo'qolgan jimirlatuvchi zavq tuyg'usi meni qamrab olardi. Yo'lning qandaydir burilishi, birdan ko'rilgan va tanilgan qandaydir yangi narsa menga o'tgan kunlarni eslatar va bolalikning beg'am quvnoqligi bilan bog'lanardi. Hatto shamollar ham yupatuvchi ohangda shivirlardi va onalarcha Tabiat menga boshqa yig'lamaslikni buyurardi. Keyin yana mehribon ta'sir to'xtardi — men o'zimni yana qayg'uga zanjirband va mulohazaning butun baxtsizligiga berilgan holda topardim. Shunda men hayvonimni niqtab, shu tarzda dunyoni, qo'rquvlarimni va hammadan ko'proq o'zimni unutishga intilardim — yoki yanada umidsizroq tarzda, tushib, dahshat va umidsizlik ostida ezilib, o'zimni o't ustiga tashlardim.

paras.en: At length I arrived at the village of Chamounix. Exhaustion succeeded to the extreme fatigue both of body and of mind which I had endured. For a short space of time I remained at the window watching the pallid lightnings that played above Mont Blanc and listening to the rushing of the Arve, which pursued its noisy way beneath. The same lulling sounds acted as a lullaby to my too keen sensations; when I placed my head upon my pillow, sleep crept over me; I felt it as it came and blessed the giver of oblivion.
paras.uz: Nihoyat Shamoni qishlog'iga yetib keldim. Men chidagan tana va ruhning haddan tashqari charchog'i o'rnini holsizlik egalladi. Qisqa vaqt men derazada Monblan ustida o'ynayotgan rangpar chaqmoqlarni kuzatib va pastda shovqinli yo'lini davom ettirayotgan Arvening shovullashini tinglab turdim. O'sha bir xil tinchlantiruvchi tovushlar haddan tashqari o'tkir his-tuyg'ularimga alla bo'ldi; boshimni yostiqqa qo'yganimda, uyqu meni o'rab oldi; uning kelayotganini his qildim va unutish beruvchini duo qildim.

paras.en: I spent the following day roaming through the valley. I stood beside the sources of the Arveiron, which take their rise in a glacier, that with slow pace is advancing down from the summit of the hills to barricade the valley. The abrupt sides of vast mountains were before me; the icy wall of the glacier overhung me; a few shattered pines were scattered around; and the solemn silence of this glorious presence-chamber of imperial Nature was broken only by the brawling waves or the fall of some vast fragment, the thunder sound of the avalanche or the cracking, reverberated along the mountains, of the accumulated ice, which, through the silent working of immutable laws, was ever and anon rent and torn, as if it had been but a plaything in their hands. These sublime and magnificent scenes afforded me the greatest consolation that I was capable of receiving.
paras.uz: Keyingi kunni vodiy bo'ylab kezib o'tkazdim. Men tog'lar cho'qqisidan vodiyni to'sish uchun sekin qadamlar bilan pastga siljib kelayotgan muzlikdan boshlanadigan Arveyron manbalari yonida turdim. Oldimda ulkan tog'larning tik yonbag'irlari turardi; tepamda muzlikning muz devori osilib turardi; atrofda bir nechta singan qarag'ay sochilib yotardi; va imperator Tabiatning bu shonli qabul xonasining tantanali sukunatini faqat shovqinli to'lqinlar yoki qandaydir ulkan parchaning qulashi, ko'chkining momaqaldiroqdek ovozi yoki o'zgarmas qonunlarning sokin harakati tufayli go'yo ularning qo'lidagi o'yinchoqdek vaqti-vaqti bilan yorilib, yirtilayotgan to'plangan muzning tog'lar bo'ylab aks-sado beruvchi qarsillashi buzardi. Bu ulug'vor va hashamatli manzaralar menga men qabul qila oladigan eng katta tasallini berdi.

paras.en: They elevated me from all littleness of feeling, and although they did not remove my grief, they subdued and tranquillised it. In some degree, also, they diverted my mind from the thoughts over which it had brooded for the last month. I retired to rest at night; my slumbers, as it were, waited on and ministered to by the assemblance of grand shapes which I had contemplated during the day. They congregated round me; the unstained snowy mountain-top, the glittering pinnacle, the pine woods, and ragged bare ravine, the eagle, soaring amidst the clouds—they all gathered round me and bade me be at peace.
paras.uz: Ular meni his-tuyg'ularning har qanday maydaligidan yuqori ko'tardi va qayg'umni olib tashlamagan bo'lsa ham, uni bosib, tinchlantirdi. Ular qaysidir darajada aqlimni o'tgan oy davomida bosh qotirgan fikrlardan ham chalg'itdi. Kechasi dam olishga yotdim; uyqumni go'yo kunduzi tomosha qilgan ulug'vor shakllar yig'ini kutib, xizmat qilardi. Ular atrofimga to'planishdi; dog'siz qorli tog' cho'qqisi, yaltirab turgan cho'qqi, qarag'ay o'rmonlari va qirrali yalang'och dara, bulutlar orasida parvoz qilayotgan burgut — hammasi atrofimga yig'ilib, menga tinch bo'lishni buyurdi.

paras.en: Where had they fled when the next morning I awoke? All of soul-inspiriting fled with sleep, and dark melancholy clouded every thought. The rain was pouring in torrents, and thick mists hid the summits of the mountains, so that I even saw not the faces of those mighty friends. Still I would penetrate their misty veil and seek them in their cloudy retreats. What were rain and storm to me? My mule was brought to the door, and I resolved to ascend to the summit of Montanvert. I remembered the effect that the view of the tremendous and ever-moving glacier had produced upon my mind when I first saw it. It had then filled me with a sublime ecstasy that gave wings to the soul and allowed it to soar from the obscure world to light and joy. The sight of the awful and majestic in nature had indeed always the effect of solemnising my mind and causing me to forget the passing cares of life. I determined to go without a guide, for I was well acquainted with the path, and the presence of another would destroy the solitary grandeur of the scene.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab uyg'onganimda ular qayerga qochib ketdi? Ruhni ilhomlantiruvchi hamma narsa uyqu bilan qochib ketdi va qorong'i g'amginlik har bir fikrni bulutladi. Yomg'ir sel bo'lib quyardi, quyuq tumanlar tog' cho'qqilarini yashirardi, shuning uchun men hatto o'sha qudratli do'stlarning chehralarini ham ko'rmadim. Shunga qaramay men ularning tuman pardasini yorib o'tib, ularni bulutli boshpanalarida izlamoqchi edim. Yomg'ir va bo'ron menga nima edi? Xachirimni eshik oldiga olib kelishdi va men Montanver cho'qqisiga ko'tarilishga qaror qildim. Dahshatli va doimo harakatdagi muzlik manzarasi birinchi marta ko'rganimda aqlimga qanday ta'sir qilganini esladim. U o'shanda meni ruhga qanot bergan va uni qorong'i dunyodan nur va quvonchga parvoz qilishiga imkon bergan ulug'vor vajdga to'ldirgan edi. Tabiatdagi dahshatli va salobatli narsani ko'rish haqiqatan ham doimo aqlimni tantanavor qilib, hayotning o'tkinchi tashvishlarini unutishimga sabab bo'lardi. Men yo'lboshchisiz borishga qaror qildim, chunki so'qmoqni yaxshi bilardim va boshqaning borligi manzaraning yolg'iz ulug'vorligini buzardi.

paras.en: The ascent is precipitous, but the path is cut into continual and short windings, which enable you to surmount the perpendicularity of the mountain. It is a scene terrifically desolate. In a thousand spots the traces of the winter avalanche may be perceived, where trees lie broken and strewed on the ground, some entirely destroyed, others bent, leaning upon the jutting rocks of the mountain or transversely upon other trees. The path, as you ascend higher, is intersected by ravines of snow, down which stones continually roll from above; one of them is particularly dangerous, as the slightest sound, such as even speaking in a loud voice, produces a concussion of air sufficient to draw destruction upon the head of the speaker. The pines are not tall or luxuriant, but they are sombre and add an air of severity to the scene.
paras.uz: Ko'tarilish tik, lekin so'qmoq tog'ning tikligini yengishga imkon beradigan uzluksiz va qisqa burilishlarga kesilgan. Bu dahshatli darajada xaroba manzara. Ming joyda qishki ko'chkining izlarini ko'rish mumkin, u yerda daraxtlar singan va yerga sochilib yotadi, ba'zilari butunlay vayron bo'lgan, boshqalari egilib, tog'ning bo'rtib chiqqan qoyalariga yoki ko'ndalangiga boshqa daraxtlarga suyanib turadi. Yuqoriroq ko'tarilgan sari so'qmoqni qor jarliklari kesib o'tadi, ular bo'ylab tepadan doimo toshlar dumalab tushadi; ulardan biri ayniqsa xavfli, chunki eng kichik tovush, hatto baland ovozda gapirish ham gapiruvchining boshiga halokat keltirish uchun yetarli havo silkinishini keltirib chiqaradi. Qarag'aylar baland yoki serhosil emas, lekin ular qorong'i va manzaraga qattiqlik tusini qo'shadi.

paras.en: I looked on the valley beneath; vast mists were rising from the rivers which ran through it and curling in thick wreaths around the opposite mountains, whose summits were hid in the uniform clouds, while rain poured from the dark sky and added to the melancholy impression I received from the objects around me. Alas! Why does man boast of sensibilities superior to those apparent in the brute; it only renders them more necessary beings. If our impulses were confined to hunger, thirst, and desire, we might be nearly free; but now we are moved by every wind that blows and a chance word or scene that that word may convey to us.
paras.uz: Pastdagi vodiyga qaradim; undan oqib o'tayotgan daryolardan ulkan tumanlar ko'tarilib, qarshidagi tog'lar atrofida quyuq halqalar bo'lib o'ralardi, ularning cho'qqilari bir xil bulutlarda yashiringan edi, qorong'i osmondan esa yomg'ir quyib, atrofimdagi narsalardan olgan g'amgin taassurotimni kuchaytirardi. Afsus! Nega inson hayvonda ko'rinadiganlardan ustun ta'sirchanligi bilan maqtanadi; bu uni faqat ko'proq muhtoj mavjudotga aylantiradi. Agar bizning turtkilarimiz ochlik, tashnalik va istak bilan cheklanganida, deyarli ozod bo'lardik; lekin endi bizni esayotgan har bir shamol va tasodifiy so'z yoki o'sha so'z bizga keltirishi mumkin bo'lgan manzara harakatga keltiradi.

paras.en: We rest; a dream has power to poison sleep. We rise; one wand’ring thought pollutes the day. We feel, conceive, or reason; laugh or weep, Embrace fond woe, or cast our cares away; It is the same: for, be it joy or sorrow, The path of its departure still is free. Man’s yesterday may ne’er be like his morrow; Nought may endure but mutability!
paras.uz: Dam olamiz — tush uyquni zaharlay oladi. / Turamiz — bitta adashgan o'y kunni bulg'aydi. / His qilamiz, o'ylaymiz; kulamiz yo yig'laymiz, / Shirin g'amni quchamiz yo tashvishni otamiz; / Baribir: quvonch bo'lsin yo qayg'u, / Uning ketar yo'li doim ochiq. / Insonning kechasi ertasiga hech o'xshamas; / O'zgaruvchanlikdan boshqa hech narsa boqiy emas!

paras.en: It was nearly noon when I arrived at the top of the ascent. For some time I sat upon the rock that overlooks the sea of ice. A mist covered both that and the surrounding mountains. Presently a breeze dissipated the cloud, and I descended upon the glacier. The surface is very uneven, rising like the waves of a troubled sea, descending low, and interspersed by rifts that sink deep. The field of ice is almost a league in width, but I spent nearly two hours in crossing it. The opposite mountain is a bare perpendicular rock. From the side where I now stood Montanvert was exactly opposite, at the distance of a league; and above it rose Mont Blanc, in awful majesty. I remained in a recess of the rock, gazing on this wonderful and stupendous scene.
paras.uz: Ko'tarilish cho'qqisiga yetib kelganimda deyarli tush edi. Bir muddat muz dengiziga qarab turgan qoya ustida o'tirdim. Uni ham, atrofdagi tog'larni ham tuman qoplagan edi. Ko'p o'tmay shabada bulutni tarqatdi va men muzlikka tushdim. Uning yuzasi juda notekis, notinch dengiz to'lqinlaridek ko'tarilib, pastga tushadi va chuqur ketadigan yoriqlar bilan kesilgan. Muz maydoni deyarli bir liga kenglikda, lekin men uni kesib o'tishga deyarli ikki soat sarfladim. Qarshidagi tog' yalang'och tik qoya. Hozir men turgan tomondan Montanver bir liga masofada aynan ro'parada edi; uning tepasida esa Monblan dahshatli salobat bilan ko'tarilib turardi. Men bu ajoyib va hayratlanarli manzaraga tikilib, qoyaning bir chuquriga panoh topib qoldim.

paras.en: The sea, or rather the vast river of ice, wound among its dependent mountains, whose aerial summits hung over its recesses. Their icy and glittering peaks shone in the sunlight over the clouds. My heart, which was before sorrowful, now swelled with something like joy; I exclaimed, “Wandering spirits, if indeed ye wander, and do not rest in your narrow beds, allow me this faint happiness, or take me, as your companion, away from the joys of life.”
paras.uz: Dengiz, yaxshisi, ulkan muz daryosi o'ziga tobe tog'lar orasida ilonizi bo'lib oqardi, ularning havodagi cho'qqilari uning chuqurliklari ustida osilib turardi. Ularning muzli va yaltiroq cho'qqilari bulutlar ustida quyosh nurida porlardi. Ilgari qayg'uli bo'lgan yuragim endi quvonchga o'xshash narsa bilan to'lib-toshdi; men xitob qildim: «Sargardon ruhlar, agar haqiqatan ham sargardon bo'lsangiz va tor to'shaklaringizda orom olmasangiz, menga bu xira baxtni ravo ko'ring yoki meni hamrohingiz sifatida hayot quvonchlaridan olib keting.»

paras.en: As I said this I suddenly beheld the figure of a man, at some distance, advancing towards me with superhuman speed. He bounded over the crevices in the ice, among which I had walked with caution; his stature, also, as he approached, seemed to exceed that of man. I was troubled; a mist came over my eyes, and I felt a faintness seize me, but I was quickly restored by the cold gale of the mountains. I perceived, as the shape came nearer (sight tremendous and abhorred!) that it was the wretch whom I had created. I trembled with rage and horror, resolving to wait his approach and then close with him in mortal combat. He approached; his countenance bespoke bitter anguish, combined with disdain and malignity, while its unearthly ugliness rendered it almost too horrible for human eyes. But I scarcely observed this; rage and hatred had at first deprived me of utterance, and I recovered only to overwhelm him with words expressive of furious detestation and contempt.
paras.uz: Buni aytganimda birdan ancha narida g'ayriinsoniy tezlik bilan men tomon kelayotgan odam qomatini ko'rdim. U men ehtiyotkorlik bilan yurgan muz yoriqlari ustidan sakrab o'tardi; yaqinlashgan sari uning qomati ham insonnikidan oshib ketadigandek tuyuldi. Men bezovtalandim; ko'zlarimni tuman qopladi va meni holsizlik bosayotganini his qildim, lekin tog'larning sovuq shamoli meni tez o'ziga keltirdi. Shakl yaqinlashgan sari (dahshatli va jirkanch manzara!) bu men yaratgan bechora ekanini payqadim. G'azab va dahshatdan titradim, uning yaqinlashishini kutib, keyin u bilan o'limtik jangga kirishishga qaror qildim. U yaqinlashdi; uning chehrasi nafrat va yovuzlik bilan qo'shilgan achchiq iztirobni ifodalardi, uning bu dunyoga xos bo'lmagan xunukligi esa uni inson ko'zlari uchun deyarli haddan tashqari dahshatli qilardi. Lekin men buni zo'rg'a payqadim; g'azab va nafrat dastlab meni gapirish qobiliyatidan mahrum qildi va men faqat uni g'azabli jirkanish va nafratni ifodalovchi so'zlar bilan ko'mib tashlash uchun o'zimga keldim.

paras.en: “Devil,” I exclaimed, “do you dare approach me? And do not you fear the fierce vengeance of my arm wreaked on your miserable head? Begone, vile insect! Or rather, stay, that I may trample you to dust! And, oh! That I could, with the extinction of your miserable existence, restore those victims whom you have so diabolically murdered!”
paras.uz: «Shayton, — deb xitob qildim, — menga yaqinlashishga jur'at etasanmi? Bechora boshingga tushadigan qo'limning qattiq qasosidan qo'rqmaysanmi? Yo'qol, razil hasharot! Yoki yaxshisi, qol, seni changga aylantirib oyoq osti qilay! Oh! Qaniydi sening ayanchli borlig'ingni o'chirish bilan sen shunchalik iblisona o'ldirgan qurbonlarni qaytara olsam!»

paras.en: “I expected this reception,” said the dæmon. “All men hate the wretched; how, then, must I be hated, who am miserable beyond all living things! Yet you, my creator, detest and spurn me, thy creature, to whom thou art bound by ties only dissoluble by the annihilation of one of us. You purpose to kill me. How dare you sport thus with life? Do your duty towards me, and I will do mine towards you and the rest of mankind. If you will comply with my conditions, I will leave them and you at peace; but if you refuse, I will glut the maw of death, until it be satiated with the blood of your remaining friends.”
paras.uz: «Men bunday kutib olishni kutgan edim, — dedi iblis. — Barcha odamlar baxtsizlardan nafratlanadi; unda barcha tirik mavjudotlardan ham ko'proq baxtsiz bo'lgan mendan qanchalik nafratlanishlari kerak! Shunga qaramay sen, mening yaratuvchim, mendan — o'z ijodingdan nafratlanasan va meni rad etasan, holbuki sen men bilan faqat birimizning yo'q bo'lishimiz bilangina uzilishi mumkin bo'lgan rishtalar bilan bog'langansan. Sen meni o'ldirmoqchisan. Hayot bilan bunday o'ynashga qanday jur'at etasan? Menga nisbatan burchingni bajar, men ham senga va qolgan insoniyatga nisbatan o'z burchimni bajaraman. Agar shartlarimga rozi bo'lsang, ularni ham, seni ham tinch qo'yaman; lekin agar rad etsang, o'limning qornini qolgan do'stlaringning qoniga to'yguncha to'ldiraman.»

paras.en: “Abhorred monster! Fiend that thou art! The tortures of hell are too mild a vengeance for thy crimes. Wretched devil! You reproach me with your creation, come on, then, that I may extinguish the spark which I so negligently bestowed.”
paras.uz: «Jirkanch yirtqich! Shayton! Do'zax qiynoqlari ham jinoyatlaring uchun juda yumshoq qasos. Bechora shayton! Meni seni yaratganim uchun ayblayapsan, unda kel, men shunchalik beparvolik bilan ato etgan uchqunni o'chiray.»

paras.en: My rage was without bounds; I sprang on him, impelled by all the feelings which can arm one being against the existence of another.
paras.uz: G'azabim chegarasiz edi; bir mavjudotni boshqasining borlig'iga qarshi qurollantira oladigan barcha his-tuyg'ular bilan undalib, unga tashlandim.

paras.en: He easily eluded me and said,
paras.uz: U mendan osongina qochib, dedi:

paras.en: “Be calm! I entreat you to hear me before you give vent to your hatred on my devoted head. Have I not suffered enough, that you seek to increase my misery? Life, although it may only be an accumulation of anguish, is dear to me, and I will defend it. Remember, thou hast made me more powerful than thyself; my height is superior to thine, my joints more supple. But I will not be tempted to set myself in opposition to thee. I am thy creature, and I will be even mild and docile to my natural lord and king if thou wilt also perform thy part, the which thou owest me. Oh, Frankenstein, be not equitable to every other and trample upon me alone, to whom thy justice, and even thy clemency and affection, is most due. Remember that I am thy creature; I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed. Everywhere I see bliss, from which I alone am irrevocably excluded. I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend. Make me happy, and I shall again be virtuous.”
paras.uz: «Tinchlan! Nafratingni qurbon qilingan boshimga to'kishdan oldin meni tinglashingni iltimos qilaman. Baxtsizligimni oshirishga intilayotganing uchun men yetarlicha azob chekmadimmi? Hayot, garchi u faqat iztiroblar yig'indisi bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa ham, menga aziz va men uni himoya qilaman. Unutma, sen meni o'zingdan qudratliroq qilib yaratding; bo'yim seningkidan baland, bo'g'imlarim egiluvchanroq. Lekin men senga qarshi chiqishga vasvasaga tushmayman. Men sening ijodingman va agar sen ham menga qarzdor bo'lgan o'z qismingni bajarsang, tabiiy hukmdorim va qirolimga hatto yuvosh va itoatkor bo'laman. Oh, Frankenshteyn, boshqa hammaga adolatli bo'lib, faqat meni — sening adolating, hatto rahm-shafqating va mehring eng ko'p kerak bo'lgan meni oyoq osti qilma. Unutma, men sening ijodingman; men sening Odam Atong bo'lishim kerak edi, lekin men ko'proq sen hech qanday gunohsiz quvonchdan quvayotgan yiqilgan farishtaman. Hamma joyda men saodatni ko'raman, faqat men undan qaytarib bo'lmas tarzda chetlatilganman. Men xayrixoh va yaxshi edim; baxtsizlik meni shaytonga aylantirdi. Meni baxtli qil, men yana fazilatli bo'laman.»

paras.en: “Begone! I will not hear you. There can be no community between you and me; we are enemies. Begone, or let us try our strength in a fight, in which one must fall.”
paras.uz: «Yo'qol! Seni tinglamayman. Sen bilan mening o'rtamda hech qanday umumiylik bo'lishi mumkin emas; biz dushmanmiz. Yo'qol, yoki birimiz yiqilishi kerak bo'lgan jangda kuchimizni sinab ko'raylik.»

paras.en: “How can I move thee? Will no entreaties cause thee to turn a favourable eye upon thy creature, who implores thy goodness and compassion? Believe me, Frankenstein, I was benevolent; my soul glowed with love and humanity; but am I not alone, miserably alone? You, my creator, abhor me; what hope can I gather from your fellow creatures, who owe me nothing? They spurn and hate me. The desert mountains and dreary glaciers are my refuge. I have wandered here many days; the caves of ice, which I only do not fear, are a dwelling to me, and the only one which man does not grudge. These bleak skies I hail, for they are kinder to me than your fellow beings. If the multitude of mankind knew of my existence, they would do as you do, and arm themselves for my destruction.
paras.uz: «Seni qanday ta'sirlantira olaman? Hech qanday iltijo seni ezguliging va rahm-shafqatingni so'rayotgan o'z ijodingga xayrixoh nigoh tashlashga majbur qilmaydimi? Ishon menga, Frankenshteyn, men xayrixoh edim; qalbim muhabbat va insoniylik bilan yonardi; lekin men yolg'iz emasmanmi, ayanchli yolg'iz? Sen, yaratuvchim, mendan jirkanasan; menga hech narsa qarzdor bo'lmagan hamjinslaringdan qanday umid yig'a olaman? Ular meni rad etadi va mendan nafratlanadi. Cho'l tog'lar va g'amgin muzliklar mening boshpanam. Men bu yerda ko'p kunlar kezdim; men faqat ulardan qo'rqmaydigan muz g'orlari men uchun turar joy va inson qizg'anmaydigan yagona joy. Men bu ma'yus osmonni olqishlayman, chunki u menga hamjinslaringdan mehribonroq. Agar insoniyat olomoni mening borligimdan xabar topsa, ular ham sen kabi qilib, meni yo'q qilish uchun qurollanishardi.

paras.en: Shall I not then hate them who abhor me? I will keep no terms with my enemies. I am miserable, and they shall share my wretchedness. Yet it is in your power to recompense me, and deliver them from an evil which it only remains for you to make so great, that not only you and your family, but thousands of others, shall be swallowed up in the whirlwinds of its rage. Let your compassion be moved, and do not disdain me. Listen to my tale; when you have heard that, abandon or commiserate me, as you shall judge that I deserve. But hear me. The guilty are allowed, by human laws, bloody as they are, to speak in their own defence before they are condemned. Listen to me, Frankenstein. You accuse me of murder, and yet you would, with a satisfied conscience, destroy your own creature. Oh, praise the eternal justice of man! Yet I ask you not to spare me; listen to me, and then, if you can, and if you will, destroy the work of your hands.”
paras.uz: Unda mendan jirkanadiganlardan nafratlanmasligim kerakmi? Men dushmanlarim bilan hech qanday shartlashmayman. Men baxtsizman va ular mening baxtsizligimni baham ko'radi. Shunga qaramay menga tovon to'lash va ularni faqat sen shunchalik buyuk qilishing mumkin bo'lgan yovuzlikdan qutqarish sening qo'lingda; agar shunday bo'lsa, uning g'azab girdoblariga nafaqat sen va oilang, balki minglab boshqalar ham yutilib ketadi. Rahm-shafqating qo'zg'alsin va mendan nafratlanma. Hikoyamni tingla; uni eshitgach, menga nimaga loyiq deb hukm qilsang, shunga qarab meni tashlab ket yoki menga achin. Lekin meni tingla. Inson qonunlari, qanchalik qonli bo'lmasin, aybdorlarga hukm qilinishidan oldin o'zini himoya qilib gapirishga ruxsat beradi. Meni tingla, Frankenshteyn. Sen meni qotillikda ayblaysan, shunga qaramay o'zing mamnun vijdon bilan o'z ijodingni yo'q qilmoqchisan. Oh, insonning abadiy adolatini maqtang! Shunga qaramay men sendan meni ayashingni so'ramayman; meni tingla, keyin, agar qo'lingdan kelsa va xohlasang, qo'llaringning ijodini yo'q qil.»

paras.en: “Why do you call to my remembrance,” I rejoined, “circumstances of which I shudder to reflect, that I have been the miserable origin and author? Cursed be the day, abhorred devil, in which you first saw light! Cursed (although I curse myself) be the hands that formed you! You have made me wretched beyond expression. You have left me no power to consider whether I am just to you or not. Begone! Relieve me from the sight of your detested form.”
paras.uz: «Nega sen menga o'zim haqida o'ylashdan seskanadigan, o'zim ularning ayanchli manbai va muallifi bo'lgan holatlarni eslatasan? — javob berdim men. — Jirkanch shayton, sen birinchi marta nur ko'rgan kun la'natlansin! Seni shakllantirgan qo'llar (garchi o'zimni la'natlasam ham) la'natlansin! Sen meni ta'riflab bo'lmas darajada baxtsiz qilding. Menga senga nisbatan adolatlimanmi yoki yo'qmi, o'ylash uchun hech qanday kuch qoldirmading. Yo'qol! Meni nafratli qiyofangni ko'rishdan xalos qil.»

paras.en: “Thus I relieve thee, my creator,” he said, and placed his hated hands before my eyes, which I flung from me with violence; “thus I take from thee a sight which you abhor. Still thou canst listen to me and grant me thy compassion. By the virtues that I once possessed, I demand this from you. Hear my tale; it is long and strange, and the temperature of this place is not fitting to your fine sensations; come to the hut upon the mountain. The sun is yet high in the heavens; before it descends to hide itself behind your snowy precipices and illuminate another world, you will have heard my story and can decide. On you it rests, whether I quit for ever the neighbourhood of man and lead a harmless life, or become the scourge of your fellow creatures and the author of your own speedy ruin.”
paras.uz: «Mana, seni xalos qilaman, yaratuvchim», — dedi u va nafratli qo'llarini ko'zlarim oldiga qo'ydi, men ularni zo'r bilan o'zimdan uloqtirdim; «mana, sendan sen jirkanadigan manzarani olib qo'yaman. Shunga qaramay sen meni tinglashing va menga rahm-shafqatingni ravo ko'rishing mumkin. Bir vaqtlar ega bo'lgan fazilatlarim nomi bilan buni sendan talab qilaman. Hikoyamni tingla; u uzun va g'alati, bu yerning harorati esa sening nozik his-tuyg'ularingga mos emas; tog'dagi kulbaga kel. Quyosh hali osmonda baland; u sening qorli jarliklaring ortiga yashirinish va boshqa dunyoni yoritish uchun tushmasidan oldin, sen hikoyamni eshitib bo'lasan va qaror qila olasan. Men inson yaqinligini abadiy tark etib, zararsiz hayot kechirishimmi yoki hamjinslaringning balosi va o'zingning tez halokatingning muallifi bo'lishim senga bog'liq.»

paras.en: As he said this he led the way across the ice; I followed. My heart was full, and I did not answer him, but as I proceeded, I weighed the various arguments that he had used and determined at least to listen to his tale. I was partly urged by curiosity, and compassion confirmed my resolution. I had hitherto supposed him to be the murderer of my brother, and I eagerly sought a confirmation or denial of this opinion. For the first time, also, I felt what the duties of a creator towards his creature were, and that I ought to render him happy before I complained of his wickedness. These motives urged me to comply with his demand. We crossed the ice, therefore, and ascended the opposite rock. The air was cold, and the rain again began to descend; we entered the hut, the fiend with an air of exultation, I with a heavy heart and depressed spirits. But I consented to listen, and seating myself by the fire which my odious companion had lighted, he thus began his tale.
paras.uz: Shuni aytib, u muz bo'ylab yo'l boshladi; men ergashdim. Yuragim to'lib ketgan edi va men unga javob bermadim, lekin borgan sari u keltirgan turli dalillarni tarozida tortib ko'rdim va hech bo'lmasa uning hikoyasini tinglashga qaror qildim. Meni qisman qiziquvchanlik undardi, rahm-shafqat esa qarorimni mustahkamladi. Shu paytgacha men uni ukamning qotili deb taxmin qilgan edim va bu fikrning tasdig'i yoki inkorini ishtiyoq bilan izlardim. Shuningdek, birinchi marta yaratuvchining o'z ijodiga nisbatan burchlari nima ekanini va uning yovuzligidan shikoyat qilishdan oldin uni baxtli qilishim kerakligini his qildim. Bu sabablar meni uning talabini bajarishga undadi. Shuning uchun biz muzni kesib o'tib, qarshidagi qoyaga ko'tarildik. Havo sovuq edi va yomg'ir yana yog'a boshladi; biz kulbaga kirdik — shayton g'alabali qiyofada, men esa og'ir yurak va tushkun ruh bilan. Lekin men tinglashga rozi bo'ldim va jirkanch hamrohim yoqqan olov yoniga o'tirgach, u hikoyasini shunday boshladi.

paras.en: “It is with considerable difficulty that I remember the original era of my being; all the events of that period appear confused and indistinct. A strange multiplicity of sensations seized me, and I saw, felt, heard, and smelt at the same time; and it was, indeed, a long time before I learned to distinguish between the operations of my various senses. By degrees, I remember, a stronger light pressed upon my nerves, so that I was obliged to shut my eyes. Darkness then came over me and troubled me, but hardly had I felt this when, by opening my eyes, as I now suppose, the light poured in upon me again. I walked and, I believe, descended, but I presently found a great alteration in my sensations.
paras.uz: «Borlig'imning ilk davrini ancha qiyinchilik bilan eslayman; o'sha davrning barcha voqealari chalkash va noaniq ko'rinadi. Meni g'alati xilma-xil his-tuyg'ular qamrab oldi va men bir vaqtning o'zida ko'rdim, his qildim, eshitdim va hidladim; aslida turli sezgilarimning ishini bir-biridan farqlashni o'rganishimga uzoq vaqt kerak bo'ldi. Eslayman, asta-sekin kuchliroq nur asablarimga bosim o'tkazdi, shuning uchun ko'zlarimni yumishga majbur bo'ldim. Keyin meni zulmat qopladi va bezovta qildi, lekin buni his qilishim bilanoq, hozir taxmin qilishimcha, ko'zlarimni ochishim bilan nur yana menga quyilib keldi. Men yurdim va, menimcha, pastga tushdim, lekin ko'p o'tmay his-tuyg'ularimda katta o'zgarishni sezdim.

paras.en: Before, dark and opaque bodies had surrounded me, impervious to my touch or sight; but I now found that I could wander on at liberty, with no obstacles which I could not either surmount or avoid. The light became more and more oppressive to me, and the heat wearying me as I walked, I sought a place where I could receive shade. This was the forest near Ingolstadt; and here I lay by the side of a brook resting from my fatigue, until I felt tormented by hunger and thirst. This roused me from my nearly dormant state, and I ate some berries which I found hanging on the trees or lying on the ground. I slaked my thirst at the brook, and then lying down, was overcome by sleep.
paras.uz: Ilgari meni teginishim yoki ko'rishim o'tolmaydigan qorong'i va noshaffof jismlar o'rab turgan edi; lekin endi men o'zim yengib o'ta olmaydigan yoki chetlab o'ta olmaydigan to'siqlarsiz erkin kezib yura olishimni payqadim. Nur menga tobora og'irroq bo'lib bordi, yurganimda issiq meni charchatgani uchun soya topa oladigan joy izladim. Bu Ingolshtadt yaqinidagi o'rmon edi; bu yerda men ochlik va tashnalik meni qiynay boshlaguncha charchog'imni chiqarib, soy bo'yida yotdim. Bu meni deyarli uyqudagi holatimdan uyg'otdi va daraxtlarda osilib turgan yoki yerda yotgan bir nechta mevani topib yedim. Tashnaligimni soyda qondirdim, keyin yotib, uyquga ketdim.

paras.en: “It was dark when I awoke; I felt cold also, and half frightened, as it were, instinctively, finding myself so desolate. Before I had quitted your apartment, on a sensation of cold, I had covered myself with some clothes, but these were insufficient to secure me from the dews of night. I was a poor, helpless, miserable wretch; I knew, and could distinguish, nothing; but feeling pain invade me on all sides, I sat down and wept.
paras.uz: Uyg'onganimda qorong'i edi; sovuqni ham his qildim va o'zimni shunchalik yolg'iz topib, go'yo instinktiv ravishda yarim qo'rqib ketdim. Sening xonangni tark etishimdan oldin, sovuqni sezib, o'zimni bir nechta kiyim bilan yopgan edim, lekin ular meni tun shudringidan himoya qilish uchun yetarli emas edi. Men bechora, ojiz, ayanchli bir mavjudot edim; men hech narsani bilmasdim va farqlay olmasdim; lekin og'riq har tomondan bostirib kelayotganini his qilib, o'tirib yig'ladim.

paras.en: “Soon a gentle light stole over the heavens and gave me a sensation of pleasure. I started up and beheld a radiant form rise from among the trees. [The moon] I gazed with a kind of wonder. It moved slowly, but it enlightened my path, and I again went out in search of berries. I was still cold when under one of the trees I found a huge cloak, with which I covered myself, and sat down upon the ground. No distinct ideas occupied my mind; all was confused. I felt light, and hunger, and thirst, and darkness; innumerable sounds rang in my ears, and on all sides various scents saluted me; the only object that I could distinguish was the bright moon, and I fixed my eyes on that with pleasure.
paras.uz: Ko'p o'tmay osmon bo'ylab mayin nur sirg'alib, menga zavq tuyg'usini berdi. Sakrab turib, daraxtlar orasidan nurli shakl ko'tarilayotganini ko'rdim. [Oy] Men qandaydir hayrat bilan tikildim. U sekin harakatlanardi, lekin yo'limni yoritdi va men yana meva izlab chiqdim. Hali ham sovqotayotgan edim, shunda daraxtlardan birining tagida ulkan plash topdim, uni ustimga yopib, yerga o'tirdim. Aqlimni hech qanday aniq fikr band qilmasdi; hammasi chalkash edi. Men nurni, ochlikni, tashnalikni va zulmatni his qilardim; quloqlarimda son-sanoqsiz tovushlar jaranglardi va har tomondan turli hidlar menga salom berardi; men farqlay oladigan yagona narsa yorqin oy edi va men unga zavq bilan ko'zimni qadadim.

paras.en: “Several changes of day and night passed, and the orb of night had greatly lessened, when I began to distinguish my sensations from each other. I gradually saw plainly the clear stream that supplied me with drink and the trees that shaded me with their foliage. I was delighted when I first discovered that a pleasant sound, which often saluted my ears, proceeded from the throats of the little winged animals who had often intercepted the light from my eyes. I began also to observe, with greater accuracy, the forms that surrounded me and to perceive the boundaries of the radiant roof of light which canopied me. Sometimes I tried to imitate the pleasant songs of the birds but was unable. Sometimes I wished to express my sensations in my own mode, but the uncouth and inarticulate sounds which broke from me frightened me into silence again.
paras.uz: Bir necha marta kun va tun almashdi, tun yoritqichi ancha kichraydi, shunda men his-tuyg'ularimni bir-biridan farqlay boshladim. Asta-sekin menga ichimlik bergan tiniq soyni va barglari bilan menga soya solgan daraxtlarni aniq ko'ra boshladim. Ko'pincha quloqlarimga salom beradigan yoqimli tovush ko'zlarimdan nurni tez-tez to'sib qo'yadigan kichkina qanotli jonivorlarning tomog'idan chiqayotganini birinchi marta kashf etganimda, xursand bo'ldim. Men atrofimdagi shakllarni ham aniqroq kuzata boshladim va ustimni yopib turgan nurli yorug'lik tomining chegaralarini idrok eta boshladim. Ba'zan qushlarning yoqimli qo'shiqlariga taqlid qilishga urinardim, lekin uddalay olmasdim. Ba'zan his-tuyg'ularimni o'zimcha ifoda etmoqchi bo'lardim, lekin mendan chiqqan qo'pol va tushunarsiz tovushlar meni qo'rqitib, yana jim qildirardi.

paras.en: “The moon had disappeared from the night, and again, with a lessened form, showed itself, while I still remained in the forest. My sensations had by this time become distinct, and my mind received every day additional ideas. My eyes became accustomed to the light and to perceive objects in their right forms; I distinguished the insect from the herb, and by degrees, one herb from another. I found that the sparrow uttered none but harsh notes, whilst those of the blackbird and thrush were sweet and enticing.
paras.uz: Men hali ham o'rmonda yashayotganimda oy tundan g'oyib bo'ldi va yana kichraygan shaklda ko'rindi. Bu vaqtga kelib his-tuyg'ularim aniq bo'lib qolgan edi va aqlim har kuni qo'shimcha g'oyalar olardi. Ko'zlarim nurga va narsalarni to'g'ri shaklida idrok etishga o'rgandi; men hasharotni o'tdan, asta-sekin esa bir o'tni boshqasidan farqladim. Chumchuq faqat qo'pol tovushlar chiqarishini, qoraqush va sayroqi qushniki esa shirin va jozibali ekanini bildim.

paras.en: “One day, when I was oppressed by cold, I found a fire which had been left by some wandering beggars, and was overcome with delight at the warmth I experienced from it. In my joy I thrust my hand into the live embers, but quickly drew it out again with a cry of pain. How strange, I thought, that the same cause should produce such opposite effects! I examined the materials of the fire, and to my joy found it to be composed of wood. I quickly collected some branches, but they were wet and would not burn. I was pained at this and sat still watching the operation of the fire. The wet wood which I had placed near the heat dried and itself became inflamed.
paras.uz: Bir kuni sovuq meni ezayotganda, qandaydir sarson gadolar qoldirib ketgan olovni topdim va undan his qilgan iliqlikdan zavqqa to'lib ketdim. Quvonchimdan qo'limni cho'g'ga tiqdim, lekin og'riqdan qichqirib, tez tortib oldim. Qanday g'alati, deb o'yladim, bitta sabab shunday qarama-qarshi oqibatlarni keltirib chiqaradi! Men olovning materiallarini ko'zdan kechirdim va quvonchimga u yog'ochdan iboratligini bildim. Tezda bir nechta shox yig'dim, lekin ular nam edi va yonmadi. Bundan xafa bo'ldim va olovning ishini kuzatib, jim o'tirdim. Issiqqa yaqin qo'ygan nam yog'och qurib, o'zi ham alangalandi.

paras.en: I reflected on this, and by touching the various branches, I discovered the cause and busied myself in collecting a great quantity of wood, that I might dry it and have a plentiful supply of fire. When night came on and brought sleep with it, I was in the greatest fear lest my fire should be extinguished. I covered it carefully with dry wood and leaves and placed wet branches upon it; and then, spreading my cloak, I lay on the ground and sank into sleep.
paras.uz: Men bu haqda o'yladim va turli shoxlarga tegib, sababini kashf etdim va uni quritib, mo'l olov zaxirasiga ega bo'lish uchun ko'p yog'och yig'ish bilan band bo'ldim. Tun kelib, o'zi bilan uyquni olib kelganda, olovim o'chib qolmasin deb eng katta qo'rquvda edim. Uni quruq yog'och va barglar bilan ehtiyotkorlik bilan yopdim va ustiga nam shoxlar qo'ydim; keyin plashimni yoyib, yerga yotdim va uyquga g'arq bo'ldim.

paras.en: “It was morning when I awoke, and my first care was to visit the fire. I uncovered it, and a gentle breeze quickly fanned it into a flame. I observed this also and contrived a fan of branches, which roused the embers when they were nearly extinguished. When night came again I found, with pleasure, that the fire gave light as well as heat and that the discovery of this element was useful to me in my food, for I found some of the offals that the travellers had left had been roasted, and tasted much more savoury than the berries I gathered from the trees. I tried, therefore, to dress my food in the same manner, placing it on the live embers. I found that the berries were spoiled by this operation, and the nuts and roots much improved.
paras.uz: Uyg'onganimda ertalab edi va birinchi tashvishim olovni ko'rish bo'ldi. Uni ochdim va mayin shabada uni tez alangaga aylantirdi. Buni ham kuzatdim va shoxlardan yelpig'ich yasadim, u deyarli o'chgan cho'g'larni jonlantirardi. Tun yana kelganda, olov issiqlik bilan bir qatorda nur ham berishini va bu unsurning kashf etilishi ovqatim uchun foydali ekanini zavq bilan bildim, chunki sayyohlar qoldirib ketgan ba'zi qoldiqlar qovurilgan va daraxtlardan yig'gan mevalarimdan ancha mazaliroq ekanini payqadim. Shuning uchun ovqatimni xuddi shunday tayyorlashga, uni cho'g' ustiga qo'yishga urindim. Bu ishdan mevalar buzilishini, yong'oqlar va ildizlar esa ancha yaxshilanishini bildim.

paras.en: “Food, however, became scarce, and I often spent the whole day searching in vain for a few acorns to assuage the pangs of hunger. When I found this, I resolved to quit the place that I had hitherto inhabited, to seek for one where the few wants I experienced would be more easily satisfied. In this emigration I exceedingly lamented the loss of the fire which I had obtained through accident and knew not how to reproduce it. I gave several hours to the serious consideration of this difficulty, but I was obliged to relinquish all attempt to supply it, and wrapping myself up in my cloak, I struck across the wood towards the setting sun. I passed three days in these rambles and at length discovered the open country. A great fall of snow had taken place the night before, and the fields were of one uniform white; the appearance was disconsolate, and I found my feet chilled by the cold damp substance that covered the ground.
paras.uz: Biroq ovqat kamayib qoldi va men ko'pincha ochlik azobini yengillashtirish uchun bir nechta dub yong'og'ini behuda qidirib butun kunni o'tkazardim. Buni ko'rib, shu paytgacha yashagan joyimni tark etib, boshdan kechirgan oz ehtiyojlarim osonroq qondiriladigan joy izlashga qaror qildim. Bu ko'chishda tasodifan qo'lga kiritgan va qanday qayta hosil qilishni bilmagan olovni yo'qotganimdan qattiq afsuslandim. Bu qiyinchilik ustida bir necha soat jiddiy o'yladim, lekin uni to'ldirish uchun har qanday urinishdan voz kechishga majbur bo'ldim va plashimga o'ralib, botayotgan quyosh tomon o'rmon bo'ylab yo'l oldim. Bu kezishlarda uch kun o'tkazdim va nihoyat ochiq dalaga chiqdim. O'tgan kechasi qalin qor yog'gan edi va dalalar bir xil oppoq edi; manzara g'amgin edi va yerni qoplagan sovuq, nam modda oyoqlarimni muzlatib yuborganini his qildim.

paras.en: “It was about seven in the morning, and I longed to obtain food and shelter; at length I perceived a small hut, on a rising ground, which had doubtless been built for the convenience of some shepherd. This was a new sight to me, and I examined the structure with great curiosity. Finding the door open, I entered. An old man sat in it, near a fire, over which he was preparing his breakfast. He turned on hearing a noise, and perceiving me, shrieked loudly, and quitting the hut, ran across the fields with a speed of which his debilitated form hardly appeared capable. His appearance, different from any I had ever before seen, and his flight somewhat surprised me.
paras.uz: Ertalab soat yettilar edi va men ovqat va boshpana topishni orzu qilardim; nihoyat tepalikda, shubhasiz, qandaydir cho'ponning qulayligi uchun qurilgan kichik kulbani ko'rdim. Bu men uchun yangi manzara edi va men inshootni katta qiziqish bilan ko'zdan kechirdim. Eshik ochiq ekanini ko'rib, ichkariga kirdim. U yerda olov yonida bir chol o'tirib, olov ustida nonushtasini tayyorlayotgan edi. U shovqinni eshitib o'girildi va meni ko'rib, baland ovozda chinqirdi va kulbani tark etib, uning zaif vujudi zo'rg'a qodir bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan tezlik bilan dalalar bo'ylab qochib ketdi. Uning men ilgari ko'rgan har qanday narsadan farq qiluvchi qiyofasi va qochishi meni biroz hayron qoldirdi.

paras.en: But I was enchanted by the appearance of the hut; here the snow and rain could not penetrate; the ground was dry; and it presented to me then as exquisite and divine a retreat as Pandæmonium appeared to the dæmons of hell after their sufferings in the lake of fire. I greedily devoured the remnants of the shepherd’s breakfast, which consisted of bread, cheese, milk, and wine; the latter, however, I did not like. Then, overcome by fatigue, I lay down among some straw and fell asleep.
paras.uz: Lekin kulbaning ko'rinishi meni maftun etdi; bu yerga qor va yomg'ir kira olmasdi; yer quruq edi; va u menga o'shanda olovli ko'ldagi azoblaridan keyin do'zax iblislariga Pandemonium ko'ringanidek nafis va ilohiy boshpana bo'lib ko'rindi. Men cho'ponning non, pishloq, sut va sharobdan iborat nonushtasi qoldiqlarini ochko'zlik bilan yeb bitirdim; ammo sharobni yoqtirmadim. Keyin charchoqdan holdan toyib, somon orasiga yotdim va uxlab qoldim.

paras.en: “It was noon when I awoke, and allured by the warmth of the sun, which shone brightly on the white ground, I determined to recommence my travels; and, depositing the remains of the peasant’s breakfast in a wallet I found, I proceeded across the fields for several hours, until at sunset I arrived at a village. How miraculous did this appear! The huts, the neater cottages, and stately houses engaged my admiration by turns. The vegetables in the gardens, the milk and cheese that I saw placed at the windows of some of the cottages, allured my appetite. One of the best of these I entered, but I had hardly placed my foot within the door before the children shrieked, and one of the women fainted.
paras.uz: Uyg'onganimda tush edi va oppoq yerda yorqin porlayotgan quyoshning iliqligidan jalb qilinib, sayohatimni qayta boshlashga qaror qildim; dehqonning nonushtasi qoldiqlarini topgan xaltamga solib, bir necha soat dalalar bo'ylab yurdim, toki quyosh botganda bir qishloqqa yetib keldim. Bu qanchalik mo''jizaviy ko'rindi! Kulbalar, ozodaroq uylar va salobatli imoratlar navbatma-navbat hayratimni uyg'otardi. Bog'lardagi sabzavotlar, ba'zi uylarning derazalariga qo'yilgan sut va pishloq ishtahamni qo'zg'atdi. Ulardan eng yaxshilaridan biriga kirdim, lekin eshikdan oyog'imni qo'yishim bilanoq bolalar chinqirishdi va ayollardan biri hushidan ketdi.

paras.en: The whole village was roused; some fled, some attacked me, until, grievously bruised by stones and many other kinds of missile weapons, I escaped to the open country and fearfully took refuge in a low hovel, quite bare, and making a wretched appearance after the palaces I had beheld in the village. This hovel however, joined a cottage of a neat and pleasant appearance, but after my late dearly bought experience, I dared not enter it. My place of refuge was constructed of wood, but so low that I could with difficulty sit upright in it. No wood, however, was placed on the earth, which formed the floor, but it was dry; and although the wind entered it by innumerable chinks, I found it an agreeable asylum from the snow and rain.
paras.uz: Butun qishloq oyoqqa turdi; ba'zilar qochishdi, ba'zilar menga hujum qilishdi, toki toshlar va boshqa ko'plab otiladigan qurollar bilan qattiq ezilib, ochiq dalaga qochib, qo'rquv bilan past, butunlay yalang'och va qishloqda ko'rgan saroylarimdan keyin ayanchli ko'rinadigan bir xarobaga panoh topmagunimcha. Biroq bu xaroba ozoda va yoqimli ko'rinishdagi kulbaga tutash edi, lekin yaqindagi qimmatga tushgan tajribamdan keyin unga kirishga jur'at etmadim. Panohim yog'ochdan qurilgan edi, lekin shunchalik past ediki, unda zo'rg'a tik o'tira olardim. Biroq pol vazifasini o'tagan yerga hech qanday yog'och yotqizilmagan edi, lekin u quruq edi; va shamol son-sanoqsiz yoriqlardan kirib tursa ham, men uni qor va yomg'irdan yoqimli boshpana deb topdim.

paras.en: “Here, then, I retreated and lay down happy to have found a shelter, however miserable, from the inclemency of the season, and still more from the barbarity of man. As soon as morning dawned I crept from my kennel, that I might view the adjacent cottage and discover if I could remain in the habitation I had found. It was situated against the back of the cottage and surrounded on the sides which were exposed by a pig sty and a clear pool of water. One part was open, and by that I had crept in; but now I covered every crevice by which I might be perceived with stones and wood, yet in such a manner that I might move them on occasion to pass out; all the light I enjoyed came through the sty, and that was sufficient for me.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, shu yerga chekindim va fasl yomonligidan, undan ham ko'proq insonning vahshiyligidan qanchalik ayanchli bo'lmasin boshpana topganimdan baxtli bo'lib yotdim. Tong otishi bilanoq qo'shni kulbani ko'rish va topgan maskanimda qola olamanmi, bilish uchun inimdan o'rmalab chiqdim. U kulbaning orqa devoriga tutash bo'lib, ochiq tomonlaridan cho'chqaxona va tiniq suv hovuzi bilan o'ralgan edi. Bir qismi ochiq edi, men o'sha yerdan o'rmalab kirgan edim; lekin endi meni ko'rib qolishlari mumkin bo'lgan har bir yoriqni tosh va yog'och bilan berkitdim, lekin shunday qildimki, zarur bo'lganda chiqish uchun ularni surib qo'ya olay; men bahramand bo'lgan barcha nur cho'chqaxona orqali kirardi va bu menga yetarli edi.

paras.en: “Having thus arranged my dwelling and carpeted it with clean straw, I retired, for I saw the figure of a man at a distance, and I remembered too well my treatment the night before to trust myself in his power. I had first, however, provided for my sustenance for that day by a loaf of coarse bread, which I purloined, and a cup with which I could drink more conveniently than from my hand of the pure water which flowed by my retreat. The floor was a little raised, so that it was kept perfectly dry, and by its vicinity to the chimney of the cottage it was tolerably warm.
paras.uz: Maskanimni shu tarzda tartibga solib, toza somon to'shab, men yashirindim, chunki uzoqda bir odam qomatini ko'rdim va o'tgan kechagi muomalani o'zimni uning ixtiyoriga ishonish uchun juda yaxshi eslardim. Biroq avval o'sha kun uchun ovqatimni o'g'irlab olgan bir bo'lak dag'al non bilan va panohim yonidan oqib o'tadigan toza suvni qo'limdan ko'ra qulayroq ichishim mumkin bo'lgan kosacha bilan ta'minladim. Pol biroz ko'tarilgan edi, shuning uchun mukammal quruq turardi va kulba mo'risiga yaqinligi tufayli ancha iliq edi.

paras.en: “Being thus provided, I resolved to reside in this hovel until something should occur which might alter my determination. It was indeed a paradise compared to the bleak forest, my former residence, the rain-dropping branches, and dank earth. I ate my breakfast with pleasure and was about to remove a plank to procure myself a little water when I heard a step, and looking through a small chink, I beheld a young creature, with a pail on her head, passing before my hovel. The girl was young and of gentle demeanour, unlike what I have since found cottagers and farmhouse servants to be. Yet she was meanly dressed, a coarse blue petticoat and a linen jacket being her only garb; her fair hair was plaited but not adorned: she looked patient yet sad.
paras.uz: Shu tarzda ta'minlangach, qarorimni o'zgartirishi mumkin bo'lgan biror narsa sodir bo'lguncha bu xarobada yashashga qaror qildim. Bu haqiqatan ham avvalgi maskanim — ma'yus o'rmon, yomg'ir tomayotgan shoxlar va nam yer bilan solishtirganda jannat edi. Nonushtamni zavq bilan yedim va o'zimga ozgina suv olish uchun bir taxtani surmoqchi bo'lganimda qadam tovushini eshitdim va kichik yoriqdan qarab, boshida chelak bilan xarobam oldidan o'tib ketayotgan yosh jonzotni ko'rdim. Qiz yosh va muloyim qiyofali edi, men keyinchalik qishloqliklar va ferma xizmatkorlarini qanday deb bilgan bo'lsam, unga o'xshamasdi. Shunga qaramay u kambag'al kiyingan edi, yagona kiyimi dag'al ko'k yubka va zig'ir kamzul edi; oq-sariq sochlari o'rilgan, lekin bezatilmagan edi: u sabrli, lekin g'amgin ko'rinardi.

paras.en: I lost sight of her, and in about a quarter of an hour she returned bearing the pail, which was now partly filled with milk. As she walked along, seemingly incommoded by the burden, a young man met her, whose countenance expressed a deeper despondence. Uttering a few sounds with an air of melancholy, he took the pail from her head and bore it to the cottage himself. She followed, and they disappeared. Presently I saw the young man again, with some tools in his hand, cross the field behind the cottage; and the girl was also busied, sometimes in the house and sometimes in the yard.
paras.uz: Men uni ko'zdan yo'qotdim va taxminan chorak soatdan keyin u endi qisman sut bilan to'ldirilgan chelakni ko'tarib qaytdi. U yukdan qiynalayotgandek yurib kelarkan, uni yuzida chuqurroq tushkunlik ifodasi bo'lgan bir yigit kutib oldi. G'amgin qiyofada bir nechta tovush chiqarib, u chelakni qizning boshidan olib, o'zi kulbaga olib bordi. Qiz ergashdi va ular g'oyib bo'lishdi. Ko'p o'tmay men yigitni yana qo'lida qandaydir asboblar bilan kulba ortidagi dalani kesib o'tayotganini ko'rdim; qiz ham ba'zan uyda, ba'zan hovlida band edi.

paras.en: “On examining my dwelling, I found that one of the windows of the cottage had formerly occupied a part of it, but the panes had been filled up with wood. In one of these was a small and almost imperceptible chink through which the eye could just penetrate. Through this crevice a small room was visible, whitewashed and clean but very bare of furniture. In one corner, near a small fire, sat an old man, leaning his head on his hands in a disconsolate attitude. The young girl was occupied in arranging the cottage; but presently she took something out of a drawer, which employed her hands, and she sat down beside the old man, who, taking up an instrument, began to play and to produce sounds sweeter than the voice of the thrush or the nightingale.
paras.uz: Maskanimni ko'zdan kechirib, ilgari kulbaning derazalaridan biri uning bir qismini egallaganini, lekin oynalar yog'och bilan berkitilganini aniqladim. Ulardan birida ko'z zo'rg'a sig'adigan kichik va deyarli sezilmas yoriq bor edi. Bu yoriq orqali oqlangan va toza, lekin jihozlari juda kam kichik xona ko'rinardi. Bir burchakda, kichik olov yonida bir chol boshini qo'llariga qo'yib, ma'yus holatda o'tirardi. Yosh qiz kulbani tartibga solish bilan band edi; lekin ko'p o'tmay u tortmadan qo'llarini band qiladigan nimadir olib, cholning yoniga o'tirdi, chol esa qandaydir asbobni olib, chala boshladi va sayroqi qush yoki bulbulning ovozidan ham shirinroq tovushlar chiqardi.

paras.en: It was a lovely sight, even to me, poor wretch who had never beheld aught beautiful before. The silver hair and benevolent countenance of the aged cottager won my reverence, while the gentle manners of the girl enticed my love. He played a sweet mournful air which I perceived drew tears from the eyes of his amiable companion, of which the old man took no notice, until she sobbed audibly; he then pronounced a few sounds, and the fair creature, leaving her work, knelt at his feet. He raised her and smiled with such kindness and affection that I felt sensations of a peculiar and overpowering nature; they were a mixture of pain and pleasure, such as I had never before experienced, either from hunger or cold, warmth or food; and I withdrew from the window, unable to bear these emotions.
paras.uz: Bu hatto men uchun ham — ilgari hech qachon go'zal narsa ko'rmagan bechora uchun ham yoqimli manzara edi. Keksa qishloqlikning kumush sochlari va xayrixoh chehrasi ehtiromimni qozondi, qizning muloyim muomalasi esa muhabbatimni o'ziga tortdi. Chol shirin, g'amgin kuy chaldi, men u yoqimtoy hamrohining ko'zlaridan yosh oqizayotganini payqadim, chol esa qiz eshitiladigan darajada ho'ngramaguncha buni payqamadi; keyin u bir nechta tovush aytdi va go'zal jonzot ishini qo'yib, uning oyoqlari ostida tiz cho'kdi. U uni turg'izdi va shunday mehribonlik va mehr bilan jilmaydiki, men o'ziga xos va kuchli tabiatli his-tuyg'ularni his qildim; ular og'riq va zavqning aralashmasi bo'lib, men ilgari na ochlikdan, na sovuqdan, na iliqlikdan, na ovqatdan bunday narsani boshdan kechirmagan edim; va bu hayajonlarga chiday olmay, derazadan chekindim.

paras.en: “Soon after this the young man returned, bearing on his shoulders a load of wood. The girl met him at the door, helped to relieve him of his burden, and taking some of the fuel into the cottage, placed it on the fire; then she and the youth went apart into a nook of the cottage, and he showed her a large loaf and a piece of cheese. She seemed pleased and went into the garden for some roots and plants, which she placed in water, and then upon the fire. She afterwards continued her work, whilst the young man went into the garden and appeared busily employed in digging and pulling up roots. After he had been employed thus about an hour, the young woman joined him and they entered the cottage together.
paras.uz: Bundan keyin ko'p o'tmay yigit yelkasida bir yuk o'tin ko'tarib qaytdi. Qiz uni eshik oldida kutib oldi, yukidan qutulishiga yordam berdi va o'tindan bir qismini kulbaga olib kirib, olovga qo'ydi; keyin u va yigit kulbaning bir burchagiga chetga chiqishdi va yigit unga katta non va bir bo'lak pishloq ko'rsatdi. Qiz xursand bo'lganga o'xshardi va bog'dan qandaydir ildiz va o'simliklar olib keldi, ularni suvga, keyin olovga qo'ydi. Keyin u ishini davom ettirdi, yigit esa bog'ga chiqib, kovlash va ildizlarni sug'urish bilan qattiq band bo'lganga o'xshardi. U taxminan bir soat shu tarzda band bo'lgach, yosh ayol unga qo'shildi va ular birga kulbaga kirishdi.

paras.en: “The old man had, in the meantime, been pensive, but on the appearance of his companions he assumed a more cheerful air, and they sat down to eat. The meal was quickly dispatched. The young woman was again occupied in arranging the cottage, the old man walked before the cottage in the sun for a few minutes, leaning on the arm of the youth. Nothing could exceed in beauty the contrast between these two excellent creatures. One was old, with silver hairs and a countenance beaming with benevolence and love; the younger was slight and graceful in his figure, and his features were moulded with the finest symmetry, yet his eyes and attitude expressed the utmost sadness and despondency. The old man returned to the cottage, and the youth, with tools different from those he had used in the morning, directed his steps across the fields.
paras.uz: Bu orada chol o'yga tolgan edi, lekin hamrohlari paydo bo'lgach, u quvnoqroq qiyofaga kirdi va ular ovqatlanishga o'tirishdi. Taom tez yeb bo'lindi. Yosh ayol yana kulbani tartibga solish bilan band bo'ldi, chol esa yigitning qo'liga suyanib, bir necha daqiqa kulba oldida quyoshda sayr qildi. Bu ikki ajoyib jonzot o'rtasidagi qarama-qarshilikdan go'zalroq narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas edi. Biri keksa, kumush sochli va xayrixohlik va muhabbat nurlanib turgan chehrali edi; yoshrog'i esa qomati ingichka va nafis, yuz chiziqlari eng nozik mutanosiblik bilan qoliplangan edi, lekin ko'zlari va holati eng chuqur g'amginlik va tushkunlikni ifodalardi. Chol kulbaga qaytdi, yigit esa ertalab ishlatganlaridan boshqacha asboblar bilan qadamlarini dalalar bo'ylab yo'naltirdi.

paras.en: “Night quickly shut in, but to my extreme wonder, I found that the cottagers had a means of prolonging light by the use of tapers, and was delighted to find that the setting of the sun did not put an end to the pleasure I experienced in watching my human neighbours. In the evening the young girl and her companion were employed in various occupations which I did not understand; and the old man again took up the instrument which produced the divine sounds that had enchanted me in the morning. So soon as he had finished, the youth began, not to play, but to utter sounds that were monotonous, and neither resembling the harmony of the old man’s instrument nor the songs of the birds; I since found that he read aloud, but at that time I knew nothing of the science of words or letters.
paras.uz: Tun tez cho'kdi, lekin nihoyatda hayratlanib, qishloqliklar shamlar yordamida nurni cho'zish vositasiga ega ekanini bildim va quyosh botishi inson qo'shnilarimni kuzatishdan olgan zavqimga chek qo'ymaganidan xursand bo'ldim. Kechqurun yosh qiz va uning hamrohi men tushunmagan turli mashg'ulotlar bilan band bo'lishdi; chol esa ertalab meni maftun etgan ilohiy tovushlarni chiqaradigan asbobni yana qo'liga oldi. U tugatishi bilanoq yigit chalishni emas, balki cholning asbobi uyg'unligiga ham, qushlarning qo'shiqlariga ham o'xshamaydigan bir xil tovushlarni chiqara boshladi; keyinchalik bildimki, u ovoz chiqarib o'qigan ekan, lekin o'shanda men so'zlar yoki harflar ilmi haqida hech narsa bilmasdim.

paras.en: “The family, after having been thus occupied for a short time, extinguished their lights and retired, as I conjectured, to rest.”
paras.uz: Oila bir oz vaqt shu tarzda band bo'lgach, chiroqlarini o'chirib, men taxmin qilganimdek, dam olishga ketishdi.»

paras.en: “I lay on my straw, but I could not sleep. I thought of the occurrences of the day. What chiefly struck me was the gentle manners of these people, and I longed to join them, but dared not. I remembered too well the treatment I had suffered the night before from the barbarous villagers, and resolved, whatever course of conduct I might hereafter think it right to pursue, that for the present I would remain quietly in my hovel, watching and endeavouring to discover the motives which influenced their actions.
paras.uz: «Men somonimda yotdim, lekin uxlay olmadim. Kunning voqealari haqida o'yladim. Meni asosan bu odamlarning muloyim muomalasi hayratga soldi va men ularga qo'shilishni orzu qildim, lekin jur'at etmadim. O'tgan kechasi vahshiy qishloqliklardan ko'rgan muomalamni juda yaxshi eslardim va keyinchalik qanday xatti-harakat yo'lini to'g'ri deb bilmay, hozircha xarobamda jimgina qolib, ularning harakatlarini boshqaradigan sabablarni kuzatib, aniqlashga harakat qilishga qaror qildim.

paras.en: “The cottagers arose the next morning before the sun. The young woman arranged the cottage and prepared the food, and the youth departed after the first meal.
paras.uz: Qishloqliklar ertasi kuni ertalab quyoshdan oldin turishdi. Yosh ayol kulbani tartibga solib, ovqat tayyorladi, yigit esa birinchi taomdan keyin jo'nab ketdi.

paras.en: “This day was passed in the same routine as that which preceded it. The young man was constantly employed out of doors, and the girl in various laborious occupations within. The old man, whom I soon perceived to be blind, employed his leisure hours on his instrument or in contemplation. Nothing could exceed the love and respect which the younger cottagers exhibited towards their venerable companion. They performed towards him every little office of affection and duty with gentleness, and he rewarded them by his benevolent smiles.
paras.uz: Bu kun ham oldingisi kabi bir xil tartibda o'tdi. Yigit doimo tashqarida, qiz esa ichkarida turli mashaqqatli yumushlar bilan band edi. Tez orada ko'r ekanini payqagan chol bo'sh soatlarini asbobi bilan yoki o'yga cho'mib o'tkazardi. Yosh qishloqliklarning muhtaram hamrohlariga ko'rsatgan muhabbat va hurmatidan ortiq narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas edi. Ular unga mehr va burchning har bir kichik xizmatini muloyimlik bilan bajarishar, u esa ularni xayrixoh tabassumlari bilan mukofotlardi.

paras.en: “They were not entirely happy. The young man and his companion often went apart and appeared to weep. I saw no cause for their unhappiness, but I was deeply affected by it. If such lovely creatures were miserable, it was less strange that I, an imperfect and solitary being, should be wretched. Yet why were these gentle beings unhappy? They possessed a delightful house (for such it was in my eyes) and every luxury; they had a fire to warm them when chill and delicious viands when hungry; they were dressed in excellent clothes; and, still more, they enjoyed one another’s company and speech, interchanging each day looks of affection and kindness. What did their tears imply? Did they really express pain? I was at first unable to solve these questions, but perpetual attention and time explained to me many appearances which were at first enigmatic.
paras.uz: Ular butunlay baxtli emas edi. Yigit va uning hamrohi ko'pincha chetga chiqib, yig'layotganga o'xshashardi. Men ularning baxtsizligi uchun hech qanday sabab ko'rmadim, lekin bundan qattiq ta'sirlandim. Agar shunday yoqimtoy jonzotlar baxtsiz bo'lsa, men — nomukammal va yolg'iz mavjudot ayanchli bo'lishim unchalik g'alati emas edi. Shunga qaramay bu muloyim jonzotlar nega baxtsiz edi? Ularda ajoyib uy (mening ko'zimda u shunday edi) va har qanday hashamat bor edi; sovqotganda isitadigan olov va och qolganda mazali taomlar bor edi; ular a'lo kiyim kiygan edi; bundan ham ko'proq, ular bir-birining hamrohligi va suhbatidan bahramand bo'lib, har kuni mehr va mehribonlik nigohlarini almashishardi. Ularning ko'z yoshlari nimani anglatardi? Ular haqiqatan ham og'riqni ifodalarmidi? Dastlab bu savollarni hal qila olmadim, lekin doimiy e'tibor va vaqt menga dastlab jumboq bo'lgan ko'p ko'rinishlarni tushuntirdi.

paras.en: “A considerable period elapsed before I discovered one of the causes of the uneasiness of this amiable family: it was poverty, and they suffered that evil in a very distressing degree. Their nourishment consisted entirely of the vegetables of their garden and the milk of one cow, which gave very little during the winter, when its masters could scarcely procure food to support it. They often, I believe, suffered the pangs of hunger very poignantly, especially the two younger cottagers, for several times they placed food before the old man when they reserved none for themselves.
paras.uz: Bu yoqimtoy oilaning bezovtaligi sabablaridan birini kashf etgunimcha ancha vaqt o'tdi: bu qashshoqlik edi va ular bu yovuzlikdan juda og'ir darajada azob chekishardi. Ularning ovqati butunlay bog'larining sabzavotlari va egalari zo'rg'a uni boqish uchun ozuqa topa oladigan qishda juda kam sut beradigan bitta sigirning sutidan iborat edi. Menimcha, ular ko'pincha ochlik azobini juda achchiq his qilishardi, ayniqsa ikki yosh qishloqlik, chunki bir necha marta ular o'zlariga hech narsa qoldirmay, ovqatni cholning oldiga qo'yishgan edi.

paras.en: “This trait of kindness moved me sensibly. I had been accustomed, during the night, to steal a part of their store for my own consumption, but when I found that in doing this I inflicted pain on the cottagers, I abstained and satisfied myself with berries, nuts, and roots which I gathered from a neighbouring wood.
paras.uz: Mehribonlikning bu belgisi meni sezilarli darajada ta'sirlantirdi. Men kechalari o'zim iste'mol qilish uchun ularning zaxirasidan bir qismini o'g'irlashga odatlangan edim, lekin buni qilish bilan qishloqliklarga og'riq yetkazayotganimni bilgach, tiyildim va qo'shni o'rmondan yig'gan mevalar, yong'oqlar va ildizlar bilan qanoatlandim.

paras.en: “I discovered also another means through which I was enabled to assist their labours. I found that the youth spent a great part of each day in collecting wood for the family fire, and during the night I often took his tools, the use of which I quickly discovered, and brought home firing sufficient for the consumption of several days.
paras.uz: Men ularning mehnatiga yordam berishimga imkon beradigan yana bir vositani ham kashf etdim. Yigit har kunning katta qismini oila o'chog'i uchun o'tin yig'ishga sarflashini payqadim va kechalari ko'pincha uning asboblarini olardim — ulardan foydalanishni tezda o'rgandim — va bir necha kunlik iste'molga yetadigan o'tin olib kelardim.

paras.en: “I remember, the first time that I did this, the young woman, when she opened the door in the morning, appeared greatly astonished on seeing a great pile of wood on the outside. She uttered some words in a loud voice, and the youth joined her, who also expressed surprise. I observed, with pleasure, that he did not go to the forest that day, but spent it in repairing the cottage and cultivating the garden.
paras.uz: Eslayman, buni birinchi marta qilganimda, yosh ayol ertalab eshikni ochganda tashqarida katta o'tin uyumini ko'rib, juda hayratga tushgandek bo'ldi. U baland ovozda bir necha so'z aytdi va unga yigit qo'shildi, u ham hayratini bildirdi. Men zavq bilan payqadimki, u o'sha kuni o'rmonga bormadi, balki kunni kulbani ta'mirlash va bog'ni ishlov berish bilan o'tkazdi.

paras.en: “By degrees I made a discovery of still greater moment. I found that these people possessed a method of communicating their experience and feelings to one another by articulate sounds. I perceived that the words they spoke sometimes produced pleasure or pain, smiles or sadness, in the minds and countenances of the hearers. This was indeed a godlike science, and I ardently desired to become acquainted with it. But I was baffled in every attempt I made for this purpose. Their pronunciation was quick, and the words they uttered, not having any apparent connection with visible objects, I was unable to discover any clue by which I could unravel the mystery of their reference. By great application, however, and after having remained during the space of several revolutions of the moon in my hovel, I discovered the names that were given to some of the most familiar objects of discourse;
paras.uz: Asta-sekin men bundan ham muhimroq kashfiyot qildim. Bu odamlar o'z tajribalari va his-tuyg'ularini bir-biriga aniq tovushlar orqali yetkazish usuliga ega ekanini bildim. Ular gapirgan so'zlar ba'zan tinglovchilarning aqli va chehrasida zavq yoki og'riq, tabassum yoki g'amginlik uyg'otishini payqadim. Bu haqiqatan ham ilohiy ilm edi va men u bilan tanishishni qizg'in istardim. Lekin bu maqsadda qilgan har bir urinishimda muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchradim. Ularning talaffuzi tez edi va ular aytgan so'zlar ko'rinadigan narsalar bilan hech qanday aniq bog'liqlikka ega bo'lmagani uchun, ularning nimaga ishora qilishi sirini ochishga imkon beradigan hech qanday kalit topa olmadim. Biroq katta tirishqoqlik bilan va xarobamda bir necha oy aylanishi davomida qolgandan keyin men suhbatning eng tanish ob'ektlaridan ba'zilariga berilgan nomlarni kashf etdim;

paras.en: I learned and applied the words, fire, milk, bread, and wood. I learned also the names of the cottagers themselves. The youth and his companion had each of them several names, but the old man had only one, which was father. The girl was called sister or Agatha, and the youth Felix, brother, or son. I cannot describe the delight I felt when I learned the ideas appropriated to each of these sounds and was able to pronounce them. I distinguished several other words without being able as yet to understand or apply them, such as good, dearest, unhappy.
paras.uz: men olov, sut, non va o'tin so'zlarini o'rgandim va qo'lladim. Qishloqliklarning o'z ismlarini ham o'rgandim.
