Yigit va uning hamrohining har birining bir nechta ismi bor edi, lekin cholning faqat bittasi bor edi — ota. Qizni singlim yoki Agata, yigitni esa Feliks, aka yoki o'g'lim deb atashardi. Bu tovushlarning har biriga tegishli g'oyalarni o'rganib, ularni talaffuz qila olganimda his qilgan quvonchimni ta'riflay olmayman. Men hali tushunmasdan yoki qo'llay olmasdan yana bir nechta so'zni farqladim, masalan, yaxshi, eng aziz, baxtsiz.

paras.en: “I spent the winter in this manner. The gentle manners and beauty of the cottagers greatly endeared them to me; when they were unhappy, I felt depressed; when they rejoiced, I sympathised in their joys. I saw few human beings besides them, and if any other happened to enter the cottage, their harsh manners and rude gait only enhanced to me the superior accomplishments of my friends. The old man, I could perceive, often endeavoured to encourage his children, as sometimes I found that he called them, to cast off their melancholy. He would talk in a cheerful accent, with an expression of goodness that bestowed pleasure even upon me. Agatha listened with respect, her eyes sometimes filled with tears, which she endeavoured to wipe away unperceived; but I generally found that her countenance and tone were more cheerful after having listened to the exhortations of her father.
paras.uz: Qishni shu tarzda o'tkazdim. Qishloqliklarning muloyim muomalasi va go'zalligi ularni menga juda aziz qildi; ular baxtsiz bo'lganda men tushkunlikka tushardim; ular quvonganda, ularning quvonchiga sherik bo'lardim. Ulardan tashqari kam insonni ko'rardim va agar kulbaga boshqa birov kirib qolsa, ularning qo'pol muomalasi va dag'al yurishi menga faqat do'stlarimning ustun fazilatlarini yanada ta'kidlardi. Payqardimki, chol ko'pincha farzandlarini — ba'zan ularni shunday atashini eshitardim — g'amginlikni tashlashga undashga urinardi. U quvnoq ohangda, hatto menga ham zavq bag'ishlaydigan ezgulik ifodasi bilan gapirardi. Agata hurmat bilan tinglar, ko'zlari ba'zan yoshga to'lar, u ularni sezdirmasdan artishga harakat qilardi; lekin odatda otasining nasihatlarini tinglagandan keyin uning chehrasi va ohangi quvnoqroq bo'lishini payqardim.

paras.en: It was not thus with Felix. He was always the saddest of the group, and even to my unpractised senses, he appeared to have suffered more deeply than his friends. But if his countenance was more sorrowful, his voice was more cheerful than that of his sister, especially when he addressed the old man.
paras.uz: Feliks bilan bunday emas edi. U doimo guruhning eng g'amginsi edi va hatto mening tajribasiz sezgilarimga ham u do'stlaridan ko'ra chuqurroq azob chekkandek ko'rinardi. Lekin agar uning chehrasi qayg'uliroq bo'lsa, ovozi singlisinikidan quvnoqroq edi, ayniqsa chol bilan gaplashganda.

paras.en: “I could mention innumerable instances which, although slight, marked the dispositions of these amiable cottagers. In the midst of poverty and want, Felix carried with pleasure to his sister the first little white flower that peeped out from beneath the snowy ground. Early in the morning, before she had risen, he cleared away the snow that obstructed her path to the milk-house, drew water from the well, and brought the wood from the outhouse, where, to his perpetual astonishment, he found his store always replenished by an invisible hand. In the day, I believe, he worked sometimes for a neighbouring farmer, because he often went forth and did not return until dinner, yet brought no wood with him. At other times he worked in the garden, but as there was little to do in the frosty season, he read to the old man and Agatha.
paras.uz: Bu yoqimtoy qishloqliklarning fe'l-atvorini ko'rsatadigan, arzimas bo'lsa ham, son-sanoqsiz misollarni keltira olaman. Qashshoqlik va muhtojlik o'rtasida Feliks qorli yer ostidan mo'ralab chiqqan birinchi kichkina oq gulni singlisiga zavq bilan olib borardi. Erta tongda, u turmasidan oldin, uning sut xonasiga boradigan yo'lini to'sib qo'ygan qorni tozalar, quduqdan suv tortar va omborxonadan o'tin olib kelardi, u yerda doimiy hayratiga ko'ra, zaxirasi doimo ko'rinmas qo'l bilan to'ldirilganini topardi. Kunduzi, menimcha, u ba'zan qo'shni fermerga ishlardi, chunki u tez-tez chiqib ketar va tushlikkacha qaytmas, lekin o'zi bilan o'tin olib kelmasdi. Boshqa paytlarda bog'da ishlardi, lekin ayozli faslda qiladigan ish kam bo'lgani uchun cholga va Agataga kitob o'qib berardi.

paras.en: “This reading had puzzled me extremely at first, but by degrees I discovered that he uttered many of the same sounds when he read as when he talked. I conjectured, therefore, that he found on the paper signs for speech which he understood, and I ardently longed to comprehend these also; but how was that possible when I did not even understand the sounds for which they stood as signs? I improved, however, sensibly in this science, but not sufficiently to follow up any kind of conversation, although I applied my whole mind to the endeavour, for I easily perceived that, although I eagerly longed to discover myself to the cottagers, I ought not to make the attempt until I had first become master of their language, which knowledge might enable me to make them overlook the deformity of my figure, for with this also the contrast perpetually presented to my eyes had made me acquainted.
paras.uz: Bu o'qish dastlab meni juda dovdiratdi, lekin asta-sekin u o'qiganda ham gapirgandagi ko'p tovushlarni aytishini kashf etdim. Shuning uchun u qog'ozda o'zi tushunadigan nutq belgilarini topadi, deb taxmin qildim va bularni ham tushunishni qizg'in orzu qildim; lekin ular belgisi bo'lgan tovushlarni ham tushunmasam, bu qanday mumkin edi? Biroq men bu ilmda sezilarli darajada rivojlandim, lekin har qanday suhbatni kuzatib borish uchun yetarli emas edi, garchi butun aqlimni bu harakatga qaratgan bo'lsam ham, chunki osongina tushundimki, men qishloqliklarga o'zimni ko'rsatishni qanchalik ishtiyoq bilan orzu qilmay, avval ularning tilini egallamagunimcha urinmasligim kerak, bu bilim ularni qiyofamning xunukligini e'tiborsiz qoldirishga undashi mumkin, chunki ko'zlarim oldida doimo namoyon bo'lgan qarama-qarshilik meni bu bilan ham tanishtirgan edi.

paras.en: “I had admired the perfect forms of my cottagers—their grace, beauty, and delicate complexions; but how was I terrified when I viewed myself in a transparent pool! At first I started back, unable to believe that it was indeed I who was reflected in the mirror; and when I became fully convinced that I was in reality the monster that I am, I was filled with the bitterest sensations of despondence and mortification. Alas! I did not yet entirely know the fatal effects of this miserable deformity.
paras.uz: Men qishloqliklarimning mukammal qomatlariga — ularning nafisligi, go'zalligi va nozik teri rangiga qoyil qolgan edim; lekin o'zimni shaffof hovuzda ko'rganimda qanchalik dahshatga tushdim! Avvaliga orqaga sakrab ketdim, ko'zguda aks etgan haqiqatan ham men ekanimga ishona olmay; va o'zim haqiqatan ham shu yirtqich ekanimga to'liq ishonch hosil qilgach, tushkunlik va xo'rlanishning eng achchiq tuyg'ulariga to'ldim. Afsus! Men hali bu ayanchli xunuklikning halokatli oqibatlarini to'liq bilmasdim.

paras.en: “As the sun became warmer and the light of day longer, the snow vanished, and I beheld the bare trees and the black earth. From this time Felix was more employed, and the heart-moving indications of impending famine disappeared. Their food, as I afterwards found, was coarse, but it was wholesome; and they procured a sufficiency of it. Several new kinds of plants sprang up in the garden, which they dressed; and these signs of comfort increased daily as the season advanced.
paras.uz: Quyosh iliqroq, kun nuri uzunroq bo'lgani sari qor yo'qoldi va men yalang'och daraxtlar va qora yerni ko'rdim. Shu vaqtdan boshlab Feliks ko'proq band bo'ldi va yaqinlashib kelayotgan ochlikning yurakni ezuvchi belgilari yo'qoldi. Keyinroq bilganimdek, ularning ovqati dag'al, lekin sog'lom edi; va ular undan yetarlicha topishardi. Bog'da bir nechta yangi turdagi o'simliklar o'sib chiqdi, ular ularga ishlov berishdi; va fasl ilgarilagan sari farovonlikning bu belgilari kundan-kunga ortib bordi.

paras.en: “The old man, leaning on his son, walked each day at noon, when it did not rain, as I found it was called when the heavens poured forth its waters. This frequently took place, but a high wind quickly dried the earth, and the season became far more pleasant than it had been.
paras.uz: Chol o'g'liga suyanib, har kuni tushda, yomg'ir yog'mayotganda sayr qilardi — osmon o'z suvlarini to'kkanda shunday deyilishini bildim. Bu tez-tez bo'lib turardi, lekin kuchli shamol yerni tez quritardi va fasl avvalgidan ancha yoqimli bo'lib qoldi.

paras.en: “My mode of life in my hovel was uniform. During the morning I attended the motions of the cottagers, and when they were dispersed in various occupations, I slept; the remainder of the day was spent in observing my friends. When they had retired to rest, if there was any moon or the night was star-light, I went into the woods and collected my own food and fuel for the cottage. When I returned, as often as it was necessary, I cleared their path from the snow and performed those offices that I had seen done by Felix. I afterwards found that these labours, performed by an invisible hand, greatly astonished them; and once or twice I heard them, on these occasions, utter the words good spirit, wonderful; but I did not then understand the signification of these terms.
paras.uz: Xarobamdagi hayot tarzim bir xil edi. Ertalab qishloqliklarning harakatlarini kuzatardim, ular turli mashg'ulotlarga tarqalganda esa uxlardim; kunning qolgan qismi do'stlarimni kuzatish bilan o'tardi. Ular dam olishga ketgach, agar oy bo'lsa yoki tun yulduzli bo'lsa, o'rmonga borib, o'zim uchun ovqat va kulba uchun o'tin yig'ardim. Qaytganimda, zarur bo'lgan har safar ularning yo'lini qordan tozalab, Feliks qilganini ko'rgan xizmatlarni bajarardim. Keyinroq bildimki, ko'rinmas qo'l bajargan bu mehnatlar ularni juda hayratga solgan ekan; bir-ikki marta men ularning bunday hollarda yaxshi ruh, ajoyib degan so'zlarni aytganini eshitdim; lekin o'shanda bu atamalarning ma'nosini tushunmasdim.

paras.en: “My thoughts now became more active, and I longed to discover the motives and feelings of these lovely creatures; I was inquisitive to know why Felix appeared so miserable and Agatha so sad. I thought (foolish wretch!) that it might be in my power to restore happiness to these deserving people. When I slept or was absent, the forms of the venerable blind father, the gentle Agatha, and the excellent Felix flitted before me. I looked upon them as superior beings who would be the arbiters of my future destiny. I formed in my imagination a thousand pictures of presenting myself to them, and their reception of me. I imagined that they would be disgusted, until, by my gentle demeanour and conciliating words, I should first win their favour and afterwards their love.
paras.uz: Endi fikrlarim faolroq bo'ldi va men bu yoqimtoy jonzotlarning sabablari va his-tuyg'ularini bilishni orzu qildim; nega Feliks shunchalik baxtsiz, Agata esa shunchalik g'amgin ko'rinishini bilishga qiziqardim. (Ahmoq bechora!) bu munosib odamlarga baxtni qaytarish mening qo'limdan kelishi mumkin, deb o'yladim. Uxlaganimda yoki yo'q bo'lganimda, muhtaram ko'r ota, muloyim Agata va ajoyib Feliksning qiyofalari ko'z oldimda lip-lip o'tardi. Men ularga kelajakdagi taqdirimning hakamlari bo'ladigan ustun mavjudotlar deb qarardim. Xayolimda ularga o'zimni ko'rsatish va ularning meni qabul qilishi haqida mingta manzara chizdim. Ular jirkanishlarini tasavvur qilardim, toki men muloyim xulqim va yarashtiruvchi so'zlarim bilan avval ularning iltifotini, keyin esa muhabbatini qozonmagunimcha.

paras.en: “These thoughts exhilarated me and led me to apply with fresh ardour to the acquiring the art of language. My organs were indeed harsh, but supple; and although my voice was very unlike the soft music of their tones, yet I pronounced such words as I understood with tolerable ease. It was as the ass and the lap-dog; yet surely the gentle ass whose intentions were affectionate, although his manners were rude, deserved better treatment than blows and execration.
paras.uz: Bu fikrlar meni ruhlantirdi va til san'atini egallashga yangi ishtiyoq bilan kirishishga undadi. A'zolarim haqiqatan ham dag'al, lekin egiluvchan edi; va ovozim ularning ohanglarining mayin musiqasiga sira o'xshamasa ham, tushungan so'zlarimni ancha oson talaffuz qilardim. Bu eshak va erka itcha kabi edi; lekin, albatta, muomalasi qo'pol bo'lsa ham, niyatlari mehribon bo'lgan muloyim eshak kaltak va la'natdan ko'ra yaxshiroq muomalaga loyiq edi.

paras.en: “The pleasant showers and genial warmth of spring greatly altered the aspect of the earth. Men who before this change seemed to have been hid in caves dispersed themselves and were employed in various arts of cultivation. The birds sang in more cheerful notes, and the leaves began to bud forth on the trees. Happy, happy earth! Fit habitation for gods, which, so short a time before, was bleak, damp, and unwholesome. My spirits were elevated by the enchanting appearance of nature; the past was blotted from my memory, the present was tranquil, and the future gilded by bright rays of hope and anticipations of joy.”
paras.uz: Bahorning yoqimli jalalari va iliq harorati yerning qiyofasini juda o'zgartirdi. Bu o'zgarishdan oldin go'yo g'orlarda yashiringan odamlar tarqalib, turli dehqonchilik ishlari bilan band bo'lishdi. Qushlar quvnoqroq ohanglarda sayradi va daraxtlarda barglar kurtak yoza boshladi. Baxtli, baxtli yer! Yaqindagina ma'yus, nam va nosog'lom bo'lgan, xudolar uchun munosib maskan. Tabiatning maftunkor qiyofasi ruhimni ko'tardi; o'tmish xotiramdan o'chdi, hozirgi kun osoyishta edi, kelajak esa umidning yorqin nurlari va quvonchni kutish bilan zarhallangan edi.»

paras.en: “I now hasten to the more moving part of my story. I shall relate events that impressed me with feelings which, from what I had been, have made me what I am.
paras.uz: «Endi hikoyamning ko'proq ta'sirli qismiga shoshilaman. Men ilgari qanday bo'lgan bo'lsam, o'shandan meni hozirgi holimga keltirgan his-tuyg'ularni menga singdirgan voqealarni hikoya qilaman.

paras.en: “Spring advanced rapidly; the weather became fine and the skies cloudless. It surprised me that what before was desert and gloomy should now bloom with the most beautiful flowers and verdure. My senses were gratified and refreshed by a thousand scents of delight and a thousand sights of beauty.
paras.uz: Bahor tez ilgariladi; havo yaxshi, osmon bulutsiz bo'ldi. Ilgari cho'l va g'amgin bo'lgan narsa endi eng go'zal gullar va yashillik bilan gullagani meni hayratga soldi. Sezgilarim mingta zavqli hid va mingta go'zal manzara bilan qondirildi va tetiklashdi.

paras.en: “It was on one of these days, when my cottagers periodically rested from labour—the old man played on his guitar, and the children listened to him—that I observed the countenance of Felix was melancholy beyond expression; he sighed frequently, and once his father paused in his music, and I conjectured by his manner that he inquired the cause of his son’s sorrow. Felix replied in a cheerful accent, and the old man was recommencing his music when someone tapped at the door.
paras.uz: Qishloqliklarim vaqti-vaqti bilan mehnatdan dam oladigan shunday kunlarning birida — chol gitarasida chalardi, bolalar esa uni tinglashardi — men Feliksning chehrasi ta'riflab bo'lmas darajada g'amgin ekanini payqadim; u tez-tez xo'rsinardi va bir marta otasi musiqasini to'xtatdi va men uning qiyofasidan o'g'lining qayg'usi sababini so'rayapti deb taxmin qildim. Feliks quvnoq ohangda javob berdi va chol musiqasini qayta boshlayotganda kimdir eshikni taqillatdi.

paras.en: “It was a lady on horseback, accompanied by a country-man as a guide. The lady was dressed in a dark suit and covered with a thick black veil. Agatha asked a question, to which the stranger only replied by pronouncing, in a sweet accent, the name of Felix. Her voice was musical but unlike that of either of my friends. On hearing this word, Felix came up hastily to the lady, who, when she saw him, threw up her veil, and I beheld a countenance of angelic beauty and expression. Her hair of a shining raven black, and curiously braided; her eyes were dark, but gentle, although animated; her features of a regular proportion, and her complexion wondrously fair, each cheek tinged with a lovely pink.
paras.uz: Bu otliq bir xonim edi, unga yo'lboshchi sifatida bir qishloqlik hamroh edi. Xonim qorong'i kostyum kiygan va qalin qora parda bilan yopingan edi. Agata savol berdi, notanish ayol unga faqat shirin talaffuzda Feliksning ismini aytib javob berdi. Uning ovozi musiqiy edi, lekin do'stlarimning hech birinikiga o'xshamasdi. Bu so'zni eshitib, Feliks shoshilib xonimga yaqinlashdi, u esa uni ko'rib, pardasini ko'tardi va men farishtalarga xos go'zallik va ifodali chehrani ko'rdim. Uning sochlari yaltiroq qarg'adek qora va g'alati o'rilgan edi; ko'zlari qorong'i, lekin jonli bo'lsa ham muloyim edi; yuz chiziqlari mutanosib, terisi ajoyib darajada oq, har bir yonog'i yoqimli pushti tusda edi.

paras.en: “Felix seemed ravished with delight when he saw her, every trait of sorrow vanished from his face, and it instantly expressed a degree of ecstatic joy, of which I could hardly have believed it capable; his eyes sparkled, as his cheek flushed with pleasure; and at that moment I thought him as beautiful as the stranger. She appeared affected by different feelings; wiping a few tears from her lovely eyes, she held out her hand to Felix, who kissed it rapturously and called her, as well as I could distinguish, his sweet Arabian. She did not appear to understand him, but smiled. He assisted her to dismount, and dismissing her guide, conducted her into the cottage. Some conversation took place between him and his father, and the young stranger knelt at the old man’s feet and would have kissed his hand, but he raised her and embraced her affectionately.
paras.uz: Feliks uni ko'rib, zavqdan maftun bo'lganga o'xshardi, yuzidan qayg'uning har bir izi yo'qoldi va u darhol men u qodir ekaniga zo'rg'a ishonadigan vajdli quvonch darajasini ifodaladi; ko'zlari chaqnadi, yonog'i zavqdan qizardi; va o'sha lahzada men uni notanish ayol kabi go'zal deb o'yladim. Ayolni boshqacha his-tuyg'ular qamrab olganga o'xshardi; yoqimtoy ko'zlaridan bir necha tomchi yoshni artib, u qo'lini Feliksga uzatdi, u esa uni vajd bilan o'pdi va, men farqlay olganimcha, uni o'zining shirin arab qizi deb atadi. Ayol uni tushunmaganga o'xshardi, lekin jilmaydi. Feliks unga otdan tushishga yordam berdi va yo'lboshchisini jo'natib, uni kulbaga olib kirdi. U va otasi o'rtasida biroz suhbat bo'ldi va yosh notanish ayol cholning oyoqlari ostida tiz cho'kib, uning qo'lini o'pmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin chol uni turg'izib, mehr bilan quchoqladi.

paras.en: “I soon perceived that although the stranger uttered articulate sounds and appeared to have a language of her own, she was neither understood by nor herself understood the cottagers. They made many signs which I did not comprehend, but I saw that her presence diffused gladness through the cottage, dispelling their sorrow as the sun dissipates the morning mists. Felix seemed peculiarly happy and with smiles of delight welcomed his Arabian. Agatha, the ever-gentle Agatha, kissed the hands of the lovely stranger, and pointing to her brother, made signs which appeared to me to mean that he had been sorrowful until she came. Some hours passed thus, while they, by their countenances, expressed joy, the cause of which I did not comprehend. Presently I found, by the frequent recurrence of some sound which the stranger repeated after them, that she was endeavouring to learn their language; and the idea instantly occurred to me that I should make use of the same instructions to the same end. The stranger learned about twenty words at the first lesson; most of them, indeed, were those which I had before understood, but I profited by the others.
paras.uz: Tez orada payqadimki, notanish ayol aniq tovushlar talaffuz qilsa va o'zining tiliga ega bo'lganga o'xshasa ham, uni qishloqliklar tushunmasdi, u ham ularni tushunmasdi. Ular men tushunmagan ko'p imo-ishoralar qilishdi, lekin men uning borligi kulbaga quvonch yoyib, quyosh tong tumanlarini tarqatgandek ularning qayg'usini tarqatganini ko'rdim. Feliks ayniqsa baxtli ko'rinardi va zavqli tabassumlar bilan arab qizini kutib oldi. Agata, doimo muloyim Agata yoqimtoy notanish ayolning qo'llarini o'pdi va akasini ko'rsatib, menimcha, u kelgunicha akasi g'amgin bo'lganini anglatadigan imo-ishoralar qildi. Bir necha soat shu tarzda o'tdi, ular chehralari bilan men sababini tushunmagan quvonchni ifoda etishdi. Ko'p o'tmay men notanish ayol ularning ortidan takrorlagan qandaydir tovushning tez-tez qaytarilishidan u ularning tilini o'rganishga harakat qilayotganini bildim; va xayolimga darhol shu maqsad uchun xuddi shu saboqlardan foydalanishim kerak, degan fikr keldi. Notanish ayol birinchi darsda yigirmatacha so'z o'rgandi; ularning ko'pchiligi, to'g'ri, men ilgari tushungan so'zlar edi, lekin boshqalaridan foyda oldim.

paras.en: “As night came on, Agatha and the Arabian retired early. When they separated Felix kissed the hand of the stranger and said, ‘Good night sweet Safie.’ He sat up much longer, conversing with his father, and by the frequent repetition of her name I conjectured that their lovely guest was the subject of their conversation. I ardently desired to understand them, and bent every faculty towards that purpose, but found it utterly impossible.
paras.uz: Tun kelgach, Agata va arab qizi erta yotishga ketishdi. Ular ajralishganda Feliks notanish ayolning qo'lini o'pib: «Xayrli tun, shirin Safiya», dedi. U otasi bilan suhbatlashib, ancha uzoq o'tirdi va uning ismi tez-tez takrorlanishidan ularning yoqimtoy mehmoni suhbat mavzusi ekanini taxmin qildim. Men ularni tushunishni qizg'in istardim va har bir qobiliyatimni shu maqsadga qaratdim, lekin bu mutlaqo imkonsiz ekanini bildim.

paras.en: “The next morning Felix went out to his work, and after the usual occupations of Agatha were finished, the Arabian sat at the feet of the old man, and taking his guitar, played some airs so entrancingly beautiful that they at once drew tears of sorrow and delight from my eyes. She sang, and her voice flowed in a rich cadence, swelling or dying away like a nightingale of the woods.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab Feliks ishiga chiqib ketdi va Agataning odatiy yumushlari tugagach, arab qizi cholning oyoqlari ostiga o'tirdi va uning gitarasini olib, shunchalik maftunkor go'zal kuylar chaldiki, ular birdaniga ko'zlarimdan qayg'u va zavq yoshlarini to'kdi. U kuyladi va ovozi boy ohangda, o'rmon bulbulidek ko'tarilib yoki so'nib oqdi.

paras.en: “When she had finished, she gave the guitar to Agatha, who at first declined it. She played a simple air, and her voice accompanied it in sweet accents, but unlike the wondrous strain of the stranger. The old man appeared enraptured and said some words which Agatha endeavoured to explain to Safie, and by which he appeared to wish to express that she bestowed on him the greatest delight by her music.
paras.uz: U tugatgach, gitarani Agataga berdi, u avvaliga rad etdi. U oddiy kuy chaldi va ovozi unga shirin ohanglarda jo'r bo'ldi, lekin notanish ayolning ajoyib qo'shig'iga o'xshamasdi. Chol maftun bo'lganga o'xshardi va bir necha so'z aytdi, Agata ularni Safiyaga tushuntirishga harakat qildi, ular orqali chol u musiqasi bilan unga eng katta zavq bag'ishlaganini ifoda etmoqchi bo'lganga o'xshardi.

paras.en: “The days now passed as peaceably as before, with the sole alteration that joy had taken place of sadness in the countenances of my friends. Safie was always gay and happy; she and I improved rapidly in the knowledge of language, so that in two months I began to comprehend most of the words uttered by my protectors.
paras.uz: Kunlar endi avvalgidek tinch o'tardi, yagona o'zgarish shu ediki, do'stlarimning chehralarida g'amginlik o'rnini quvonch egalladi. Safiya doimo quvnoq va baxtli edi; u va men til bilimida tez rivojlandik, shuning uchun ikki oyda men homiylarim aytgan so'zlarning ko'pini tushuna boshladim.

paras.en: “In the meanwhile also the black ground was covered with herbage, and the green banks interspersed with innumerable flowers, sweet to the scent and the eyes, stars of pale radiance among the moonlight woods; the sun became warmer, the nights clear and balmy; and my nocturnal rambles were an extreme pleasure to me, although they were considerably shortened by the late setting and early rising of the sun, for I never ventured abroad during daylight, fearful of meeting with the same treatment I had formerly endured in the first village which I entered.
paras.uz: Bu orada qora yerni ham o'tlar qopladi, yashil qirg'oqlar son-sanoqsiz gullar bilan bezandi — hidi va ko'rinishi shirin, oydin o'rmonlar orasidagi xira nur yulduzlari; quyosh iliqroq, tunlar tiniq va xushbo'y bo'ldi; tungi sayrlarim men uchun nihoyatda zavqli edi, garchi quyoshning kech botishi va erta chiqishi ularni ancha qisqartirgan bo'lsa ham, chunki men birinchi kirgan qishloqda ilgari chidagan muomalaga duch kelishdan qo'rqib, kunduzi hech qachon tashqariga chiqishga jur'at etmasdim.

paras.en: “My days were spent in close attention, that I might more speedily master the language; and I may boast that I improved more rapidly than the Arabian, who understood very little and conversed in broken accents, whilst I comprehended and could imitate almost every word that was spoken.
paras.uz: Tilni tezroq egallash uchun kunlarim zo'r diqqat bilan o'tardi; maqtanishim mumkinki, men juda kam tushunadigan va uzuq-yuluq gapiradigan arab qizidan tezroq rivojlandim, men esa aytilgan deyarli har bir so'zni tushunar va takrorlay olardim.

paras.en: “While I improved in speech, I also learned the science of letters as it was taught to the stranger, and this opened before me a wide field for wonder and delight.
paras.uz: Nutqimni rivojlantirar ekanman, notanish ayolga o'rgatilganidek harflar ilmini ham o'rgandim va bu oldimda hayrat va zavq uchun keng maydon ochdi.

paras.en: “The book from which Felix instructed Safie was Volney’s Ruins of Empires. I should not have understood the purport of this book had not Felix, in reading it, given very minute explanations. He had chosen this work, he said, because the declamatory style was framed in imitation of the Eastern authors. Through this work I obtained a cursory knowledge of history and a view of the several empires at present existing in the world; it gave me an insight into the manners, governments, and religions of the different nations of the earth. I heard of the slothful Asiatics, of the stupendous genius and mental activity of the Grecians, of the wars and wonderful virtue of the early Romans—of their subsequent degenerating—of the decline of that mighty empire, of chivalry, Christianity, and kings. I heard of the discovery of the American hemisphere and wept with Safie over the hapless fate of its original inhabitants.
paras.uz: Feliks Safiyaga dars bergan kitob Volneyning «Imperiyalar xarobalari» edi. Agar Feliks uni o'qiyotganda juda batafsil izohlar bermaganida, men bu kitobning mazmunini tushunmagan bo'lardim. Uning aytishicha, u bu asarni tanlagan, chunki uning notiqlik uslubi Sharq mualliflariga taqlid qilib yaratilgan edi. Bu asar orqali men tarix haqida yuzaki bilim va hozirgi dunyoda mavjud bo'lgan bir nechta imperiyalar haqida tasavvur oldim; u menga yer yuzidagi turli xalqlarning urf-odatlari, hukumatlari va dinlarini tushunishga imkon berdi. Men dangasa osiyoliklar, yunonlarning ulkan dahosi va aqliy faolligi, ilk rimliklarning urushlari va ajoyib fazilati — ularning keyingi tanazzuli — o'sha qudratli imperiyaning inqirozi, ritsarlik, nasroniylik va qirollar haqida eshitdim. Amerika yarim sharining kashf etilishi haqida eshitdim va Safiya bilan birga uning tub aholisining baxtsiz taqdiri ustida yig'ladim.

paras.en: “These wonderful narrations inspired me with strange feelings. Was man, indeed, at once so powerful, so virtuous and magnificent, yet so vicious and base? He appeared at one time a mere scion of the evil principle and at another as all that can be conceived of noble and godlike. To be a great and virtuous man appeared the highest honour that can befall a sensitive being; to be base and vicious, as many on record have been, appeared the lowest degradation, a condition more abject than that of the blind mole or harmless worm. For a long time I could not conceive how one man could go forth to murder his fellow, or even why there were laws and governments; but when I heard details of vice and bloodshed, my wonder ceased and I turned away with disgust and loathing.
paras.uz: Bu ajoyib hikoyalar menda g'alati his-tuyg'ularni uyg'otdi. Inson haqiqatan ham bir vaqtning o'zida shunchalik qudratli, shunchalik fazilatli va ulug'vor, shu bilan birga shunchalik buzuq va tuban bo'la oladimi? U bir paytda yovuzlik tamoyilining shunchaki avlodidek, boshqa paytda esa olijanob va ilohiy deb tasavvur qilish mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsadek ko'rinardi. Buyuk va fazilatli inson bo'lish his qiluvchi mavjudotga nasib etishi mumkin bo'lgan eng oliy sharafdek tuyulardi; tarixda ko'plar bo'lganidek tuban va buzuq bo'lish eng past xorlanish, ko'r ko'rsichqon yoki zararsiz qurtnikidan ham pastroq holat bo'lib tuyulardi. Uzoq vaqt men bir inson qanday qilib o'z hamjinsini o'ldirishga chiqishini, hatto nega qonunlar va hukumatlar borligini tasavvur qila olmadim; lekin illat va qon to'kish tafsilotlarini eshitganimda, hayratim to'xtadi va jirkanish va nafrat bilan yuz o'girdim.

paras.en: “Every conversation of the cottagers now opened new wonders to me. While I listened to the instructions which Felix bestowed upon the Arabian, the strange system of human society was explained to me. I heard of the division of property, of immense wealth and squalid poverty, of rank, descent, and noble blood.
paras.uz: Endi qishloqliklarning har bir suhbati menga yangi mo''jizalarni ochardi. Feliks arab qiziga bergan saboqlarni tinglar ekanman, menga inson jamiyatining g'alati tizimi tushuntirildi. Men mulkning taqsimlanishi, ulkan boylik va qashshoq kambag'allik, mavqe, nasl-nasab va oliy qon haqida eshitdim.

paras.en: “The words induced me to turn towards myself. I learned that the possessions most esteemed by your fellow creatures were high and unsullied descent united with riches. A man might be respected with only one of these advantages, but without either he was considered, except in very rare instances, as a vagabond and a slave, doomed to waste his powers for the profits of the chosen few! And what was I? Of my creation and creator I was absolutely ignorant, but I knew that I possessed no money, no friends, no kind of property. I was, besides, endued with a figure hideously deformed and loathsome; I was not even of the same nature as man. I was more agile than they and could subsist upon coarser diet; I bore the extremes of heat and cold with less injury to my frame; my stature far exceeded theirs. When I looked around I saw and heard of none like me. Was I, then, a monster, a blot upon the earth, from which all men fled and whom all men disowned?
paras.uz: Bu so'zlar meni o'zimga qarashga undadi. Hamjinslaringiz eng qadrlaydigan mulk boylik bilan qo'shilgan yuksak va dog'siz nasl ekanini bildim. Inson bu afzalliklarning faqat bittasi bilan ham hurmat qilinishi mumkin edi, lekin ikkalasisiz ham u juda kam holatlardan tashqari sarson va qul, kuchlarini tanlangan ozchilikning foydasi uchun sarflashga mahkum deb hisoblanardi! Men esa nima edim? Men yaratilishim va yaratuvchim haqida mutlaqo bexabar edim, lekin pulim, do'stlarim, hech qanday mulkim yo'qligini bilardim. Bundan tashqari, menga dahshatli darajada xunuk va jirkanch qiyofa ato etilgan edi; men hatto inson bilan bir xil tabiatda ham emas edim. Men ulardan chaqqonroq edim va dag'alroq ovqat bilan kun kechira olardim; issiq va sovuqning chekka darajalariga vujudimga kamroq zarar yetkazgan holda bardosh berardim; bo'yim ularnikidan ancha baland edi. Atrofimga qaraganimda menga o'xshagan hech kimni ko'rmadim va eshitmadim. Unda men yirtqich, yer yuzidagi dog' edimmi, undan barcha odamlar qochadi va hamma undan tonadi?

paras.en: “I cannot describe to you the agony that these reflections inflicted upon me; I tried to dispel them, but sorrow only increased with knowledge. Oh, that I had for ever remained in my native wood, nor known nor felt beyond the sensations of hunger, thirst, and heat!
paras.uz: Bu mulohazalar menga yetkazgan iztirobni senga ta'riflab berolmayman; men ularni tarqatishga urindim, lekin bilim bilan qayg'u faqat ortib bordi. Oh, qaniydi ona o'rmonimda abadiy qolib, ochlik, tashnalik va issiqlik sezgilaridan nariga hech narsani bilmagan va his qilmagan bo'lsam!

paras.en: “Of what a strange nature is knowledge! It clings to the mind when it has once seized on it like a lichen on the rock. I wished sometimes to shake off all thought and feeling, but I learned that there was but one means to overcome the sensation of pain, and that was death—a state which I feared yet did not understand. I admired virtue and good feelings and loved the gentle manners and amiable qualities of my cottagers, but I was shut out from intercourse with them, except through means which I obtained by stealth, when I was unseen and unknown, and which rather increased than satisfied the desire I had of becoming one among my fellows. The gentle words of Agatha and the animated smiles of the charming Arabian were not for me. The mild exhortations of the old man and the lively conversation of the loved Felix were not for me. Miserable, unhappy wretch!
paras.uz: Bilim qanday g'alati tabiatga ega! U bir marta aqlni egallagach, qoyadagi lishaynikdek unga yopishib oladi. Ba'zan barcha fikr va his-tuyg'ulardan qutulishni istardim, lekin og'riq tuyg'usini yengishning faqat bitta vositasi borligini bildim — bu o'lim edi, men undan qo'rqardim, lekin uni tushunmasdim. Men fazilat va yaxshi tuyg'ularga qoyil qolardim va qishloqliklarimning muloyim muomalasi va yoqimtoy fazilatlarini sevardim, lekin men ular bilan muloqotdan chetlatilgan edim, faqat ko'rinmas va noma'lum bo'lganimda yashirincha qo'lga kiritgan vositalardan tashqari, ular hamjinslarimdan biri bo'lish istagimni qondirishdan ko'ra ko'proq kuchaytirardi. Agataning muloyim so'zlari va maftunkor arab qizining jonli tabassumlari men uchun emas edi. Cholning yumshoq nasihatlari va suyukli Feliksning jonli suhbati men uchun emas edi. Ayanchli, baxtsiz bechora!

paras.en: “Other lessons were impressed upon me even more deeply. I heard of the difference of sexes, and the birth and growth of children, how the father doted on the smiles of the infant, and the lively sallies of the older child, how all the life and cares of the mother were wrapped up in the precious charge, how the mind of youth expanded and gained knowledge, of brother, sister, and all the various relationships which bind one human being to another in mutual bonds.
paras.uz: Boshqa saboqlar menga yanada chuqurroq singdi. Men jinslarning farqi, bolalarning tug'ilishi va o'sishi haqida, otaning go'dakning tabassumlari va kattaroq bolaning jonli hazillaridan qanday huzur qilishi, onaning butun hayoti va tashvishlari qimmatbaho omonatga qanday bog'langani, yoshlik aqli qanday kengayib, bilim orttirishi, aka, opa-singil va bir insonni boshqasiga o'zaro rishtalar bilan bog'laydigan turli qarindoshliklar haqida eshitdim.

paras.en: “But where were my friends and relations? No father had watched my infant days, no mother had blessed me with smiles and caresses; or if they had, all my past life was now a blot, a blind vacancy in which I distinguished nothing. From my earliest remembrance I had been as I then was in height and proportion. I had never yet seen a being resembling me or who claimed any intercourse with me. What was I? The question again recurred, to be answered only with groans.
paras.uz: Lekin mening do'stlarim va qarindoshlarim qayerda edi? Hech bir ota go'daklik kunlarimni kuzatmagan, hech bir ona meni tabassumlar va erkalashlar bilan duo qilmagan edi; yoki agar qilgan bo'lsalar ham, butun o'tmish hayotim endi dog', men hech narsani farqlay olmaydigan ko'r bo'shliq edi. Eng ilk xotiramdan beri men bo'y va mutanosiblikda o'shandagidek edim. Men hali hech qachon menga o'xshagan yoki men bilan biror muloqotni da'vo qilgan mavjudotni ko'rmagan edim. Men nima edim? Savol yana qaytib kelardi va unga faqat ingroq bilan javob berish mumkin edi.

paras.en: “I will soon explain to what these feelings tended, but allow me now to return to the cottagers, whose story excited in me such various feelings of indignation, delight, and wonder, but which all terminated in additional love and reverence for my protectors (for so I loved, in an innocent, half-painful self-deceit, to call them).”
paras.uz: Bu his-tuyg'ular nimaga olib kelganini tez orada tushuntiraman, lekin hozir menga qishloqliklarga qaytishga ruxsat ber, ularning hikoyasi menda g'azab, zavq va hayratning shunchalik turli his-tuyg'ularini uyg'otdi, lekin ularning hammasi homiylarimga (men ularni beg'ubor, yarim og'riqli o'zini aldash bilan shunday atashni yaxshi ko'rardim) bo'lgan muhabbat va ehtiromimning ortishi bilan yakunlandi.»

paras.en: “Some time elapsed before I learned the history of my friends. It was one which could not fail to impress itself deeply on my mind, unfolding as it did a number of circumstances, each interesting and wonderful to one so utterly inexperienced as I was.
paras.uz: «Do'stlarimning tarixini bilib olgunimcha bir muncha vaqt o'tdi. Bu men kabi butunlay tajribasiz kishi uchun har biri qiziqarli va ajoyib bo'lgan bir qator holatlarni ochib bergani uchun aqlimga chuqur ta'sir qilmasdan qolmaydigan tarix edi.

paras.en: “The name of the old man was De Lacey. He was descended from a good family in France, where he had lived for many years in affluence, respected by his superiors and beloved by his equals. His son was bred in the service of his country, and Agatha had ranked with ladies of the highest distinction. A few months before my arrival they had lived in a large and luxurious city called Paris, surrounded by friends and possessed of every enjoyment which virtue, refinement of intellect, or taste, accompanied by a moderate fortune, could afford.
paras.uz: Cholning ismi De Lasi edi. U Fransiyadagi yaxshi oiladan kelib chiqqan edi, u yerda ko'p yillar farovonlikda, yuqori turuvchilar tomonidan hurmat qilinib, tengdoshlari tomonidan sevilib yashagan. Uning o'g'li vatani xizmatida tarbiyalangan, Agata esa eng nufuzli xonimlar qatorida turgan. Men kelishimdan bir necha oy oldin ular Parij deb ataladigan katta va hashamatli shaharda, do'stlar qurshovida, fazilat, aql nafisligi yoki did o'rtacha boylik bilan birga bera oladigan har qanday zavqqa ega bo'lib yashashgan.

paras.en: “The father of Safie had been the cause of their ruin. He was a Turkish merchant and had inhabited Paris for many years, when, for some reason which I could not learn, he became obnoxious to the government. He was seized and cast into prison the very day that Safie arrived from Constantinople to join him. He was tried and condemned to death. The injustice of his sentence was very flagrant; all Paris was indignant; and it was judged that his religion and wealth rather than the crime alleged against him had been the cause of his condemnation.
paras.uz: Ularning halokatiga Safiyaning otasi sabab bo'lgan. U turk savdogari bo'lib, ko'p yillar Parijda yashagan, keyin men bilib ololmagan qandaydir sabab bilan hukumatning g'azabiga uchragan. Safiya unga qo'shilish uchun Konstantinopoldan kelgan aynan o'sha kuni uni hibsga olib, qamoqqa tashlashgan. Uni sud qilib, o'limga hukm qilishgan. Hukmining adolatsizligi juda ochiq edi; butun Parij g'azablandi; va uning hukm qilinishiga unga qo'yilgan ayb emas, balki dini va boyligi sabab bo'lgan, deb hisoblandi.

paras.en: “Felix had accidentally been present at the trial; his horror and indignation were uncontrollable when he heard the decision of the court. He made, at that moment, a solemn vow to deliver him and then looked around for the means. After many fruitless attempts to gain admittance to the prison, he found a strongly grated window in an unguarded part of the building, which lighted the dungeon of the unfortunate Muhammadan, who, loaded with chains, waited in despair the execution of the barbarous sentence. Felix visited the grate at night and made known to the prisoner his intentions in his favour. The Turk, amazed and delighted, endeavoured to kindle the zeal of his deliverer by promises of reward and wealth. Felix rejected his offers with contempt, yet when he saw the lovely Safie, who was allowed to visit her father and who by her gestures expressed her lively gratitude, the youth could not help owning to his own mind that the captive possessed a treasure which would fully reward his toil and hazard.
paras.uz: Feliks tasodifan sudda hozir bo'lgan; sudning qarorini eshitganda uning dahshati va g'azabi jilovsiz bo'lgan. U o'sha lahzada uni qutqarish haqida tantanali qasam ichgan va keyin vosita izlab atrofga qaragan. Qamoqxonaga kirishga ko'plab samarasiz urinishlardan keyin u binoning qo'riqlanmagan qismida baxtsiz musulmonning zindonini yoritib turgan mustahkam panjarali derazani topgan, u esa zanjirlarga solingan holda vahshiyona hukmning ijro etilishini umidsizlikda kutardi. Feliks kechalari panjaraga kelib, mahbusga uning foydasiga niyatlarini ma'lum qilgan. Hayratlangan va xursand bo'lgan turk mukofot va boylik va'dalari bilan qutqaruvchisining g'ayratini alangalatishga uringan. Feliks uning takliflarini nafrat bilan rad etgan, lekin otasini ko'rishga ruxsat berilgan va imo-ishoralari bilan jonli minnatdorligini ifoda etgan yoqimtoy Safiyani ko'rganda, yigit o'z-o'ziga mahbusda uning mehnati va tavakkalini to'liq mukofotlaydigan xazina borligini tan olmasdan turolmagan.

paras.en: “The Turk quickly perceived the impression that his daughter had made on the heart of Felix and endeavoured to secure him more entirely in his interests by the promise of her hand in marriage so soon as he should be conveyed to a place of safety. Felix was too delicate to accept this offer, yet he looked forward to the probability of the event as to the consummation of his happiness.
paras.uz: Turk qizi Feliksning yuragida qoldirgan taassurotni tez payqagan va xavfsiz joyga yetkazilishi bilanoq qizini unga turmushga berishni va'da qilib, uni o'z manfaatlariga yanada mahkamroq bog'lashga uringan. Feliks bu taklifni qabul qilish uchun haddan tashqari nozik tabiatli edi, lekin bu voqea ehtimolini baxtining cho'qqisi sifatida intiqib kutardi.

paras.en: “During the ensuing days, while the preparations were going forward for the escape of the merchant, the zeal of Felix was warmed by several letters that he received from this lovely girl, who found means to express her thoughts in the language of her lover by the aid of an old man, a servant of her father who understood French. She thanked him in the most ardent terms for his intended services towards her parent, and at the same time she gently deplored her own fate.
paras.uz: Savdogarning qochishiga tayyorgarlik ketayotgan keyingi kunlarda Feliksning g'ayratini bu yoqimtoy qizdan olgan bir nechta maktubi isitgan; qiz otasining fransuz tilini tushunadigan keksa xizmatkori yordamida o'z fikrlarini sevgilisining tilida ifoda etish yo'lini topgan. U ota-onasiga nisbatan rejalashtirilgan xizmatlari uchun uni eng qizg'in so'zlar bilan minnatdorlik bildirgan va shu bilan birga o'z taqdiridan yumshoq nolagan.

paras.en: “I have copies of these letters, for I found means, during my residence in the hovel, to procure the implements of writing; and the letters were often in the hands of Felix or Agatha. Before I depart I will give them to you; they will prove the truth of my tale; but at present, as the sun is already far declined, I shall only have time to repeat the substance of them to you.
paras.uz: Menda bu maktublarning nusxalari bor, chunki xarobada yashagan paytimda yozuv asboblarini topishning yo'lini topdim; maktublar esa tez-tez Feliks yoki Agataning qo'lida bo'lardi. Ketishimdan oldin ularni senga beraman; ular hikoyamning haqiqatini isbotlaydi; lekin hozir quyosh allaqachon ancha engashgani uchun, senga ularning mazmunini takrorlashga vaqtim yetadi, xolos.

paras.en: “Safie related that her mother was a Christian Arab, seized and made a slave by the Turks; recommended by her beauty, she had won the heart of the father of Safie, who married her. The young girl spoke in high and enthusiastic terms of her mother, who, born in freedom, spurned the bondage to which she was now reduced. She instructed her daughter in the tenets of her religion and taught her to aspire to higher powers of intellect and an independence of spirit forbidden to the female followers of Muhammad. This lady died, but her lessons were indelibly impressed on the mind of Safie, who sickened at the prospect of again returning to Asia and being immured within the walls of a harem, allowed only to occupy herself with infantile amusements, ill-suited to the temper of her soul, now accustomed to grand ideas and a noble emulation for virtue. The prospect of marrying a Christian and remaining in a country where women were allowed to take a rank in society was enchanting to her.
paras.uz: Safiya onasi turklar tomonidan qo'lga olinib, qul qilingan nasroniy arab ekanini hikoya qilgan; go'zalligi tufayli u Safiyaning otasining yuragini zabt etgan va u unga uylangan. Yosh qiz ozodlikda tug'ilgan va endi tushib qolgan qullikni rad etgan onasi haqida yuksak va ishtiyoqli so'zlar bilan gapirgan. U qiziga o'z dinining aqidalarini o'rgatgan va unga Muhammad izdoshlarining ayollariga taqiqlangan yuksakroq aql qudrati va ruh mustaqilligiga intilishni o'rgatgan. Bu xonim vafot etgan, lekin uning saboqlari Safiyaning ongiga o'chmas qilib singgan va u yana Osiyoga qaytish va haram devorlari ichida qamalib, faqat endi ulug'vor g'oyalar va fazilatga olijanob raqobatga odatlangan ruhining tabiatiga mos kelmaydigan bolalarcha ermaklar bilan shug'ullanishga ruxsat berilishi istiqbolidan ko'ngli aynigan. Nasroniyga turmushga chiqish va ayollarga jamiyatda o'rin egallashga ruxsat berilgan mamlakatda qolish istiqboli uni maftun etgan.

paras.en: “The day for the execution of the Turk was fixed, but on the night previous to it he quitted his prison and before morning was distant many leagues from Paris. Felix had procured passports in the name of his father, sister, and himself. He had previously communicated his plan to the former, who aided the deceit by quitting his house, under the pretence of a journey and concealed himself, with his daughter, in an obscure part of Paris.
paras.uz: Turkning qatl kuni belgilangan edi, lekin undan oldingi kechasi u qamoqxonasini tark etgan va tongga qadar Parijdan ko'p liga uzoqlashgan. Feliks otasi, singlisi va o'zining nomidan pasportlar olgan edi. U avvaldan rejasini otasiga aytgan edi, u esa safar bahonasi bilan uyini tark etib, aldovga yordam bergan va qizi bilan Parijning xilvat bir qismida yashiringan.

paras.en: “Felix conducted the fugitives through France to Lyons and across Mont Cenis to Leghorn, where the merchant had decided to wait a favourable opportunity of passing into some part of the Turkish dominions.
paras.uz: Feliks qochoqlarni Fransiya bo'ylab Lionga, Mon-Senis orqali Livornoga olib borgan, u yerda savdogar turk hududlarining biror qismiga o'tish uchun qulay imkoniyatni kutishga qaror qilgan.

paras.en: “Safie resolved to remain with her father until the moment of his departure, before which time the Turk renewed his promise that she should be united to his deliverer; and Felix remained with them in expectation of that event; and in the meantime he enjoyed the society of the Arabian, who exhibited towards him the simplest and tenderest affection. They conversed with one another through the means of an interpreter, and sometimes with the interpretation of looks; and Safie sang to him the divine airs of her native country.
paras.uz: Safiya otasining jo'nash lahzasigacha u bilan qolishga qaror qilgan, bu vaqtgacha turk uni qutqaruvchisiga turmushga berish va'dasini yangilagan; Feliks esa shu voqeani kutib, ular bilan qolgan; bu orada u arab qizining hamrohligidan bahramand bo'lgan, qiz esa unga eng sodda va eng nozik mehr ko'rsatgan. Ular tarjimon orqali, ba'zan esa nigohlar tarjimasi bilan suhbatlashishgan; Safiya esa unga ona yurtining ilohiy kuylarini kuylab bergan.

paras.en: “The Turk allowed this intimacy to take place and encouraged the hopes of the youthful lovers, while in his heart he had formed far other plans. He loathed the idea that his daughter should be united to a Christian, but he feared the resentment of Felix if he should appear lukewarm, for he knew that he was still in the power of his deliverer if he should choose to betray him to the Italian state which they inhabited. He revolved a thousand plans by which he should be enabled to prolong the deceit until it might be no longer necessary, and secretly to take his daughter with him when he departed. His plans were facilitated by the news which arrived from Paris.
paras.uz: Turk bu yaqinlikka yo'l qo'ygan va yosh oshiqlarning umidlarini rag'batlantirgan, holbuki yuragida butunlay boshqa rejalar tuzgan edi. U qizining nasroniyga turmushga chiqishi g'oyasidan nafratlanardi, lekin agar u sovuq ko'rinsa, Feliksning g'azabidan qo'rqardi, chunki agar qutqaruvchisi uni ular yashayotgan Italiya davlatiga sotib qo'yishni xohlasa, u hali ham uning qo'lida ekanini bilardi. U aldovni endi kerak bo'lmagunicha cho'zish va ketayotganda qizini yashirincha o'zi bilan olib ketish imkonini beradigan mingta rejani o'ylab chiqdi. Uning rejalarini Parijdan kelgan xabarlar osonlashtirdi.

paras.en: “The government of France were greatly enraged at the escape of their victim and spared no pains to detect and punish his deliverer. The plot of Felix was quickly discovered, and De Lacey and Agatha were thrown into prison. The news reached Felix and roused him from his dream of pleasure. His blind and aged father and his gentle sister lay in a noisome dungeon while he enjoyed the free air and the society of her whom he loved. This idea was torture to him. He quickly arranged with the Turk that if the latter should find a favourable opportunity for escape before Felix could return to Italy, Safie should remain as a boarder at a convent at Leghorn; and then, quitting the lovely Arabian, he hastened to Paris and delivered himself up to the vengeance of the law, hoping to free De Lacey and Agatha by this proceeding.
paras.uz: Fransiya hukumati qurbonining qochib ketganidan qattiq g'azablangan va qutqaruvchisini topish va jazolash uchun hech qanday harakatni ayamagan. Feliksning fitnasi tez fosh bo'lgan va De Lasi va Agata qamoqqa tashlangan. Xabar Feliksga yetib borgan va uni zavq tushidan uyg'otgan. U erkin havodan va sevgan qizining hamrohligidan bahramand bo'layotganda uning ko'r va keksa otasi va muloyim singlisi badbo'y zindonda yotgan. Bu fikr uning uchun qiynoq edi. U tezda turk bilan kelishib olgan: agar Feliks Italiyaga qaytishidan oldin turk qochish uchun qulay imkoniyat topsa, Safiya Livornodagi monastirda pansioner sifatida qoladi; keyin yoqimtoy arab qizini tark etib, Parijga shoshilgan va shu yo'l bilan De Lasi va Agatani ozod qilishga umid qilib, o'zini qonun qasosiga topshirgan.

paras.en: “He did not succeed. They remained confined for five months before the trial took place, the result of which deprived them of their fortune and condemned them to a perpetual exile from their native country.
paras.uz: U muvaffaqiyat qozonmagan. Sud bo'lgunicha ular besh oy qamoqda qolishgan va uning natijasi ularni boyliklaridan mahrum qilib, ona yurtlaridan abadiy surgunga hukm qilgan.

paras.en: “They found a miserable asylum in the cottage in Germany, where I discovered them. Felix soon learned that the treacherous Turk, for whom he and his family endured such unheard-of oppression, on discovering that his deliverer was thus reduced to poverty and ruin, became a traitor to good feeling and honour and had quitted Italy with his daughter, insultingly sending Felix a pittance of money to aid him, as he said, in some plan of future maintenance.
paras.uz: Ular men topgan Germaniyadagi kulbada ayanchli boshpana topishgan. Tez orada Feliks o'zi va oilasi shunday eshitilmagan zulmga chidagan xoin turk qutqaruvchisi shu tarzda qashshoqlik va halokatga uchraganini bilgach, yaxshi tuyg'u va sharafga xiyonat qilib, qizi bilan Italiyani tark etganini va Feliksga, o'zi aytganidek, kelajakdagi tirikchilik rejasiga yordam berish uchun haqoratli tarzda arzimas pul jo'natganini bilib olgan.

paras.en: “Such were the events that preyed on the heart of Felix and rendered him, when I first saw him, the most miserable of his family. He could have endured poverty, and while this distress had been the meed of his virtue, he gloried in it; but the ingratitude of the Turk and the loss of his beloved Safie were misfortunes more bitter and irreparable. The arrival of the Arabian now infused new life into his soul.
paras.uz: Feliksning yuragini yegan va men uni birinchi ko'rganimda uni oilasining eng baxtsizi qilgan voqealar shular edi. U qashshoqlikka chiday olardi va bu kulfat fazilatining mukofoti bo'lgan ekan, u bundan faxrlanardi; lekin turkning noshukurligi va sevikli Safiyasini yo'qotishi yanada achchiqroq va tuzatib bo'lmas baxtsizliklar edi. Endi arab qizining kelishi uning ruhiga yangi hayot baxsh etdi.

paras.en: “When the news reached Leghorn that Felix was deprived of his wealth and rank, the merchant commanded his daughter to think no more of her lover, but to prepare to return to her native country. The generous nature of Safie was outraged by this command; she attempted to expostulate with her father, but he left her angrily, reiterating his tyrannical mandate.
paras.uz: Livornoga Feliks boyligi va mavqeidan mahrum bo'lgani haqida xabar yetib kelganda, savdogar qiziga sevgilisi haqida boshqa o'ylamaslikni, balki ona yurtiga qaytishga tayyorlanishni buyurgan. Safiyaning saxiy tabiati bu buyruqdan g'azablangan; u otasiga e'tiroz bildirishga uringan, lekin u zolimona buyrug'ini takrorlab, uni jahl bilan tashlab ketgan.

paras.en: “A few days after, the Turk entered his daughter’s apartment and told her hastily that he had reason to believe that his residence at Leghorn had been divulged and that he should speedily be delivered up to the French government; he had consequently hired a vessel to convey him to Constantinople, for which city he should sail in a few hours. He intended to leave his daughter under the care of a confidential servant, to follow at her leisure with the greater part of his property, which had not yet arrived at Leghorn.
paras.uz: Bir necha kundan keyin turk qizining xonasiga kirib, unga shoshilib Livornodagi qarorgohi oshkor bo'lgan deb ishonishga asosi borligini va tez orada Fransiya hukumatiga topshirilishini aytgan; shuning uchun u Konstantinopolga olib boradigan kema yollagan va bir necha soatdan keyin o'sha shaharga suzib ketadi. U qizini ishonchli xizmatkorning qaramog'ida qoldirmoqchi edi, toki u hali Livornoga yetib kelmagan mol-mulkining katta qismi bilan o'z vaqtida ergashsin.

paras.en: “When alone, Safie resolved in her own mind the plan of conduct that it would become her to pursue in this emergency. A residence in Turkey was abhorrent to her; her religion and her feelings were alike averse to it. By some papers of her father which fell into her hands she heard of the exile of her lover and learnt the name of the spot where he then resided. She hesitated some time, but at length she formed her determination. Taking with her some jewels that belonged to her and a sum of money, she quitted Italy with an attendant, a native of Leghorn, but who understood the common language of Turkey, and departed for Germany.
paras.uz: Yolg'iz qolgach, Safiya bu favqulodda holatda o'ziga yarashadigan xatti-harakat rejasini o'zicha belgilab oldi. Turkiyada yashash unga jirkanch edi; dini ham, his-tuyg'ulari ham bunga birday qarshi edi. Qo'liga tushgan otasining ba'zi qog'ozlaridan u sevgilisining surgun qilingani haqida eshitdi va u o'sha paytda yashayotgan joyning nomini bilib oldi. U bir muddat ikkilandi, lekin oxir-oqibat qaror qildi. O'ziga tegishli ba'zi zeb-ziynatlar va bir miqdor pulni olib, Livornolik, lekin Turkiyaning umumiy tilini tushunadigan bir xizmatkor ayol bilan Italiyani tark etib, Germaniyaga jo'nadi.

paras.en: “She arrived in safety at a town about twenty leagues from the cottage of De Lacey, when her attendant fell dangerously ill. Safie nursed her with the most devoted affection, but the poor girl died, and the Arabian was left alone, unacquainted with the language of the country and utterly ignorant of the customs of the world. She fell, however, into good hands. The Italian had mentioned the name of the spot for which they were bound, and after her death the woman of the house in which they had lived took care that Safie should arrive in safety at the cottage of her lover.”
paras.uz: U De Lasining kulbasidan taxminan yigirma liga uzoqlikdagi shaharga xavfsiz yetib keldi, shunda xizmatkor ayoli xavfli kasal bo'lib qoldi. Safiya unga eng sadoqatli mehr bilan qaradi, lekin bechora qiz vafot etdi va arab qizi mamlakat tilini bilmagan va dunyo urf-odatlaridan mutlaqo bexabar holda yolg'iz qoldi. Biroq u yaxshi qo'llarga tushdi. Italiyalik ayol ular yo'l olgan joyning nomini aytgan edi va uning o'limidan keyin ular yashagan uyning bekasi Safiyaning sevgilisining kulbasiga xavfsiz yetib borishiga g'amxo'rlik qildi.»

paras.en: “Such was the history of my beloved cottagers. It impressed me deeply. I learned, from the views of social life which it developed, to admire their virtues and to deprecate the vices of mankind.
paras.uz: «Sevimli qishloqliklarimning tarixi shunday edi. U menga chuqur ta'sir qildi. U ochib bergan ijtimoiy hayot manzaralaridan men ularning fazilatlariga qoyil qolishni va insoniyatning illatlarini qoralashni o'rgandim.

paras.en: “As yet I looked upon crime as a distant evil, benevolence and generosity were ever present before me, inciting within me a desire to become an actor in the busy scene where so many admirable qualities were called forth and displayed. But in giving an account of the progress of my intellect, I must not omit a circumstance which occurred in the beginning of the month of August of the same year.
paras.uz: Hozircha men jinoyatga uzoqdagi yovuzlik deb qarardim, xayrixohlik va saxovat doimo ko'z oldimda bo'lib, menda shuncha ajoyib fazilatlar namoyon bo'ladigan serharakat sahnada ishtirokchi bo'lish istagini uyg'otardi. Lekin aqlimning rivojlanishi haqida hikoya qilar ekanman, o'sha yilning avgust oyi boshida sodir bo'lgan bir holatni tushirib qoldirmasligim kerak.

paras.en: “One night during my accustomed visit to the neighbouring wood where I collected my own food and brought home firing for my protectors, I found on the ground a leathern portmanteau containing several articles of dress and some books. I eagerly seized the prize and returned with it to my hovel. Fortunately the books were written in the language, the elements of which I had acquired at the cottage; they consisted of Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch’s Lives, and the Sorrows of Werter. The possession of these treasures gave me extreme delight; I now continually studied and exercised my mind upon these histories, whilst my friends were employed in their ordinary occupations.
paras.uz: Bir kechasi o'zim uchun ovqat yig'adigan va homiylarim uchun o'tin olib keladigan qo'shni o'rmonga odatiy tashrifim chog'ida yerdan bir nechta kiyim va bir nechta kitob solingan charm jomadon topdim. Bu o'ljani ishtiyoq bilan olib, u bilan xarobamga qaytdim. Baxtimga kitoblar men kulbada asoslarini o'rgangan tilda yozilgan edi; ular «Yo'qotilgan jannat», Plutarxning «Hayotnomalar»idan bir jild va «Verterning iztiroblari»dan iborat edi. Bu xazinalarga ega bo'lish menga nihoyatda katta quvonch bag'ishladi; endi men do'stlarim odatiy mashg'ulotlari bilan band bo'lganda, tinimsiz bu hikoyalarni o'rganib, ular ustida aqlimni mashq qildirardim.

paras.en: “I can hardly describe to you the effect of these books. They produced in me an infinity of new images and feelings, that sometimes raised me to ecstasy, but more frequently sunk me into the lowest dejection. In the Sorrows of Werter, besides the interest of its simple and affecting story, so many opinions are canvassed and so many lights thrown upon what had hitherto been to me obscure subjects that I found in it a never-ending source of speculation and astonishment. The gentle and domestic manners it described, combined with lofty sentiments and feelings, which had for their object something out of self, accorded well with my experience among my protectors and with the wants which were for ever alive in my own bosom. But I thought Werter himself a more divine being than I had ever beheld or imagined; his character contained no pretension, but it sank deep. The disquisitions upon death and suicide were calculated to fill me with wonder. I did not pretend to enter into the merits of the case, yet I inclined towards the opinions of the hero, whose extinction I wept, without precisely understanding it.
paras.uz: Bu kitoblarning ta'sirini senga zo'rg'a ta'riflab bera olaman. Ular menda cheksiz yangi tasavvurlar va his-tuyg'ularni uyg'otdi, ular ba'zan meni vajdga ko'tarar, lekin ko'pincha eng chuqur tushkunlikka botirardi. «Verterning iztiroblari»da oddiy va ta'sirli hikoyasining qiziqishidan tashqari, shuncha ko'p fikrlar muhokama qilinadi va shu paytgacha men uchun qorong'i bo'lgan mavzularga shuncha ko'p nur sochiladiki, men unda tugamas mulohaza va hayrat manbaini topdim. U tasvirlagan muloyim va oilaviy odob-axloq, maqsadi o'zidan tashqaridagi narsa bo'lgan yuksak tuyg'u va his-hayajonlar bilan qo'shilib, homiylarim orasidagi tajribamga va o'z ko'kragimda doimo tirik bo'lgan ehtiyojlarga yaxshi mos kelardi. Lekin men Verterning o'zini men ko'rgan yoki tasavvur qilgan har qanday mavjudotdan ilohiyroq deb o'yladim; uning xarakterida hech qanday da'vo yo'q edi, lekin u chuqur singardi. O'lim va o'z joniga qasd qilish haqidagi mulohazalar meni hayratga to'ldirishga mo'ljallangan edi. Men masalaning mohiyatiga kirishga da'vo qilmadim, lekin men aniq tushunmasdan uning o'limiga yig'lagan qahramonning fikrlariga moyil bo'ldim.

paras.en: “As I read, however, I applied much personally to my own feelings and condition. I found myself similar yet at the same time strangely unlike to the beings concerning whom I read and to whose conversation I was a listener. I sympathised with and partly understood them, but I was unformed in mind; I was dependent on none and related to none. ‘The path of my departure was free,’ and there was none to lament my annihilation. My person was hideous and my stature gigantic. What did this mean? Who was I? What was I? Whence did I come? What was my destination? These questions continually recurred, but I was unable to solve them.
paras.uz: Biroq o'qiyotganimda men ko'p narsani shaxsan o'z his-tuyg'ularim va ahvolimga tatbiq qilardim. Men o'zimni men o'qiyotgan va suhbatini tinglayotgan mavjudotlarga o'xshash, shu bilan birga g'alati tarzda o'xshamas deb topdim. Men ularga hamdard edim va qisman tushunardim, lekin aqlim shakllanmagan edi; men hech kimga qaram emasdim va hech kim bilan qarindosh emasdim. «Ketishim yo'li ochiq edi» va mening yo'q bo'lishimga motam tutadigan hech kim yo'q edi. Qiyofam xunuk, bo'yim ulkan edi. Bu nimani anglatardi? Men kim edim? Men nima edim? Qayerdan kelgan edim? Mening manzilim qayer edi? Bu savollar doimo qaytib kelardi, lekin men ularni hal qila olmasdim.

paras.en: “The volume of Plutarch’s Lives which I possessed contained the histories of the first founders of the ancient republics. This book had a far different effect upon me from the Sorrows of Werter. I learned from Werter’s imaginations despondency and gloom, but Plutarch taught me high thoughts; he elevated me above the wretched sphere of my own reflections, to admire and love the heroes of past ages. Many things I read surpassed my understanding and experience. I had a very confused knowledge of kingdoms, wide extents of country, mighty rivers, and boundless seas. But I was perfectly unacquainted with towns and large assemblages of men. The cottage of my protectors had been the only school in which I had studied human nature, but this book developed new and mightier scenes of action. I read of men concerned in public affairs, governing or massacring their species.
paras.uz: Menda bo'lgan Plutarx «Hayotnomalar»ining jildida qadimgi respublikalarning ilk asoschilarining tarixi bor edi. Bu kitob menga «Verterning iztiroblari»dan butunlay boshqacha ta'sir qildi. Verterning xayollaridan men tushkunlik va g'amginlikni o'rgandim, lekin Plutarx menga yuksak fikrlarni o'rgatdi; u meni o'z mulohazalarimning ayanchli doirasidan ko'tarib, o'tgan asrlar qahramonlariga qoyil qolishga va ularni sevishga undadi. O'qiganlarimning ko'pi tushuncham va tajribamdan oshib ketardi. Men qirolliklar, keng hududlar, qudratli daryolar va chegarasiz dengizlar haqida juda chalkash bilimga ega edim. Lekin shaharlar va odamlarning katta to'planishlari bilan mutlaqo tanish emas edim. Homiylarimning kulbasi men inson tabiatini o'rgangan yagona maktab bo'lgan edi, lekin bu kitob yangi va qudratliroq harakat sahnalarini ochib berdi. Men davlat ishlari bilan shug'ullangan, o'z zotini boshqargan yoki qirg'in qilgan odamlar haqida o'qidim.

paras.en: I felt the greatest ardour for virtue rise within me, and abhorrence for vice, as far as I understood the signification of those terms, relative as they were, as I applied them, to pleasure and pain alone. Induced by these feelings, I was of course led to admire peaceable lawgivers, Numa, Solon, and Lycurgus, in preference to Romulus and Theseus. The patriarchal lives of my protectors caused these impressions to take a firm hold on my mind; perhaps, if my first introduction to humanity had been made by a young soldier, burning for glory and slaughter, I should have been imbued with different sensations.
paras.uz: Ichimda fazilatga eng katta ishtiyoq va illatga nafrat ko'tarilganini his qildim — men bu atamalarning ma'nosini tushunganim darajasida, chunki men ularni faqat zavq va og'riqqa nisbatan qo'llardim. Bu tuyg'ulardan undalib, men tabiiyki Romul va Teseydan ko'ra tinchliksevar qonun chiqaruvchilar — Numa, Solon va Likurgga qoyil qoldim. Homiylarimning patriarxal hayoti bu taassurotlarning aqlimga mustahkam o'rnashishiga sabab bo'ldi; balki agar insoniyat bilan ilk tanishuvim shon-shuhrat va qirg'in uchun yonib turgan yosh askar orqali bo'lganida, menga boshqacha his-tuyg'ular singgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: “But Paradise Lost excited different and far deeper emotions. I read it, as I had read the other volumes which had fallen into my hands, as a true history. It moved every feeling of wonder and awe that the picture of an omnipotent God warring with his creatures was capable of exciting. I often referred the several situations, as their similarity struck me, to my own. Like Adam, I was apparently united by no link to any other being in existence; but his state was far different from mine in every other respect. He had come forth from the hands of God a perfect creature, happy and prosperous, guarded by the especial care of his Creator; he was allowed to converse with and acquire knowledge from beings of a superior nature, but I was wretched, helpless, and alone. Many times I considered Satan as the fitter emblem of my condition, for often, like him, when I viewed the bliss of my protectors, the bitter gall of envy rose within me.
paras.uz: Lekin «Yo'qotilgan jannat» boshqacha va ancha chuqurroq hayajonlarni uyg'otdi. Men uni qo'limga tushgan boshqa jildlar kabi haqiqiy tarix sifatida o'qidim. U o'z mavjudotlari bilan urushayotgan qodir Xudo manzarasi uyg'ota oladigan har bir hayrat va dahshat tuyg'usini qo'zg'atdi. Men ko'pincha turli vaziyatlarni, o'xshashligi meni hayratga solganda, o'zimnikiga taqqoslardim. Odam Ato kabi men ham aftidan boshqa hech bir mavjud mavjudot bilan hech qanday rishta bilan bog'lanmagan edim; lekin uning holati boshqa har jihatdan menikidan butunlay farq qilardi. U Xudoning qo'lidan mukammal mavjudot sifatida chiqqan, baxtli va farovon, Yaratuvchisining alohida g'amxo'rligi bilan himoyalangan edi; unga ustun tabiatli mavjudotlar bilan suhbatlashish va ulardan bilim olish ruxsat etilgan edi, men esa baxtsiz, ojiz va yolg'iz edim. Ko'p marta men Shaytonni ahvolimning munosibroq timsoli deb hisobladim, chunki ko'pincha, u kabi, homiylarimning saodatini ko'rganimda, ichimda hasadning achchiq zahri ko'tarilardi.

paras.en: “Another circumstance strengthened and confirmed these feelings. Soon after my arrival in the hovel I discovered some papers in the pocket of the dress which I had taken from your laboratory. At first I had neglected them, but now that I was able to decipher the characters in which they were written, I began to study them with diligence. It was your journal of the four months that preceded my creation. You minutely described in these papers every step you took in the progress of your work; this history was mingled with accounts of domestic occurrences. You doubtless recollect these papers. Here they are.
paras.uz: Yana bir holat bu tuyg'ularni kuchaytirdi va tasdiqladi. Xarobaga kelganimdan ko'p o'tmay men sening laboratoriyangdan olgan kiyimning cho'ntagidan qandaydir qog'ozlarni topdim. Dastlab men ularni e'tiborsiz qoldirgan edim, lekin endi ular yozilgan harflarni o'qiy olganimdan keyin ularni tirishqoqlik bilan o'rgana boshladim. Bu sening yaratilishimdan oldingi to'rt oylik kundaliging edi. Sen bu qog'ozlarda ishing davomida qo'ygan har bir qadamingni batafsil tasvirlagansan; bu tarix oilaviy voqealar haqidagi hikoyalar bilan aralashgan edi. Shubhasiz, bu qog'ozlarni eslaysan. Mana ular.

paras.en: Everything is related in them which bears reference to my accursed origin; the whole detail of that series of disgusting circumstances which produced it is set in view; the minutest description of my odious and loathsome person is given, in language which painted your own horrors and rendered mine indelible. I sickened as I read. ‘Hateful day when I received life!’ I exclaimed in agony. ‘Accursed creator! Why did you form a monster so hideous that even you turned from me in disgust? God, in pity, made man beautiful and alluring, after his own image; but my form is a filthy type of yours, more horrid even from the very resemblance. Satan had his companions, fellow devils, to admire and encourage him, but I am solitary and abhorred.’
paras.uz: Ularda mening la'nati kelib chiqishimga taalluqli hamma narsa hikoya qilingan; uni vujudga keltirgan o'sha jirkanch holatlar silsilasining butun tafsiloti ko'z oldiga qo'yilgan; mening jirkanch va nafratli qiyofamning eng mayda tasviri sening o'z dahshatlaringni chizgan va menikini o'chmas qilgan tilda berilgan. O'qiyotganimda ko'nglim aynidi. «Hayot olgan nafratli kun!» deb xitob qildim iztirob ichida. «La'nati yaratuvchi! Nega sen hatto o'zing ham mendan jirkanib yuz o'girgan shunchalik xunuk yirtqichni yaratding? Xudo rahm qilib, insonni o'z suratida go'zal va jozibali qilib yaratdi; mening qiyofam esa seningkining iflos nusxasi, hatto o'xshashligining o'zi bilan yanada dahshatliroq. Shaytonning uni qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan va ruhlantiradigan hamrohlari, sherik shaytonlari bor edi, men esa yolg'iz va nafratlanganman.»

paras.en: “These were the reflections of my hours of despondency and solitude; but when I contemplated the virtues of the cottagers, their amiable and benevolent dispositions, I persuaded myself that when they should become acquainted with my admiration of their virtues they would compassionate me and overlook my personal deformity. Could they turn from their door one, however monstrous, who solicited their compassion and friendship? I resolved, at least, not to despair, but in every way to fit myself for an interview with them which would decide my fate. I postponed this attempt for some months longer, for the importance attached to its success inspired me with a dread lest I should fail. Besides, I found that my understanding improved so much with every day’s experience that I was unwilling to commence this undertaking until a few more months should have added to my sagacity.
paras.uz: Bular tushkunlik va yolg'izlik soatlarimdagi mulohazalarim edi; lekin qishloqliklarning fazilatlarini, ularning yoqimtoy va xayrixoh fe'l-atvorini tomosha qilganimda, o'zimni ishontirardimki, ular mening ularning fazilatlariga qoyil qolishimdan xabar topganlarida, menga rahm qilishadi va shaxsiy xunukligimni e'tiborsiz qoldirishadi. Ular rahm-shafqat va do'stlik so'ragan kishini, qanchalik yirtqich bo'lmasin, eshiklaridan haydab yuborisharmidi? Men hech bo'lmasa umidsizlikka tushmaslikka, balki har tomonlama ular bilan taqdirimni hal qiladigan uchrashuvga o'zimni tayyorlashga qaror qildim. Bu urinishni yana bir necha oyga qoldirdim, chunki uning muvaffaqiyatiga berilgan ahamiyat menda muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrashdan qo'rquv uyg'otardi. Bundan tashqari, aqlim har kunlik tajriba bilan shunchalik rivojlanayotganini ko'rdimki, yana bir necha oy zukkoligimni oshirmaguncha bu ishni boshlashni istamadim.

paras.en: “Several changes, in the meantime, took place in the cottage. The presence of Safie diffused happiness among its inhabitants, and I also found that a greater degree of plenty reigned there. Felix and Agatha spent more time in amusement and conversation, and were assisted in their labours by servants. They did not appear rich, but they were contented and happy; their feelings were serene and peaceful, while mine became every day more tumultuous. Increase of knowledge only discovered to me more clearly what a wretched outcast I was. I cherished hope, it is true, but it vanished when I beheld my person reflected in water or my shadow in the moonshine, even as that frail image and that inconstant shade.
paras.uz: Bu orada kulbada bir nechta o'zgarishlar yuz berdi. Safiyaning borligi uning aholisi orasida baxt yoydi va men u yerda ko'proq farovonlik hukm surayotganini ham payqadim. Feliks va Agata ko'proq vaqtni ko'ngilxushlik va suhbatga sarflashardi va mehnatlarida ularga xizmatkorlar yordam berardi. Ular boy ko'rinmasdi, lekin qanoatli va baxtli edi; ularning his-tuyg'ulari osoyishta va tinch edi, meniki esa kundan-kunga g'alayonliroq bo'lib borardi. Bilimning ortishi menga qanchalik ayanchli quvg'indi ekanimni yanada aniqroq ochib berdi. To'g'ri, men umidni qalbimda saqlardim, lekin u suvda aks etgan qiyofamni yoki oy nurida soyamni ko'rganimda, xuddi o'sha mo'rt tasvir va o'sha o'zgaruvchan soyadek g'oyib bo'lardi.

paras.en: “I endeavoured to crush these fears and to fortify myself for the trial which in a few months I resolved to undergo; and sometimes I allowed my thoughts, unchecked by reason, to ramble in the fields of Paradise, and dared to fancy amiable and lovely creatures sympathising with my feelings and cheering my gloom; their angelic countenances breathed smiles of consolation. But it was all a dream; no Eve soothed my sorrows nor shared my thoughts; I was alone. I remembered Adam’s supplication to his Creator. But where was mine? He had abandoned me, and in the bitterness of my heart I cursed him.
paras.uz: Men bu qo'rquvlarni bosishga va bir necha oydan keyin boshdan kechirishga qaror qilgan sinovga o'zimni mustahkamlashga harakat qildim; ba'zan esa aql jilovlamagan fikrlarimga Jannat dalalarida kezishga yo'l qo'yar va his-tuyg'ularimga hamdard bo'lib, g'amimni tarqatadigan yoqimtoy va go'zal jonzotlarni tasavvur qilishga jur'at etardim; ularning farishtalarga xos chehralari tasalli tabassumlarini taratardi. Lekin hammasi tush edi; hech bir Havvo qayg'ularimni yupatmadi va fikrlarimni baham ko'rmadi; men yolg'iz edim. Men Odam Atoning Yaratuvchisiga iltijosini esladim. Lekin meniki qayerda edi? U meni tashlab ketgan edi va yuragimning achchig'ida men uni la'natladim.

paras.en: “Autumn passed thus. I saw, with surprise and grief, the leaves decay and fall, and nature again assume the barren and bleak appearance it had worn when I first beheld the woods and the lovely moon. Yet I did not heed the bleakness of the weather; I was better fitted by my conformation for the endurance of cold than heat. But my chief delights were the sight of the flowers, the birds, and all the gay apparel of summer; when those deserted me, I turned with more attention towards the cottagers. Their happiness was not decreased by the absence of summer. They loved and sympathised with one another; and their joys, depending on each other, were not interrupted by the casualties that took place around them.
paras.uz: Kuz shu tarzda o'tdi. Men hayrat va qayg'u bilan barglarning so'lib, to'kilishini va tabiat yana men o'rmonlar va yoqimtoy oyni birinchi ko'rganimdagi qup-quruq va ma'yus qiyofaga kirganini ko'rdim. Shunga qaramay men havoning ma'yusligiga e'tibor bermadim; tuzilishimga ko'ra men issiqdan ko'ra sovuqqa chidashga ko'proq moslashgan edim. Lekin asosiy zavqlarim gullar, qushlar va yozning barcha quvnoq libosini ko'rish edi; ular meni tark etgach, men qishloqliklarga ko'proq e'tibor bilan o'girildim. Yozning yo'qligi ularning baxtini kamaytirmadi. Ular bir-birini sevishar va bir-biriga hamdard edi; va bir-biriga bog'liq bo'lgan quvonchlari atrofda yuz bergan tasodiflar bilan uzilmasdi.

paras.en: The more I saw of them, the greater became my desire to claim their protection and kindness; my heart yearned to be known and loved by these amiable creatures; to see their sweet looks directed towards me with affection was the utmost limit of my ambition. I dared not think that they would turn them from me with disdain and horror. The poor that stopped at their door were never driven away. I asked, it is true, for greater treasures than a little food or rest: I required kindness and sympathy; but I did not believe myself utterly unworthy of it.
paras.uz: Ularni qanchalik ko'p ko'rsam, ularning himoyasi va mehribonligini talab qilish istagim shunchalik kuchayardi; yuragim bu yoqimtoy jonzotlar tomonidan tanilish va sevilishni orzu qilardi; ularning shirin nigohlarini menga mehr bilan qaratilganini ko'rish orzuyimning eng chekka chegarasi edi. Ular ularni mendan nafrat va dahshat bilan burib olishlarini o'ylashga jur'at etmasdim. Ularning eshigi oldida to'xtagan kambag'allar hech qachon haydab yuborilmasdi. To'g'ri, men ozgina ovqat yoki dam olishdan ko'ra kattaroq xazinalarni so'rardim: menga mehribonlik va hamdardlik kerak edi; lekin o'zimni bunga mutlaqo noloyiq deb hisoblamasdim.

paras.en: “The winter advanced, and an entire revolution of the seasons had taken place since I awoke into life. My attention at this time was solely directed towards my plan of introducing myself into the cottage of my protectors. I revolved many projects, but that on which I finally fixed was to enter the dwelling when the blind old man should be alone. I had sagacity enough to discover that the unnatural hideousness of my person was the chief object of horror with those who had formerly beheld me.
